**Reads.** The modern Apple Notes store, `NoteStore.sqlite` (or `notes.sqlite`), selected by basename and magic through the crate's shared front end `with_db`: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the last path segment of the artifact's `name` and acts on exactly `notestore.sqlite` or `notes.sqlite`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The first 16 bytes are read with a looping `read_full` and must be `SQLite format 3\0`. The file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 1 GiB cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one, and the copy opened read-only. `probe_table` must list `ZICCLOUDSYNCINGOBJECT` (iOS 9+); the pre-iOS-9 `ZNOTE` layout is not read. Its columns are read with `PRAGMA table_info`, and Core Data's entity table `Z_PRIMARYKEY` is read (`Z_NAME`, `Z_ENT`) to find the `ICNote`, `ICFolder`, `ICAccount`, `ICAttachment` and `ICLegacyTombstone` entity numbers: notes are selected by `Z_ENT = <ICNote>` when both the entity and the `Z_ENT` column exist, and otherwise by `ZTITLE1 IS NOT NULL`, with the summary saying which. Accounts are read as `Z_PK, ZIDENTIFIER` where `Z_ENT` is the account entity; folders as `Z_PK, ZTITLE2, ZFOLDERTYPE, ZIDENTIFIER` where `Z_ENT` is the folder entity; and because Core Data flattens each subclass's `account` relationship into its own column (`ZACCOUNT4` for a note and `ZACCOUNT5` for a folder on the device held, other numbers on other releases), every `ZACCOUNT<n>` column is selected and the first that names an account row is taken. Bodies are read from `ZICNOTEDATA` (`ZNOTE`, `ZDATA`, and whether `ZCRYPTOTAG` is set) into a map by note. Notes are walked by `SELECT Z_PK, ZTITLE1, ZSNIPPET, ZCREATIONDATE, ZMODIFICATIONDATE, ZFOLDER, ZMARKEDFORDELETION, ZIDENTIFIER, ZISPASSWORDPROTECTED, <ZACCOUNT columns> … ORDER BY ZMODIFICATIONDATE DESC LIMIT 200001`, one past the 200,000-note cap (`MAX_NOTES`), any absent optional column being `NULL`. A body is decoded by `notes_proto::note_text`: the `ZDATA` blob must begin with the gzip magic, is inflated under a 16 MiB cap, and the text is field 2 of field 3 of field 2 of the resulting protobuf, taken as UTF-8. Dates are Cocoa REALs converted with their fraction.

**Produces.** One `NotesFolder` (`subtype: "notes_folder"`, `platform: "iOS"`) per folder row: `folder_id`, `title`, `folder_type`, `is_trash` (true when `ZFOLDERTYPE` is 1) with `is_trash_basis` stating that reading rests on the Recently Deleted folders of the device held carrying 1, `identifier`, `account_id` and `account` when resolved, and a `name` of `Notes folder: <title or (untitled)>`. One `Note` (`subtype: "note"`, `platform: "iOS"`) per note row, newest modified first, up to 200,000: `note_id`, `title`, `snippet`, `created` and `date` (both from `ZCREATIONDATE`) and `modified`, each in whole Unix seconds with `_ns` when a fraction was recorded and a `_source` string naming the column and its 2001 epoch, `identifier`, `account_id`/`account`, `folder_id`/`folder`, `marked_for_deletion` when the column exists, `in_recently_deleted` (the folder's type is 1), `deleted` (either of those), — or, when the folder or account lookup failed before reaching the note's folder or account, `folder_unresolved: true` with `in_recently_deleted` null and `deleted` null unless the note is marked for deletion, and `account_unresolved: true` — `password_protected`, and the body state: `body_present: false` (with `body_table_absent: true` when `ZICNOTEDATA` is not there); or `body_present: true` with `body`, `body_decoded: true` and `body_source: "notestore_protobuf"`; or `body_decoded: false` with `content_incomplete: true` — reason `encrypted` and a sentence naming the crypto tag when the note is password-protected or its data row carries one, reason `cap_reached` when the inflate exceeded 16 MiB, otherwise `unresolved_structure` with `body_undecoded_reason` (`not_gzip`, `unexpected_structure`, `not_utf8`) and `body_bytes`; or, when the `ZICNOTEDATA` query did not run, `body_unread: true` with `body_unread_reason`, never `body_present: false`. A `name` of the title, else `Note`. Then a `NoteIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker (`source_table: "ZICCLOUDSYNCINGOBJECT"`, both pairs) when the engine refused to step a note row. Then one `NotesSummary` (`platform`, `notes`, `deleted_notes` stated even when zero, `folders`, `bodies_decoded`, `bodies_undecoded`, `bodies_absent`, `bodies_unread` with `body_query_did_not_run: true` and `body_query_error` when the body query did not run, `entity_resolution: "z_primarykey" | "title_heuristic"`, `note_entity`, `attachment_rows` with `attachments_decoded: false` — or `attachment_entity_unresolved: true` — `tombstone_rows` when the entity exists, `deleted_notes_unresolved` when any note's deletion could not be established, `lookup_failures` naming each entity, account, folder, attachment-count or tombstone-count query that did not complete, with `content_incomplete: true`, reason `unresolved_structure` and a detail sentence, `rows_dropped`, `records_recovered`, and `inventory_incomplete: true` with reason `cap_reached` and `cap: 200000` or `unresolved_structure` when capped or lossy). A store carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged or opened yields one `IosArtifactParseStatus` `DatabaseUnreadable` record with both pairs. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event of its own.

**Cannot.** It cannot read a locked note: a password-protected body is ciphertext behind a key derived from the user's passphrase, and no key handling exists here — the record says `encrypted`. It cannot decode an attachment: `ICAttachment` rows are counted on the summary and never read, because no device this project holds has one, and a reader written from a specification alone would pass its own fixture and nothing else; the same is true of deleted notes' bodies. Its body decoder is a fixed path through the protobuf (field 2 → 3 → 2) validated on the device held, not a schema-driven reader: a note whose text lives elsewhere in the document, or whose `ZDATA` is not gzip, is `body_decoded: false` with the reason, and checklists, tables, styled runs, inline attachment placeholders and embedded links are flattened to whatever bytes that one field holds. It cannot read the pre-iOS-9 `notes.sqlite` layout (`ZNOTE`/`ZNOTEBODY`): a store of that generation carries no `ZICCLOUDSYNCINGOBJECT` and yields one `IosArtifactParseStatus` `ExpectedTableAbsent` record (`expected_tables`, both pairs under `unresolved_structure`) saying no notes were read from it — not that it held none; a catalogue that would not read yields `DatabaseUnreadable` . A note `SELECT` that will not prepare or run yields `DatabaseUnreadable` beside whatever folders were read; there is no column map for `ZTITLE1` or `ZSNIPPET`, so a generation that renamed either is reported unread rather than read for what remains. Its trash reading rests on one device: `ZFOLDERTYPE = 1` is the Recently Deleted folder there, and the record says so, but a release that numbers folder types differently would misfile. A note with no `Z_ENT` resolution is selected by having a title, so an untitled note in such a store is missed, and the summary says `title_heuristic`. It cannot see past the two-hundred-thousandth most recently modified note. It does not read `ZLASTVIEWEDMODIFICATIONDATE`, `ZISPINNED`, `ZISSHARED`, hashtags, mentions or the `ZICCLOUDSTATE` sync state. It recovers no deleted rows.

**Refuses.** It refuses to present an unread body as a note with no body: a body in the evidence that would not decode is `body_present: true`, `body_decoded: false`, with the reason, the byte count and the incompleteness pair, and a store with no `ZICNOTEDATA` says `body_table_absent` rather than leaving bodies silently missing. It refuses to decode ciphertext as text, filing a crypto-tagged or locked note as `encrypted`. It refuses to decode an attachment it has never seen a real instance of, counting it and stating `attachments_decoded: false`. It refuses to name the album-style join or the note entity by a hard-coded number, reading `Z_PRIMARYKEY` and saying on the summary which resolution was used. It refuses to place an unset Cocoa date at 2001-01-01, and refuses to drop the fraction a REAL column records. It refuses to inflate a body without bound, stopping at 16 MiB and saying so. It refuses to present a capped or lossy walk as the whole store, and states `deleted_notes` even when zero because "none were deleted" is a finding. It refuses to present a folder or account it could not look up as none: the rows a failed lookup read before it failed are kept, the notes it never reached are marked unresolved, and the summary names the failure. It refuses to file a store it recognised and could not stage or open as a device with no notes, emitting `DatabaseUnreadable`. And it refuses to present a partially staged store as whole, stamping every record with the spill's incompleteness.

### `plugin.ios.photos`

**Reads.** The iOS Photos library catalogue, `Photos.sqlite`, selected by basename and magic through the crate's shared front end `with_db`: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the last path segment of the artifact's `name` and acts on exactly `photos.sqlite`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The first 16 bytes are read with a looping `read_full` and must be `SQLite format 3\0`. The file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 1 GiB cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one, and the copy opened read-only. The asset table is whichever of `ZGENERICASSET` (iOS 12) or `ZASSET` (newer) `probe_table` lists first; with neither the file yields nothing. Core Data's `Z_PRIMARYKEY` is read for entity names, numbers and `Z_SUPER` parents, and the album↔asset join table is found rather than named: `Z_<albumEnt>ASSETS` with columns `Z_<albumEnt>ALBUMS` and `Z_<assetEnt>ASSETS`, where the entity numbers are those of `Album`/`GenericAlbum` and `Asset`/`GenericAsset` — because those numbers move between releases (`Z_27ASSETS` on iOS 15, `Z_26ASSETS`/`Z_28ASSETS`/`Z_30ASSETS` on others) and a hard-coded name yields silent zero membership everywhere else. Assets are walked by one fixed statement, `SELECT a.ZFILENAME, a.ZDATECREATED, a.ZLATITUDE, a.ZLONGITUDE, a.ZWIDTH, a.ZHEIGHT, a.ZKIND, a.ZFAVORITE, a.ZTRASHEDSTATE, aa.ZORIGINALFILENAME, a.Z_PK FROM <asset> a LEFT JOIN ZADDITIONALASSETATTRIBUTES aa ON aa.ZASSET = a.Z_PK ORDER BY a.ZDATECREATED`, with no row limit. Albums are walked from `ZGENERICALBUM` (`Z_PK`, `ZKIND`, `ZTITLE` fixed; `Z_ENT`, `ZCACHEDCOUNT`, `ZTRASHEDSTATE`, `ZCREATIONDATE`, `ZUUID`, `ZPARENTFOLDER`, `ZCLOUDOWNEREMAILKEY` when present) in `Z_PK` order, and each album's asset count is taken from the join only when its entity is `Album` or descends from it through `Z_SUPER` (bounded to 32 steps). `ZDETECTEDFACE` and `ZPERSON` are counted, not read. Dates are Cocoa REALs converted with their fraction.

**Produces.** One `PhotoAsset` (`subtype: "photo_asset"`, `platform: "iOS"`) per asset row: `asset_id`, `album_ids` when the join placed it in any album, `filename`, `original_filename`, `date` in Unix seconds with `date_ns` and a `date_source` naming `<asset table>.ZDATECREATED` and its 2001 epoch, `latitude`/`longitude`/`has_gps: true` only when both are present, within range and neither is -180 (iOS's "no location"), `width`, `height`, `media_kind` (`photo` for `ZKIND` 0, `video` for 1, `unknown` for anything else or NULL), `favorite` and `deleted` as booleans (JSON `null` when the column is NULL — nothing recorded, nothing asserted), and a `name` of the original filename, else the filename, else `asset`. One `PhotoAlbum` (`subtype: "photo_album"`) per `ZGENERICALBUM` row: `album_id`, `entity_id` and `entity` (the Core Data entity name, else `unknown`), `kind`, `title`, `cached_count`, `trashed`, `created`/`date` with `_ns` and `_source`, `uuid`, `parent_folder_id`, `cloud_owner_email`, and either `asset_count` from the join or `asset_count_unresolved: true` with a reason — no join table was found, or the entity (a `FetchingAlbum` or `Folder` descends from `GenericAlbum`, not `Album`) does not descend from the root whose table is the only join found, or the lookups that find and read the join did not complete (the reason names them) — never 0. `RowsUndecodable` markers under `PhotoAssetIncomplete` (source the asset table) and `PhotoAlbumIncomplete` (`ZGENERICALBUM`) when the engine refused to step a row. Then one `PhotosSummary` (`asset_table`, `assets`, `albums`, `album_table_present`, `album_entity_histogram`, `album_membership_present` with `album_membership_table` and `album_memberships` or `album_membership_unresolved_reason: unresolved_structure`, `face_rows`/`person_rows` or `*_table_absent: true`, `faces_decoded: false`, `records_recovered`). When any lookup those counts are built on did not complete — `Z_PRIMARYKEY`'s entity names or parents, the join table's presence or column list, the membership rows (read to the end or not at all), `ZGENERICALBUM`'s presence, column list, query or a row of it, or the face and person counts — the summary carries `lookup_failures` (one sentence each, with SQLite's error) and `content_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` and a detail naming them; a face or person count that would not read is a failure, not `*_table_absent`. A store carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged or opened yields one `IosArtifactParseStatus` `DatabaseUnreadable` record with both incompleteness pairs. A readable catalogue holding neither `ZGENERICASSET` nor `ZASSET` yields one `IosArtifactParseStatus` with `status: "ExpectedTableAbsent"`, `expected_tables`, both pairs under `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0` and a sentence saying this is not a schema this reader knows — not a finding that the device held none; a catalogue that would not read, and a fixed `SELECT` that would not prepare or run, each yield one `DatabaseUnreadable` record naming SQLite's error. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event of its own; no image bytes.

**Cannot.** It cannot show you a photo: the catalogue is read, the files under `DCIM` are not joined to it, and no thumbnail, hash or EXIF comes from here. It cannot name a face or a person: `ZDETECTEDFACE` and `ZPERSON` are counted and never decoded, because no device this project holds has a row in either and a reader written from a specification alone would pass its own fixture and nothing else. It does not read `ZMOMENT`, `ZMEMORY`, `ZCLOUDMASTER`, `ZINTERNALRESOURCE`, `ZEXTENDEDATTRIBUTES`, `ZMODIFICATIONDATE`, `ZADDEDDATE`, `ZHIDDEN`, `ZSAVEDASSETTYPE`, `ZDURATION`, `ZUNIFORMTYPEIDENTIFIER` or `ZTRASHEDDATE`, so when an asset was added, edited, hidden or trashed, whether it came from the camera, a screenshot, a message or a download, whether the original is on the device or only in iCloud, and how long a video runs are not on the record — only `deleted` as a flag. It cannot read a generation that renamed a column of its fixed asset `SELECT` (or lacks `ZADDITIONALASSETATTRIBUTES`): there is no column map, so that store is reported `DatabaseUnreadable` rather than read for what remains; an album or membership query that will not prepare, run or finish yields no albums or no memberships, stated on the summary's `lookup_failures` rather than as zero. It has no row cap. It recovers no deleted rows.

**Refuses.** It refuses to report zero album membership on a release whose join table has a different entity number: the table is discovered from `Z_PRIMARYKEY`, and where none is found the summary says `album_membership_present: false` with an unresolved reason. It refuses to report an album's asset count as 0 when its entity has no membership table (`FetchingAlbum`, `Folder`), stating `asset_count_unresolved` with the entity and the root it does not descend from. It refuses to plot a "no location" asset: a latitude or longitude of -180, or one out of range, leaves the GPS keys off. It refuses to label an unknown `ZKIND` a photo. It refuses to decode faces and people it has never seen a real instance of, counting them and stating `faces_decoded: false`. It refuses to place an unset Cocoa date at 2001-01-01, and refuses to drop the fraction a REAL column records. It refuses to file a store it recognised and could not stage or open as a device with no photos, emitting `DatabaseUnreadable`, and refuses to spend an absent asset table, an unreadable catalogue or an asset query that would not run as "no photos". It refuses to write `false` for a NULL `ZFAVORITE` or `ZTRASHEDSTATE`. And it refuses to present a partially staged catalogue as whole, stamping every record with the spill's incompleteness.

### `plugin.ios.powerlog`

**Reads.** iOS's PowerLog — `CurrentPowerlog.PLSQL` and its rotated `*.PLSQL` siblings — selected by basename and magic: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the last path segment of the artifact's `name` and acts when it ends `.plsql` or begins `currentpowerlog`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The first 16 bytes are read with a looping `read_full` and must be `SQLite format 3\0`. The file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 1 GiB cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one, and the copy opened read-only. Two things are then read, and only two. First, the flashlight table `PLCameraAgent_EventForward_Torch`, when `probe_table` lists it: its columns are read through `PRAGMA table_info`, sorted, and the timestamp column is the first whose lower-cased name contains `timestamp`, is `time`, or contains `date`; the state column is the first containing `state`, `value`, `level` or equal to `torch`, and if none exists the timestamp alone is read with the state left unknown rather than defaulted to on. The rows are walked `ORDER BY <timestamp>`; each timestamp is a REAL, read as Unix seconds when at or above the 2001 epoch in Unix terms and as Cocoa seconds since 2001 below it, both keeping the fraction. Second, an inventory of every table in `sqlite_master` whose name begins `PL`, in name order. Nothing else in the PowerLog — battery, app usage, camera, display, location, network agents — is parsed, deliberately, because those schemas have not been validated on a held device.

**Produces.** One `PowerLogEvent` (`subtype: "powerlog_event"`, `platform: "iOS"`, `category: "torch"`) per torch row: `event` and `name` as `flashlight on` / `Flashlight ON` when the state is non-zero, `flashlight off` / `Flashlight OFF` when it is zero, and `flashlight (state unknown)` / `Flashlight event` when no state column exists or the value is NULL; `state` as recorded when present; `date` in whole Unix seconds with `date_ns` when the fraction is non-zero, omitted when the value was unset, negative or non-finite. Then one `PowerLogSummary` (`subtype: "powerlog_summary"`, `table_count`, `tables` listing every `PL*` table name, `torch_rows_dropped`, `table_names_dropped`, `torch_status` — `read`, `table_absent` (the catalogue answered: no torch table, a finding), or one of the answers that mean the torch events were not looked at: `undetermined` (the catalogue would not say), `query_did_not_run` (the column list, prepare or query failed) or `time_column_unresolved` (no column recognised as the event time) — with `torch_query_error` carrying SQLite's text or the columns seen; `table_inventory_did_not_run` and `table_inventory_error` when the `PL*` inventory query failed; and — when rows or names were dropped, the torch table was not read, or the inventory did not run — `content_incomplete: true` and `inventory_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` and a `content_incomplete_detail` naming each, because the counts are then a lower bound), emitted whenever a `PL*` table or a dropped name was seen, the torch table was not read, or the inventory did not run; a readable database with no `PL*` table and no torch table yields no summary. A `.PLSQL` carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged or opened yields one `IosArtifactParseStatus` `DatabaseUnreadable` record with both incompleteness pairs. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event of its own beyond what the `date` key projects.

**Cannot.** It cannot tell you anything the PowerLog knows except when the flashlight was toggled and which agent tables exist: battery level and charging (`PLBatteryAgent_*`), app foreground time (`PLApplicationAgent_*`, `PLAppTimeService_*`), screen state (`PLDisplayAgent_*`), camera use, Wi-Fi and cellular state, airplane mode, audio routes and the process-level accounting tables are inventoried by name on the summary and not read, so a `tables` list of two hundred entries is a list of what this device recorded and this tool did not decode. It chooses the torch table's columns by substring on a sorted name list, so a table carrying two timestamp-like or two state-like columns is read from whichever sorts first with nothing on the record to say which was taken. A torch table with no time-like column is not read for its states at all — it is reported `time_column_unresolved`, not guessed at. Its timestamp base is decided by magnitude — a REAL below 978,307,200 is taken as Cocoa — so a genuine Unix time before 2001 is impossible to express, which no PowerLog row predates. It does not join `PLCameraAgent_EventForward_Torch` to the display or lock state, so "flashlight on" is not "phone in hand" without corroboration. It reads one file at a time and does not stitch a rotated `PLSQL` series into one sequence. It recovers no deleted rows.

**Refuses.** It refuses to default an unrecorded flashlight state to "on": without a state column, or with a NULL, the event says the state is unknown. It refuses to parse the agent tables it has not validated on a held device, listing them instead, because a torch event is an activity signal an examiner will place a person by and an over-parsed unvalidated schema would place them wrongly. It refuses to let a dropped torch row or table name vanish, counting each on the summary with the incompleteness pairs, because a gap in that timeline reads as an absence of activity, and refuses to let a torch table that was there and not read — undetermined, unqueryable, or with no time column — pass as a device whose flashlight was never used, stating it as `torch_status` with the error. It refuses to collapse two toggles inside one second onto one instant, keeping the fraction as `date_ns`. It refuses to place an unset timestamp at either epoch. It refuses to file a store it recognised and could not stage or open as a device with no PowerLog, emitting `DatabaseUnreadable`. And it refuses to present a partially staged log as whole, stamping every record with the spill's incompleteness.

### `plugin.ios.routined_locations`

**Reads.** The location cache iOS keeps for itself — `com.apple.routined`'s `Cache.sqlite` — selected by basename, magic and then by table, through the crate's shared front end `with_db`: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the last path segment of the artifact's `name` and acts on exactly `cache.sqlite`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The first 16 bytes are read with a looping `read_full` and must be `SQLite format 3\0`. The file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 1 GiB cap (`MAX_DB_BYTES`) with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one, and the copy opened read-only. Because `Cache.sqlite` is a name many apps use, the table is what selects it: `probe_table` must list `ZRTCLLOCATIONMO`, else the file yields nothing — except that a `Cache.sqlite` whose `path` lies under `com.apple.routined` and whose catalogue would not read is claimed by where it lives and reported (below); elsewhere an unreadable catalogue stays unclaimed, because another app's damaged cache is not a location history. The walk is one fixed statement, `SELECT ZLATITUDE, ZLONGITUDE, ZTIMESTAMP, ZHORIZONTALACCURACY, ZVERTICALACCURACY, ZALTITUDE, ZSPEED, ZCOURSE FROM ZRTCLLOCATIONMO ORDER BY ZTIMESTAMP DESC LIMIT 200001` — one past the 200,000-fix cap (`MAX_LOCATION_FIXES`), newest first — every column read as a REAL with an integer accepted. `ZTIMESTAMP` is Cocoa seconds since 2001-01-01, converted with its fraction. Two CoreLocation conventions are honoured: a negative horizontal accuracy is CoreLocation's own invalidity flag, and -1 speed or course means not measured.

**Produces.** One `CachedLocation` record (`platform: "iOS"`, `source: "com.apple.routined"`) per valid fix, newest first, up to 200,000: `gps_lat` and `gps_lon` (the keys the map screen reads), `timestamp` as an RFC 3339 string to the nanosecond when the Cocoa value is set, `horizontal_accuracy_m` when present, `vertical_accuracy_m` only when non-negative, `altitude_m` only when non-zero, `speed_mps` and `course_deg` only when non-negative, and a `name` of the coordinates to six decimals. Then one `CachedLocationSummary` (`platform`, `source`, `fixes` as the number carried, `invalid_fixes` — rows whose horizontal accuracy was negative, counted and left off the map — and `undecodable_rows` — rows the engine would not step or whose latitude or longitude was NULL), with `inventory_incomplete: true` and a detail sentence when more than 200,000 fixes were in the cache (reason `cap_reached`: the older ones are not in this case) or when any row was undecodable (reason `unresolved_structure`). A `Cache.sqlite` carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged or opened, one whose fixed `SELECT` would not prepare or run, and one at the `com.apple.routined` path whose catalogue would not read, each yield one `IosArtifactParseStatus` record with `status: "DatabaseUnreadable"`, both incompleteness pairs under `unresolved_structure` and the error. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event of its own; the fixes reach the map through their `gps_lat`/`gps_lon` keys.

**Cannot.** It cannot say what the phone was doing at a fix, only where it was: `ZRTLEARNEDLOCATIONOFINTERESTMO`, `ZRTLEARNEDVISITMO`, `ZRTHINTMO`, the `Local.sqlite` visits and the `Cloud.sqlite` store are not read, so significant locations, visit durations and named places are not on the record — only the raw fix trail. It cannot see past the two-hundred-thousandth fix, and since the walk is newest-first the oldest are the ones dropped, as the summary says. It cannot read a generation that renamed a column of its fixed `SELECT`: there is no column map, so that store is reported `DatabaseUnreadable` rather than read for what remains. A `Cache.sqlite` outside the `com.apple.routined` path whose catalogue will not read is not claimed, so a relocated copy of the location cache that is damaged is silent. It does not read `ZSOURCE`, `ZSIGNALENVIRONMENTTYPE`, `ZMAPITEM` or the entity's Core Data relationships, so whether a fix came from GPS, Wi-Fi or cell is not stated and its provenance is `com.apple.routined` only. It treats an altitude of exactly 0.0 as unmeasured and omits it, so a genuine sea-level fix loses its altitude. It cannot tell a fix with no `ZTIMESTAMP`, or one at the 2001 sentinel, from one that was never timed — both carry no `timestamp`. It recovers no deleted rows and reads no `-journal` sibling.

**Refuses.** It refuses to put the phone in the Gulf of Guinea: a fix CoreLocation itself flagged invalid by a negative horizontal accuracy — usually carrying 0,0 — is counted as `invalid_fixes` and left off the map, never plotted. It refuses to report a phone travelling backwards at one metre per second: -1 speed and course are absent from the record, not values. It refuses to present a capped or lossy walk as the whole trail, fetching one row past the cap and stating both shortfalls on the summary with their reasons. It refuses to place an unset Cocoa timestamp at 2001-01-01. It refuses to file a store it recognised and could not stage or open as a device with no cached locations, emitting `DatabaseUnreadable`. It refuses to claim any `Cache.sqlite` on its name, requiring the `ZRTCLLOCATIONMO` table. And it refuses to present a partially staged cache as whole, stamping every record with the spill's incompleteness.

### `plugin.ios.safari_bookmarks`

**Reads.** Safari on iOS's saved bookmarks and reading list, `Bookmarks.db`, selected by basename and magic through the crate's shared front end `with_db` and then told apart from the open-tabs store by table: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the last path segment of the artifact's `name` and acts on exactly `bookmarks.db`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The first 16 bytes are read with a looping `read_full` and must be `SQLite format 3\0`. The file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 1 GiB cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one, and the copy opened read-only. `probe_table` must list `bookmarks`; because that table is byte-identical to the one `SafariTabs.db` keeps its open tabs in, a file that also carries a `windows` table is declared the tabs store and not read here, whatever its name. `PRAGMA user_version` is compared through the shared `check_schema_version` with the single-point range `43..=43`, the version of the one generation these readers were validated against (iOS 15.0, 19A404, the Magnet 2022 iOS 15 device whose counts and shapes were read into `tests/fixtures/magnet2022_ios15` before the code was written). One fixed statement reads every row: `SELECT id, special_id, parent, type, title, url, num_children, hidden, deleted, read, last_modified, order_index, external_uuid, date_closed, length(extra_attributes), length(local_attributes), length(sync_data) FROM bookmarks ORDER BY id`, with no row limit; the three blobs are measured, not decoded. The folder tree is walked upward through `parent`, at most 32 levels (`MAX_FOLDER_DEPTH`) so a cycle cannot loop, and the reading-list folder is the row with `special_id` 3. `last_modified` and `date_closed` are Cocoa REALs converted with their fraction.

**Produces.** One `SafariBookmarkFolder` (`subtype: "safari_bookmark_folder"`) per row of `type` 1 — `bookmark_id`, `parent_id`, `title`, `order_index`, `external_uuid`, `hidden`, `deleted`, `last_modified` with `_ns` and `_source`, `special_id` and, for 1, 3 and 5, `special_role` (`bookmarks_bar`, `reading_list`, `frequently_visited`), `num_children`, `folder_path` from the root, `name: "Safari folder: <title or (untitled)>"` — and one `SafariBookmark` (`subtype: "safari_bookmark"`) per other row: the same identity fields plus `url`, `reading_list` (true when its parent is the `special_id` 3 folder), `read` as a boolean only when Safari recorded it (NULL is absent, not unread), `date_closed`, `folder_path` of its parent, `parent_title`, and `name` of the title, else the URL, else `Safari bookmark`; every record carries `platform: "iOS"` and `source: "Bookmarks.db"`. Before them, unless `PRAGMA user_version` is inside `43..=43`, one shared `ParserStaleWarning` schema record (`app: "Safari Bookmarks.db"`, `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `supported_range`, `validated_against` naming the Magnet 2022 iPhone 8 file, `message`, `detail`, `name`): `SchemaOutsideValidated` with `seen_schema_version` and no incompleteness claim (a disclosure) for another recorded version, `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` with no incompleteness claim for 0, `SchemaVersionUndetermined` with the content pair (reason `unresolved_structure`) for a pragma that would not read. Then one `SafariBookmarksSummary` (`platform`, `source`, `bookmarks`, `folders`, `reading_list_items`, `reading_list_folder_present`, `deleted_rows`, `hidden_rows`, `rows_with_last_modified`, `rows_dropped`, `schema_version`, `attribute_blobs_decoded: false` with `attribute_blob_bytes` so "unread" is a number, `records_recovered`, and `inventory_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` and the first error when any row would not decode). A file with a `windows` table yields a single `SafariBookmarksSummary` with `not_a_bookmarks_store: true`, `records_recovered: 0` and a detail naming `plugin.ios.safari_tabs`. A store whose fixed statement will not prepare — a generation missing a column — yields one `IosArtifactParseStatus` `DatabaseUnreadable` record with both incompleteness pairs and SQLite's own error, after the stale marker; one that could not be staged or opened yields the same record. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event of its own.

**Cannot.** It cannot tell you what is inside `extra_attributes`, `local_attributes` or `sync_data` — the reading-list preview text, the date a reading-list item was added, the site's icon and the iCloud sync payload live there as embedded plists and are counted in bytes, not decoded. It cannot say when a bookmark was created: `last_modified` is what the row carries. It has been validated on one generation: `43` from one iOS 15.0 device, and a store at any other version parses on the assumption its columns mean the same with a stale marker beside the rows — a marker whose `PRAGMA user_version` read goes through the shared `check_schema_version`, which states a version of 0 as not recorded (never older) and a pragma that will not read as undetermined (never in range); no column map exists, so a renamed column fails the whole statement and is reported as unreadable rather than by field. It cannot distinguish a deleted bookmark's content from a live one beyond the `deleted` flag. It cannot read `Bookmarks.db-wal` on its own, `CloudTabs.db`, `History.db` or the reading-list article cache. It has no row cap. It recovers no deleted rows beyond those Safari itself flags.

**Refuses.** It refuses to publish three open tabs as three saved favourites: a `bookmarks` table beside a `windows` table is the open-tabs store, declared as such and left to `plugin.ios.safari_tabs`. It refuses to default `read` to unread when Safari never recorded it. It refuses to present a store whose statement would not run as one with no bookmarks — a generation missing a column is `DatabaseUnreadable` with SQLite's reason, not an empty result. It refuses to decode the attribute blobs it has not validated, counting their bytes instead. It refuses to loop on a cyclic `parent`, stopping at 32 levels. It refuses to place an unset Cocoa date at 2001-01-01 and refuses to drop the fraction a REAL records. It refuses to let a dropped row vanish, counting it on the summary with the `inventory_incomplete` pair and the first error. And it refuses to present a partially staged store as whole, stamping every record with the spill's incompleteness.

### `plugin.ios.safari_searches`

**Reads.** Safari on iOS's recent web searches, which are not in `RecentSearches.plist` but in the `RecentWebSearches` array of the app's own preferences file, `com.apple.mobilesafari.plist`, inside its container. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the last path segment of the artifact's `name` and acts on exactly `com.apple.mobilesafari.plist`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. A file declaring more than 16 MiB (`MAX_SEARCHES_PLIST_BYTES`; the real one is 3.5 KB) is refused before any read. Otherwise the whole file is read with a looping `read_full` and parsed by the `plist` crate as a binary or XML property list; a file that is not a plist, or not a dictionary, is not this reader's and yields nothing. The key selects the file: a dictionary with no `RecentWebSearches` array — CloudDocs keeps an `iCloud.com.apple.mobilesafari.plist` under the same basename, and a preferences file with no search history is not a search store — is left to the generic plist reader. Each array entry is read as a dictionary for `SearchString` and `Date` (a plist date, its fraction intact). From the top level it also reads `DidPromptSearchEngineAlertUDID`, `SSDeviceType` (`buildVersion`, `hardwareModel`, `deviceTypeNumber`), `CloudTabsEnabled`, `HasExtensionsInstalled`, the keys of `BrowserControllersSavedState`, and `LastBookmarksDatabaseHealthReportDate`. The shape was read from the Magnet 2022 iOS 15 device before the code was written.

**Produces.** One `WebSearchQuery` (`subtype: "web_search_query"`, `platform: "iOS"`, `browser: "Safari"`, `source: "com.apple.mobilesafari.plist"`) per array entry with a `SearchString`: `index` (its position in the array), `query`, `search_engine_not_recorded: true` on every record — the plist records the query and when, not which engine served it, and the device's default-engine setting is not read to fill the gap — and either `timestamp` and `date` in Unix seconds with `timestamp_ns`/`date_ns` when a fraction was recorded and `timestamp_source` naming the `RecentWebSearches[].Date` key and its 2001 epoch, or `timestamp_not_recorded: true`; a `name` of `Safari search: <query>`. Then one `SafariSearchesSummary` (`platform`, `source`, `searches`, `entries_undecodable` — entries that were not a dictionary or had no `SearchString` — and, where present, `device_udid` with `device_udid_source: "DidPromptSearchEngineAlertUDID"` so the value is sourced rather than asserted, `build_version`, `hardware_model`, `device_type_number`, `cloud_tabs_enabled`, `extensions_installed`, `browser_window_uuids`, and `last_bookmarks_health_report` with `_ns` and `_source`; `inventory_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` when any entry was undecodable). A file over 16 MiB yields one `IosArtifactParseStatus` record with `status: "PlistUnreadable"`, both incompleteness pairs under `cap_reached`, `records_recovered: 0` and the sizes; one that delivered fewer bytes than declared yields the same with reason `short_read` and the counts. No timeline event of its own beyond what `date` projects.

**Cannot.** It cannot say which search engine ran a query, and says so on every record rather than reading the default-engine preference and presenting it as the engine used. It cannot see a search Safari has already aged out of the array — the plist keeps a bounded recent list, not a history — nor a search typed in a private tab, nor one on another device, and it cannot say whether the query was submitted or only typed. It reads the array in file order and does not order by date. It does not read the rest of the preferences — `SearchEngineStringSetting` (the engine setting itself), `WarnAboutFraudulentWebsites`, `SafariDoNotTrackEnabled`, the per-site settings — and the `BrowserControllersSavedState` dictionaries are reduced to their keys. A file whose `RecentWebSearches` is present but not an array yields nothing, as if the key were absent. It cannot tell a plist that is a dictionary without the key from one that is not Safari's at all: both are silently left to the generic plist reader. It has no cap on the array's length beyond the 16 MiB file ceiling.

**Refuses.** It refuses to fill the engine from the device's default: `search_engine_not_recorded` is stated as a limit of the source. It refuses to claim the file by name alone, because the same basename exists elsewhere; the `RecentWebSearches` key is what selects it. It refuses to read a short delivery as the file, filing `PlistUnreadable` with `short_read` and the counts, and refuses to read a file over the ceiling, filing `cap_reached`. It refuses to invent a timestamp for an entry with no `Date`, stating `timestamp_not_recorded`. It refuses to drop the fraction a plist date records. It refuses to present the device UDID without naming the key it came from. And it refuses to let an undecodable entry vanish, counting it on the summary with the `inventory_incomplete` pair.

### `plugin.ios.safari_tabs`

**Reads.** Safari on iOS's open tabs, from whichever generation of store the device wrote, selected by basename and magic through the crate's shared front end `with_db` and by table set thereafter: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the last path segment of the artifact's `name` and acts on exactly `safaritabs.db` or `browserstate.db`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The first 16 bytes are read with a looping `read_full` and must be `SQLite format 3\0`. The file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 1 GiB cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one, and the copy opened read-only. A store with both `windows` and `bookmarks` is the iOS 15+ generation; one with both `tabs` and `browser_windows` is iOS 13/14; anything else yields nothing. On the iOS 15+ generation `PRAGMA user_version` is compared through the shared `check_schema_version` with `43..=43` and every `bookmarks` row is read by the same fixed 17-column statement the bookmarks reader uses, then `windows` (`id, uuid, private_tab_group_id, local_tab_group_id, active_tab_group_id, date_closed`), `windows_tab_groups` (`tab_group_id, window_id, active_tab_id`), and each tab's `local_attributes` blob (`WHERE type = 0 AND local_attributes IS NOT NULL`), which is a binary plist read for `LastVisitTime` (a plist date, fraction intact), `OpenedFromLink`, `ShowingReader`, `TabIndex` and `SessionState` — a 4-byte big-endian version followed by a binary plist whose `SessionHistory` dictionary holds the tab's back/forward list (`SessionHistoryCurrentIndex`, `SessionHistoryEntries` with URL, original URL and title), observed uncompressed at version 2 on iOS 15 and read only in that form. On the iOS 13/14 generation the range is `5..=5`, `tabs` is read by a fixed 13-column statement `ORDER BY browser_window_id, order_index`, `tab_sessions` (`tab_uuid, length(session_data), uncompressed_session_data_size`) is measured, and `browser_windows` is counted. Every shape and count was read from the Magnet 2022 iOS 15 device (19A404) into `tests/fixtures/magnet2022_ios15` before the code was written; a device carries both files, and on iOS 15 the older one has an empty `tabs` table.

**Produces.** One `SafariOpenTab` (`subtype: "safari_open_tab"`, `platform: "iOS"`, `source` and `source_schema` naming the file) per tab. From `SafariTabs.db`: `tab_id`, `title`, `url` (when non-empty), `order_index`, `tab_uuid`, `deleted`, `private_browsing` (true when the tab's parent folder is any window's `private_tab_group_id`), `tab_group_id`, `tab_group` (the folder's title), `window_id`, `window_uuid`, `is_active_tab`, `tab_group_is_active`, or `window_unresolved: true` when no window claims the group; `last_modified` and `date_closed` with `_ns` and `_source`; from the attributes plist `last_visit` and `date` (both in Unix seconds, `_ns` when a fraction was recorded, `last_visit_source` naming the plist key and its 2001 epoch), `opened_from_link`, `showing_reader`, `tab_index`; and the session state — `session_state_present: false`, or `true` with `session_state_bytes` and either `session_history_decoded: true`, `session_history_current_index`, `session_history_entries` (the total) and `session_history` (up to 500 entries of `url`/`original_url`/`title`, with `session_history_truncated: true`, reason `cap_reached` and `session_history_cap: 500` beyond that), or `session_history_decoded: false` with `content_incomplete: true`, reason `unresolved_structure` and a sentence saying the back/forward history is present and unread; `local_attributes_present: false` when the tab has no blob; a `name` of the title, else the URL, else `Safari tab`, suffixed ` (private)`. One `SafariWindow` (`subtype: "safari_window"`) per `windows` row with its uuid, the three group ids, `date_closed`. Titled folders under Root are counted as tab groups, not emitted. From `BrowserState.db`: `tab_id`, `tab_uuid`, `title`, `url`, `user_visible_url`, `order_index`, `last_visit`/`date` from `last_viewed_time` (Cocoa REAL, with `_ns` and `_source`), `private_browsing` from the column (`false` when NULL), `opened_from_link`, `showing_reader`, `window_uuid`, `window_id`, `reading_list_bookmark_id` when non-zero, and `session_state_present` with `session_state_bytes`, `session_state_uncompressed_bytes`, `session_history_decoded: false`, `content_incomplete: true` and reason `unvalidated` because no held generation has a `tab_sessions` row — or, when the `tab_sessions` query did not run, `session_state_unknown: true` with `session_state_unknown_reason`, never "no session". Before the tabs, unless the version is inside the range, one shared `ParserStaleWarning` schema record (`app` `Safari SafariTabs.db` or `Safari BrowserState.db`, `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `supported_range`, `validated_against`, `message`, `detail`, `name`): `SchemaOutsideValidated` with `seen_schema_version` and no incompleteness claim (a disclosure), `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` for 0 with no incompleteness claim, or `SchemaVersionUndetermined` with the content pair (reason `unresolved_structure`) for a pragma that would not read. Then one `SafariTabsSummary` (`source`, `source_schema`, `tabs`, `private_tabs`, `windows`, `tab_groups` or — on `BrowserState.db` — `session_rows`, `windows` or, where the `browser_windows` count would not read, `windows_count_error` with `content_incomplete` (reason `unresolved_structure`) and a name saying `windows not counted` rather than zero windows , `tab_sessions_table_absent: true`, or `session_rows_query_did_not_run: true` with `session_rows_query_error`; `rows_dropped`, `attribute_blob_bytes_undecoded` (the `extra_attributes`, `sync_data` and every attribute blob's bytes), `schema_version`, `records_recovered`, `inventory_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` when any row would not decode, and on an empty iOS 13/14 `tabs` table `tabs_table_empty: true` with a `generation_note` saying an empty `BrowserState.db` does not mean no tabs were open). A statement that will not prepare — the `bookmarks`, `windows` or `windows_tab_groups` query on the newer generation, `tabs` on the older — yields one `IosArtifactParseStatus` `DatabaseUnreadable` record with both incompleteness pairs and SQLite's error, because a tab published without the windows answer is a tab published as not private. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended.

**Cannot.** It cannot decode a `SessionState` that is not an uncompressed version-2 binary plist — a compressed or differently versioned one is `session_history_decoded: false` with the incompleteness pair — and it cannot decode `tab_sessions.session_data` on iOS 13/14 at all, because no held device has a row there; both are present-and-unread, never absent. It cannot say what `extra_attributes` or `sync_data` hold, counting their bytes. Its schema knowledge is one point per generation (43 and 5, from one iOS 15.0 device), the version check goes through the shared `check_schema_version`, which states a `PRAGMA user_version` of 0 as not recorded (never older) and a pragma that will not read as undetermined (never in range) , and no column map exists: a renamed column fails the fixed statement and the store is reported unreadable rather than by field. It cannot tell a pinned tab from a recently-closed one on iOS 15: the untitled containers are counted among neither tab groups nor tabs in a distinguished way, and `date_closed` is the only sign a tab was closed. It cannot name the window a tab-group folder belongs to when `windows_tab_groups` does not claim it (`window_unresolved`). Its private-tab reading on iOS 15 rests on the tab's parent being a window's `private_tab_group_id`; a private tab moved to a user-named group would read as not private. It does not read `CloudTabs.db` (tabs open on the user's other devices), `History.db`, or the tab's favicon and snapshot. It has no row cap beyond the 500-entry session history. It recovers no deleted rows beyond those Safari flags.

**Refuses.** It refuses to report an empty iOS 13/14 `tabs` table as "no tabs were open": on an iOS 15 device that file is still written and its tabs live in `SafariTabs.db`, so the summary says `tabs_table_empty` and why. It refuses to publish a tab as not private when the windows query that decides privacy did not run — the whole store is `DatabaseUnreadable` instead. It refuses to decode a session encoding it has not seen on a held device, marking it present and unread with the pair (`unvalidated` on iOS 13/14, `unresolved_structure` on a non-plist `SessionState`). It refuses to present a 500-entry back/forward list as the whole when more entries exist, stating the total, the cap and the reason. It refuses to place an unset Cocoa date at 2001-01-01 and refuses to drop the fraction a plist date or REAL column records. It refuses to let a dropped row vanish, counting it on the summary with the `inventory_incomplete` pair. And it refuses to present a partially staged store as whole, stamping every record with the spill's incompleteness.

### `plugin.ios.voicemail`

**Reads.** iOS's visual-voicemail index, `voicemail.db`, selected by basename and magic through the crate's shared front end `with_db`: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the last path segment of the artifact's `name` and acts only on exactly `voicemail.db`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The first 16 bytes are read with a looping `read_full` and must be `SQLite format 3\0`, else the file is passed over in silence. The file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 1 GiB cap (`MAX_DB_BYTES`) with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one — on a live-seized device the newest rows are only there — and the copy opened read-only. `probe_table` must list a table or view named `voicemail`. The walk is one fixed statement, `SELECT ROWID, date, sender, callback_num, duration, trashed_date, receiver FROM voicemail ORDER BY date`, with no row limit; `date` is taken as Unix seconds as `voicemail.db` stores it, text columns are read with an empty string treated as absent, and integer columns tolerate a real. No column map is used: the seven names are fixed. Then, when `probe_table` lists a `deleted` table, its rows are read the same way, `ORDER BY ROWID`, with a column the table lacks read as NULL. On the Magnet 2022 iPhone 8 the top-level `Library/Voicemail/voicemail.db` has one, with the `voicemail` table's twelve columns and no rows; the per-account store beside it has none.

**Produces.** One `Voicemail` record (`subtype: "voicemail"`, `platform: "iOS"`) per row: `rowid`, `date` in Unix seconds when positive, `sender` and `contact` (both the `sender` string), `callback_number`, `duration_seconds`, `receiver`, `deleted` — `true` when `trashed_date` is positive, `false` when it is 0 or negative, JSON `null` when the column is NULL (the column recorded nothing, so nothing is asserted) — and a `name` of `Voicemail from <sender or "unknown">`, and `source_table` naming the table it came from; a row of the `deleted` table also carries `row_semantics_validated: false`. After the rows, one `VoicemailIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker (`subtype: parse_incomplete`, `source_table: "voicemail"`, `rows_dropped`, `records_recovered`, `first_error`, both incompleteness pairs with reason `unresolved_structure`) when the engine refused to step a row. Then one `VoicemailSummary` (`platform: "iOS"`, `source`, `source_table`, `voicemails`, `trashed`, `rows_undecodable`, `records_recovered`, `name`, and `deleted_table_present`; where it is present, `deleted_table_rows`, `deleted_table_rows_undecodable`, `deleted_table_semantics_validated: false` and a `deleted_table_note` sentence; where it could not be read, `deleted_table_unread: true` with the `content_incomplete` pair) for every store whose `voicemail` table was walked, zero included, so a present and empty table is a record rather than silence (both `voicemail.db` files on the Magnet 2022 iPhone 8 are that). A `voicemail.db` carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged or opened yields one `IosArtifactParseStatus` record with `status: "DatabaseUnreadable"`, both pairs under `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0` and the error. A readable catalogue holding none of the tables this reader is built on yields one `IosArtifactParseStatus` with `status: "ExpectedTableAbsent"`, `expected_tables`, both pairs under `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0` and a sentence saying this is not a schema this reader knows — not a finding that the device held none; a catalogue that would not read, and a fixed `SELECT` that would not prepare or run, each yield one `DatabaseUnreadable` record naming SQLite's error. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended, even when nothing parsed. No timeline event of its own.

**Cannot.** It cannot give you the message: the audio (`.amr` files beside the database) and any transcript (`transcription` on iOS 10+) are not read, so a voicemail is a sender, a time and a length. It does not read `flags` (heard/unheard, downloaded), `token`, `remote_uid`, `expiration_date` or `label`, so whether a voicemail was listened to is not on the record. It cannot read a generation that renamed any column of its fixed `SELECT` (`callback_num`, `trashed_date`, …): there is no column map, so such a store is reported `DatabaseUnreadable` rather than read for the columns that remain. It cannot say what a row of the store's `deleted` table means: no device held has one, so each is read with the `voicemail` table's column meanings, labelled by its table and marked unvalidated, and `voicemails` on the summary counts the `voicemail` table alone. It has no row cap. It recovers no deleted rows and reads no `-journal` sibling.

**Refuses.** It refuses to file a store it recognised and could not stage or open as a device with no voicemails, emitting `DatabaseUnreadable` with both incompleteness pairs, and refuses to spend an absent table, an unreadable catalogue or a query that would not run as "no voicemails". It refuses to write `deleted: false` for a NULL `trashed_date`. It refuses to read a short probe as "not SQLite": the magic is read with a looping `read_full`. It refuses to let a row the engine would not step vanish, counting it into the `RowsUndecodable` marker so the count reads as a floor. It refuses to place a 0 `date` at the epoch, leaving `date` off. And it refuses to present a partially staged database as whole, stamping every record — and an empty result — with the spill's incompleteness.

### `plugin.linux.host_facts`

**Reads.** Six identity files of a Linux system, recognised by path and not by name. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` artifacts, takes `path` or, failing that, `name`, normalises backslashes to slashes and lowercases, and accepts the artifact only when that string equals or ends with `/etc/os-release` or `/usr/lib/os-release`, `/etc/lsb-release`, `/etc/hostname`, `/etc/machine-id` or `/var/lib/dbus/machine-id`, `/etc/timezone`, or `/etc/passwd` — a leading-slash-stripped exact match is also accepted so a volume walked without a root prefix still matches. A directory at such a path, and an entry with no data source, are declined. It then issues one `read_at` from offset 0 for the lesser of the file's declared size and 1,048,576 bytes, and works on whatever that single call returned. A release file is parsed line by line as `KEY=value`: blank lines and `#` comments skipped, the value trimmed and unwrapped from one pair of double or single quotes, empty values dropped, keys uppercased. From `os-release` it takes `NAME` as `os_name`, `VERSION` as `os_version`, `VERSION_ID`, `VERSION_CODENAME` then `UBUNTU_CODENAME` as `codename`, `ID` as `os_id`, `ID_LIKE` as `os_like`, `PRETTY_NAME`, `BUILD_ID` and `VARIANT`; from `lsb-release` it takes `DISTRIB_ID` as `os_name` — the vendor's capitalised name, not the lowercase `ID` — `DISTRIB_RELEASE` as `version_id`, `DISTRIB_CODENAME` as `codename` and `DISTRIB_DESCRIPTION` as `pretty_name`. `hostname`, `machine-id` and `timezone` are read as the first non-blank line, trimmed, and accepted only if it is 255 characters or fewer and contains no whitespace or control character; a machine id must further be exactly 32 hexadecimal characters and a time zone must contain a `/`. `passwd` is read as colon-separated lines: a line that is not exactly seven fields, or whose uid or gid is not a `u32`, is counted as unparsed; at most 2,000 accounts are kept; an account is marked a login account when its uid is 0 or at least 1000 and is not 65534.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per identity file, of `type: HostDeviceInfo` with `platform: linux`, parented to the file. It carries a `name` naming the file's role (`Linux host facts from os-release`, `Linux host name`, `Linux accounts from passwd`, and so on), `source_file` (the path as it was matched), `source_kind` (`os_release`, `lsb_release`, `hostname`, `machine_id`, `timezone`, `passwd`), a `facts` object and a `fact_sources` object that names, for every fact, the key it was read from — `VERSION_ID` against `DISTRIB_RELEASE`, or `file contents` for the single-line files, or `passwd entry` — because two files can state different things and an examiner quoting one has to say which. The `passwd` record's only fact is `user_account`, an array of strings of the form `name (uid N, home, shell)` holding the login accounts alone, alongside `accounts_read` (every parsed line, service accounts included) and `unparsed_lines`. Nothing is reconciled across files: `/etc/os-release` and `/usr/lib/os-release` each get their own record, and the device-facts endpoint — `GET /api/v1/cases/:id/device_info`, which fetches every `HostDeviceInfo` record and folds it in `compile_device_info` — shows the disagreement rather than choosing. When the single read returned fewer bytes than asked, or the file was over 1 MiB, the record carries `content_incomplete: true`, `content_incomplete_reason: short_read` and a `content_incomplete_detail` sentence naming the byte count; when such a truncated file yielded no fact at all, a record with `subtype: identity_unread`, empty `facts` and the same pair is emitted so the file does not vanish from the host summary. A file at an identity path that is read in full and states no fact produces nothing. No timeline events, no hashes, no `SystemArtifact` — the record is the whole output.

**Cannot.** It cannot tell the system's own identity file from a copy of one. The match is a path suffix, so `/etc/hostname` inside a Docker overlay, a chroot, a backup tarball's extracted tree or a second distribution's root on the same image is claimed as a Linux host name with the same confidence as the root's, and only `source_file` lets an examiner tell them apart. It reconciles nothing and ranks nothing, by design. It reads no `/etc/shadow`, `/etc/group`, `/etc/sudoers`, `/etc/hosts`, `/etc/fstab`, network configuration, SSH host keys, `/etc/localtime` (so a system whose zone is set only by that symlink, which is every systemd system without an `/etc/timezone`, has no `timezone` fact), no kernel version (nothing under `/boot` or `/lib/modules` is read), and none of the older release files — `/etc/redhat-release`, `/etc/debian_version`, `/etc/alpine-release`, `/etc/issue`. The `passwd` record carries the login accounts only; the doc comment above `is_login_account` says the record carries every account and merely marks these, and that is not what the code does — service accounts survive as a count in `accounts_read` and nothing else. The uid rule is a convention: a person given uid 999, or a service given 1000, is misfiled. A `/etc/timezone` holding `UTC` — a valid tzdata name — is rejected for lacking a slash and nothing is recorded; a hostname with a space, or over 255 characters, likewise. Only the first non-blank line of a single-line file is read. Values are lossily decoded from UTF-8. The read is one `read_at`, not `read_full`: the core I/O module says a single call may legitimately return fewer bytes, so a windowed or container-backed source can produce a `short_read` record for a file that was entirely readable — the marker is then true of the read and misleading about the evidence. The 1 MiB ceiling is a hard cap on `passwd`; a host with more than 2,000 accounts lists the first 2,000. `FileContent` artifacts are subscribed to but a decoded span carries a generated name, not an identity path, so none has been observed to match. It records nothing about *when*: no file times reach the record, and it emits nothing to the timeline.

**Refuses.** It refuses to claim a fact from a file whose contents do not state one. A `machine-id` that is not 32 hex characters — a placeholder, a comment, an empty file — is not a machine id and produces nothing rather than an invented identity; a `hostname` or `timezone` that fails the single-line rules produces nothing; a release file with none of the tabled keys produces nothing; a `passwd` with no parseable line, or no login account, produces nothing. Those silences are deliberate and are logged at debug level only. It refuses to let a name alone select the file: a shell script called `hostname` or a Metasploit module called `passwd` is not matched, because the path is what makes the file the system's own. It refuses a directory and an entry without content. It refuses to present a partial read as a whole one — the `short_read` pair and detail exist for that — and refuses to let a truncated identity file disappear: where the truncated bytes stated nothing, `identity_unread` records that whether the file named this host could not be established from what is here. A read error from the source is returned as `ParsingError` naming the path, which the processing log records as an error against that artifact.

### `plugin.linux.utmp`

**Reads.** The login-accounting family, whose files carry no magic number at all: Linux `utmp`, `wtmp` and `btmp` (`struct utmp`), Linux `lastlog` (`struct lastlog`) and macOS `/var/run/utmpx` (Darwin's `struct utmpx`). Which C struct wrote a file is worked out from the bytes — the record stride must divide the file exactly, and the sampled records must clear a field-sanity filter — and the byte order is detected the same way rather than assumed. The filename supplies only the file's role, because the three `struct utmp` files are byte-for-byte identical and nothing in a record says 'this attempt failed'. Three layouts are known: glibc's 384-byte record, musl's 400-byte one, and Darwin's 628-byte one, which is a different record rather than a variant — its strings come first, its `ut_type` sits at 296 rather than 0, and it has no address field.

**Produces.** One `LoginSession` per reconstructed session, with the account, the terminal, the source host and address, the PID and both ends where both were written; one `FailedLogin` per record in a `btmp`; one `BootEvent` per boot, clean shutdown, run-level change or clock change; one `LastLogin` per UID from a `lastlog`; a `UtmpParseStatus` provenance row naming the layout, the byte order and every count; and a `TimelineEvent` per dated record. Timestamps are UTC Unix seconds, which is what the kernel writes, so no timezone conversion is applied.

**Cannot.** It cannot invent an end. A session closed by a reboot has no recorded logout; `last(1)` prints a duration for it anyway by assuming the machine went down at the boot record, and this reader carries that time as an explicit upper bound instead, leaving the logout absent — because a logout that was never written must not be presented as one that was. It cannot name the account behind a `lastlog` record: that file is indexed by UID and carries no username, so the UID is reported and no name is derived. On a macOS `utmpx` it cannot give any history: that file holds only the sessions open when the image was taken, macOS keeps no `btmp`, and since 10.5 no on-disk `wtmpx` — `plugin.macos.asl` and `plugin.macos.openbsm` read where that history went. It cannot tell you which direction a Darwin clock change moved the wall clock with evidence behind it: three and four mean opposite things in the two `ut_type` enumerations, the Darwin order is taken from Apple's header, and no macOS clock-change record has been seen to check it against.

**Refuses.** It refuses a file whose size is not a whole number of records of a **known** layout, because a stride wrong by four bytes yields records that look sane and are entirely fictional. It refuses to read a plain-text file as login accounting whatever it is called — `/etc/logrotate.d/wtmp` is four lines of configuration and was being filed as a failed parse. It refuses to report a timestamp outside 1980–2106 as a date, reporting the stored value instead of a fabricated 1970. And where a file's name claimed it was login accounting and it was not read, it refuses to stay silent: a zeroed `wtmp` is a classic anti-forensic artefact and gets a record saying so, because absence of login records is not evidence that no logins occurred.

### `plugin.macos.ds_store`

**Reads.** A Finder `.DS_Store` file — an Apple Buddy allocator holding a B-tree of per-filename records — and it decodes the records, where the carver only recognises the magic. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent`, declines a directory and an entry with no data source, and selects in two ways: if the artifact's `name` (its basename, case-insensitive) is `.ds_store` the file is read; otherwise eight bytes are gathered with `read_full` and the file is read only if bytes 4–8 are `Bud1`. Either way it then reads up to 268,435,456 bytes with `read_capped`, again requires `Bud1` at 4–8 (bytes 0–4, the alignment word, are not checked), and notes whether fewer bytes arrived than the source declared. All buddy structures are big-endian. The buddy header at 8 gives the bookkeeping offset, which must equal its copy at 16; the bookkeeping block sits at that offset plus 4 and holds a block count (1 to 4,194,304), an unused word, the block address table padded to a multiple of 256 slots, a directory count (at most 65,536) and that many entries of `u8 length`, name, `u32 block`. The entry named `DSDB`, matched case-insensitively, names the master block, whose first word is the root node id; levels, record count and block count that follow are not read. An address is decoded as the 32-aligned offset in its high bits plus 4, with a 5-bit size exponent in the low bits. A node opens with `mode` and `count`: mode 0 is a leaf of `count` records; otherwise `count` pairs of child id and record followed by the trailing child named by `mode`. A record is a `u32` name length in UTF-16 units (1 to 8,192), the UTF-16BE name decoded lossily, a 4-byte structure id, a 4-byte data type that must be one of `bool`, `shor`, `long`, `type`, `comp`, `dutc`, `blob` or `ustr`, and the typed value, which is measured — 1, 4, 8, or a length-prefixed blob or string — and skipped. The walk keeps a visited set, stops at depth 64 and at 2,000,000 records. If the B-tree walk yields no record at all, the whole buffer is scanned byte by byte for the same record shape under stricter rules — names of 1 to 1,024 units that decode as strict UTF-16 with no control characters, a structure id of four printable ASCII bytes, a known data type, an in-bounds value.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per distinct filename, in first-seen order, of `type: DSStoreEntry` with `subtype: ds_store`, parented to the `.DS_Store` file. It carries the `filename` (also as `name`) and `structures`: the de-duplicated, ordered list of four-character structure ids that were recorded for that name — `Iloc`, `bwsp`, `lsvp`, `vSrn`, `moDD`, `ptbL` and the rest — which is the evidence that Finder held metadata about a file of that name in that folder. The value of a record is never published: `structures` says a `moDD` existed, not what date it held. When the input was read short of its declared size, or the 2,000,000-record budget stopped the walk, one further `ParsedRecord` of `type: DSStoreParseStatus` with `subtype: ds_store_incomplete` and `name: .DS_Store (partially parsed)` follows, carrying `content_incomplete: true`, `content_incomplete_reason` (`cap_reached` if the budget fired, else `short_read`), `entries_emitted`, `record_cap_reached`, `input_truncated`, `bytes_read`, `declared_size`, `max_records` and `max_file_bytes`. The frontend lists the entries as a filename-by-structures table under Files and media, and the status record under what could not be read. No timeline events, no hashes, no per-record values.

**Cannot.** It cannot say when. Every date a `.DS_Store` holds — the `moDD`/`modD` modification dates, the `dutc` values — is measured and skipped, so nothing from this module reaches the timeline and no entry carries an instant. It cannot say where a file was, what its icon position, window geometry, view style, sort order or comment were: the value of every structure is discarded, and `ptbL`/`ptbN` path records are reported as present, not decoded. It does not say which folder the `.DS_Store` describes beyond the parent artifact link. It recovers nothing from a record it could not decode, and says nothing about having stopped: a record with an unknown data type, a name length outside the cap or a value running past the buffer ends the current node silently, and the remaining records of that node — and, for an internal node, the subtrees after it — are absent from the output with no `DSStoreParseStatus`, because only the record budget and a short input produce one. A B-tree that yields nothing falls back to a pattern scan of the entire buffer, free and stale buddy blocks included; records recovered that way are indistinguishable in the output from records read from the live tree, though a stale record may name a file long since removed from the folder — often the more interesting fact, and one that is not marked. The linear scan is a heuristic with the false-positive rate its rules give it, and it can also miss a record whose name contains a control character or a lone surrogate. Names are lossily decoded. The tree is never cross-checked against the master block's record count or levels, so a truncated tree that happens to end on a node boundary reads as complete. Ceilings: 256 MiB of input, 2,000,000 records, 4,194,304 buddy blocks, 65,536 directory entries, depth 64, 8,192-unit names in the tree and 1,024 in the scan. A file at a `.DS_Store` name that lacks the `Bud1` magic yields nothing and no record. No real `.DS_Store` is in the fixture set: `real_sample` runs only when `SEANCE_DSSTORE_SAMPLE` names one, and it asserts every artifact is a `DSStoreEntry`, so a real sample that also emits the status marker fails it.

**Refuses.** It refuses to present a prefix of a folder's inventory as the whole of it, because a `.DS_Store` entry is often the only surviving proof that a named file was ever in a folder, and a list that stopped early would let an examiner conclude a name was never there : a short read of the input, and a walk that hit the record budget, each produce the `DSStoreParseStatus` record with its counts. It refuses a bookkeeping offset that does not match its own copy, a block count of zero or over the cap, a directory count over the cap, a missing `DSDB` entry, a node id outside the address table, a record with an unknown data type or a name outside the length cap, and any offset that would leave the buffer — each ends the walk or the node it is in, and none panics; malformed input yields fewer entries or none. It refuses to trust the name alone: a `.DS_Store` without `Bud1` at bytes 4–8 is not parsed. It refuses to read more than 256 MiB of a candidate, and to keep more than 2,000,000 records. What it does not refuse, and what the section above records, is a structural stop inside a node: that ends decoding quietly.

### `plugin.macos.fsevents`

**Reads.** The per-volume FSEvents logs a Mac keeps under `/.fseventsd/`, recognised by content alone. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with no path, name or magic pre-check: every artifact that has a data source is read with `read_capped` up to 268,435,456 bytes, and what was read is examined. If the first two bytes are `1f 8b` the buffer is inflated as a gzip stream — as concatenated members, since FSEvents logs are sometimes several — under a 268,435,456-byte ceiling checked one byte past the limit so a stream cut at the cap is told apart from one that ended there; a decode error keeps whatever inflated and marks it truncated rather than discarding it, because the commonest cause is an input cut short. If the result, or the raw buffer when it was not gzip, does not begin with `1SLD` or `2SLD` the artifact is declined in silence. The DLS stream is then walked page by page: a 12-byte header of the four-byte magic, an unread `u32`, and a `u32` page size (at least 12), followed by records packed to the page end. Each record is a NUL-terminated UTF-8 path, a `u64` event id and a `u32` flag word; a `2SLD` page's records carry a further `u64` node id. The flag word is decoded against a table of twenty-one named bits — `FolderEvent`, `Mount`, `Unmount`, `EndOfTransaction`, `LastHardLinkRemoved`, `HardLink`, `SymbolicLink`, `FileEvent`, `PermissionChange`, `ExtendedAttrModified`, `ExtendedAttrRemoved`, `DocumentRevision`, `ItemCloned`, `Created`, `Removed`, `InodeMetaMod`, `Renamed`, `Modified`, `Exchange`, `FinderInfoMod`, `FolderCreated`. A page's zero-padded tail is recognised as the natural end; anything else left unread on a page, a header claiming more bytes than the buffer holds, a page magic that is neither `1SLD` nor `2SLD` on bytes that are not padding, and a trailing fragment too short for a header are each recorded as a structural stop. At most 500,000 records are taken from one log.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per record with a non-empty path, of `type: FSEventsRecord` with `subtype: fsevents`, parented to the log file, carrying `path` exactly as the record wrote it, `name` (its last path component), `event_id`, `flags` (the raw word), `flag_names` (the decoded list, empty when no known bit is set) and, for a `2SLD` record, `node_id`. Records are emitted in log order, one log at a time; nothing joins the logs of a volume, orders them by event id or de-duplicates. When anything stopped the walk short — the input read short of its declared size, the gzip output capped or its decode failing, the 500,000-record cap, or a structural stop — one further `ParsedRecord` of `type: FSEventsParseStatus` with `subtype: fsevents_incomplete` and `name: FSEvents log (partially parsed)` follows, carrying both `content_incomplete` and `inventory_incomplete` with the same reason and detail: `short_read` when the source delivered fewer bytes than it declared while that size was at or under the cap — the rest is not in this image; `unresolved_structure` when only the page structure stopped early — the log is damaged rather than long; `cap_reached` otherwise — the rest exists and was not extracted. It also carries `records_emitted`, `compressed_input_truncated`, `decompressed_output_truncated`, `record_cap_reached`, `page_structure_stopped_early` and the three ceilings. The help page's description — per-path change records with their event ids, independent of file timestamps — is what these are. No timeline events: an FSEvents record carries no time and none is invented.

**Cannot.** It cannot say when anything happened. A DLS record holds an event id and flags, no timestamp; the log's own file name (the hex of its last event id) and the log file's modification time are the only things that bound its events in time, and neither is read, so no record reaches the timeline and none carries an instant. The comparison table's ✅ and the help page are accurate about that; the macOS design document's section on this plugin is not — it still describes an output of `TimelineEvent` with event ids mapped to timestamps, a `Stream` input and selection on `.fseventsd/sl-*`, none of which the code does, and marks the plugin shipped. It cannot pair events into a rename, reconstruct a file's history or attribute an event to a process or user; each record stands alone. It reads only `1SLD` and `2SLD` pages; any other page version stops the walk as a structural stop and the events in and after it are unread. Flag bits outside the table — `0x08`, `0x10`, `0x40`, the bits between `0x20` and `0x800` — are absent from `flag_names` and visible only in `flags`. It does not say which volume a log belongs to beyond the parent link, nor whether the path is absolute: paths are published as written, which in a real log is relative to the volume root. Its selection is by content alone and it has no cheap pre-check, so every `FileEntry` with content on every exhibit is read whole up to 256 MiB, and every gzip file — every `.gz` log, every gzipped archive member — is inflated up to 256 MiB, before four bytes decide it was not an FSEvents log; that is a cost, not an error, but it is paid on every image. Paths are decoded lossily. A record with an empty path is dropped without count. The walk does not check that pages are contiguous by event id, so a log with an internal gap reads as complete. Ceilings: 256 MiB of compressed input, 256 MiB inflated, 500,000 records per log, and a log that exceeds any of them is cut at that point and reported. No real `.fseventsd` log is in the fixture set — the tests build DLS pages by hand — though the Raspberry Pi validation run recorded two `FSEventsRecord`s from a card that had been mounted on a Mac.

**Refuses.** It refuses to let a partly parsed event history look like a whole one, and refuses to give the wrong reason for the shortfall: a parser cap, a damaged log and a source that could not deliver its bytes call for three different follow-ups — raise a limit, recover the file, re-image — and `content_incomplete_reason` names which. It refuses to discard what inflated when a gzip member ends mid-stream, keeping the pages that decoded and marking them partial rather than treating the log as not an FSEvents log at all. It refuses to inflate past 256 MiB, reading one byte past the ceiling so the truncation is detectable, and refuses to read a record whose terminator or fixed fields fall past the page end — that record and the rest of its page are left unread and the stop is recorded when the bytes were not padding. It refuses a page whose declared size is under 12 bytes, since it would never advance. It refuses to enter a page whose magic it does not know. It declines, silently and by design, anything that is neither a gzip stream wrapping DLS pages nor a raw DLS buffer, and an artifact with no data source; and it never panics on truncated or malformed input, which the tests hold in place.

### `plugin.macos.host_facts`
