**Cannot.** It cannot attribute a match to a process or to an allocation, and says so on every record: an image's own space has no allocation list, the rows carry no `pid` and no region, and the per-process scan is what answers that question — for a capture with no page tables it cannot be asked at all. It cannot evaluate a YARA rule over the image: each rule is evaluated against one 16 MiB chunk at a time, so a condition joining two strings fires only where both fall in the same chunk, `filesize` is meaningless because there is no file, a count counts within a chunk, and a larger chunk moves those boundaries rather than removing them. Because neither a YARA rule nor a regular expression has a knowable maximum match length, the chunk overlap is the 4,096-byte ceiling and a match straddling a boundary is not guaranteed to be found — the pass publishes `pattern_may_exceed_overlap` for it, and `content_complete` does not account for it. A regular expression here matches raw bytes and is Unicode-unaware, so a pattern written in ASCII does not find the same characters held as UTF-16, and a zero-length match is not reported at all. It stops at finite ceilings and names the address each fired at: 100,000 matches per pass, 10,000 matches carried as rows with the totals still exact, 262,144 planned regions, and 512 GiB of one image. The bytes above a ceiling that fired are published as `not_searched_bytes`, apart from `unreadable_bytes` and `unmapped_bytes`: on the corpus hibernation file the capped pass reports 4,554,682,367 not searched and 0 unreadable. It cannot tell a swap slot written by the workload from one left by an earlier run, which is why the corpus swap area yields 4,587 markers where the workload wrote 4,096. Finally, it cannot be present at all when nothing was named, so an examiner must read the module list rather than an empty result, and it cannot say more about a refused chunk than its address, its length and the engine's own words.

**Refuses.** It refuses to exist with no pattern to search for: `ImagePatternScan::new` returns nothing for an empty set list, so a deployment that named neither a rule set nor a pattern does not carry this module, because a module that is registered, reports success and searches for nothing reads to an examiner as searched and nothing found. It refuses an image record that carries no decoded address space, returning a refusal saying an examiner's patterns were not searched for in it, rather than a record of a scan that matched nothing. It refuses to scan a decode-failure record — which carries the same record type so an examiner sees it — and produces no record for it, because there is no address space behind it and a scan of nothing must not be reported as a scan of something. And where a space will not enumerate, it refuses to render that as a pass that was searched and held nothing: the pass is published as truncated with the sentence that this image's address space could not be enumerated, so it was not searched, and the reason the layer gave.

### `plugin.memory.windows`

**Reads.** It reads the `MemoryImage` record the container stage emits after decoding an acquisition format, recognised by that record's `type` field and never by a file name or extension, and re-wraps the decoded physical address space the record carries as a `MemoryLayer` rather than re-detecting the format for itself. From those bytes it discovers the three things a memory image has no header to state — the directory table base, the kernel's load address, and an ISF symbol table proved against the running kernel's own CodeView GUID and age — searching for symbols under `SEANCE_SYMBOL_DIRS`, `<exe dir>/symbols`, `./symbols` and `reference/volatility3/volatility3/symbols`, first hit winning. Beyond the image it reads only what the examiner names: `SEANCE_MEM_DTB` for a supplied directory table base, `SEANCE_MEM_TCPIP_ISF` for the `tcpip.sys` types the kernel's PDB does not hold, `SEANCE_PAGEFILES` and `SEANCE_CASE_PAGEFILES` for pagefiles under the index Windows assigned them, and a YARA rule set for the one stage that searches for something this product did not choose, and a file of physical offsets from the examiner's own run of `strings` for the one stage that asks which address spaces reach a frame. Nothing is discovered beside the capture: a pagefile lying next to a memory image is a second evidence item whose pages may predate the acquisition, so it is attached only when named, and a case reference is resolved inside the case the image belongs to. Everything downstream — thirty-six stages over processes, pool, drivers, network, services, registry hives, handles, VADs, objects, the cache manager's file pages, the kernel-side tamper checks, where each live user thread started (each `_ETHREAD`'s `StartAddress` and `Win32StartAddress` placed in its own process's VAD tree, with `MmProtectToValue`, the thread's `SystemThread` bit and, on x86, `MmSystemRangeStart` read from the kernel), and eight kernel-structure dumps — reads that one discovered profile rather than rediscovering anything. Those eight read: `KiProcessorBlock` to its first null or non-canonical slot and each `_KPCR` through the PRCB offset the symbols declare (`Prcb` on x64, `PrcbData` on x86), with `KeNumberProcessors` read for comparison and never preferred; `PoolBigPageTable` and `PoolBigPageTableSize`, every `_POOL_TRACKER_BIG_PAGES` slot up to 4,194,304, and `ExpPoolBigEntriesInUse`; `MiState.Vs.SystemVaRegions` with the declared length and the per-slice type map `Vs.SystemVaType`, the slice size derived from `MmSystemRangeStart` and the array length; `CmpHiveListHead` and each `_HHIVE`'s `GetCellRoutine` and `ReleaseCellRoutine`; every kernel module's and every process DLL's PE resource tree (directory 2 → `RT_VERSION` → first name → first language) for `VS_VERSIONINFO`, up to 32,768 images; every 512-byte-aligned sector of physical memory ending `55 AA`; the in-memory `SOFTWARE` hive's `TaskCache\Tasks` with each task's `Actions` and `DynamicInfo` values; the kernel module list for `truecrypt.sys` or `veracrypt.sys`, sweeping the region the virtual map types `MiVaNonPagedPool` for AES key schedules only when the driver is present (the region that holds most of the loader entries instead, when the typed one holds none of them: on Windows Server 2022 build 20348.587 the map types the region holding all of them `MiVaPagedPool`); and the private heap of every `conhost.exe` and `OpenConsole.exe` on the process list, swept on 8-byte boundaries for the console history vector.

**Produces.** It publishes a stage manifest naming all thirty-six stages in `STAGES` before any stage runs, so the case records what this build could have run even when none of it did, and then a `MemoryProfile` record stating how each discovered fact was established, its weakest evidence grade and whether the symbols were verified. Each stage then contributes its own record — image-wide for thirty-three of them, one record per process for `vad`, `dlls` and `handles` — and every record carries `stage_ran`, `content_complete`, and where a count is a floor rather than a total the `content_incomplete_reason` its own `incomplete` entries and the process inventory's give. A stage that could not run becomes a `MemoryStageFailure` of its own rather than a silence, because a stage that ran and found nothing and a stage that never ran are opposite findings. Per-process records carry the PID, the process name, and the `_EPROCESS` address in hex beside the number, since a JSON double rounds an x64 kernel pointer by up to a kilobyte. Where the `SYSTEM` and `SAM` hives are both resident it also emits one audited `MemoryCredential` record per recovered NT hash, LSA secret and cached domain logon, and files the cache manager still held whole are re-emitted as ordinary `FileEntry` artifacts stamped `recovered_from: "memory"` for the same parsers a disk image feeds. The eight kernel-structure records are `MemoryProcessorBlocks` (per processor: current, next and idle thread, whether it was idle, the current thread's process placed through the declared `Pcb` offset, GDT/IDT/TSS bases, `KdVersionBlock`, versions, core counts, and three self-checks — `Self`/`SelfPcr` back at the KPCR, `CurrentPrcb` at the embedded block, `_KPRCB.Number` equal to the slot — each reported as agree, disagree or not made, with the claimed processor count beside the walked one); `MemoryBigPool` (live, freed and never-used slots told apart by type from the `Va` low bit, exact per-tag totals whatever the 50,000-row publication cap, `PoolType` from `_POOL_TYPE` where declared or the raw `PoolFlags` bitfield where the build has that instead, and the in-use counter compared with the walk); `MemoryVirtualMap` (each region named from the kernel's own type map rather than its slot index, `type_uniform` per region, overlaps, and two cross-checks — the kernel base lies in an image region and `MmPfnDatabase` in the region typed `MiVaPfnDatabase` — and `SystemVaTypeCount` per type with its unit and each count's check against the type's `SystemVa.DynamicBitMap`); `MemoryHiveCellRoutines` (each hive's two routines placed against the shared module map and symbolicated inside the kernel image, exact or nearest-plus-offset flagged, and "outside every module" claimed only when the map is authoritative); `MemoryVersionInfo` (fixed info with its signature checked, `StringFileInfo` tables and `VarFileInfo` translations, with seven outcomes told apart: read, headers unreadable, not a PE, no resource directory, no `RT_VERSION`, resource unreadable, resource discarded because its section is `IMAGE_SCN_MEM_DISCARDABLE` — the kernel's own case on build 26200); `MemoryMbrScan` (each candidate decoded — disk signature, four entries with well-known type names — and held to six named checks with every outcome published, a GPT protective MBR recognised, boot code hashed with SHA-256 and not judged, and the bytes scanned, unread and unmapped stated); `MemoryScheduledTasks` (per task the `Actions` blob decoded — version 3; exec, COM handler, mail and message-box records, an unknown kind or an over-long string refused and reported — and `DynamicInfo` by length: creation, last run, state, last result, last successful run; `Triggers` decoded trigger by trigger — time with its schedule mode, boot, logon, idle, registration, session change, event with its XPath subscription, WNF — start, repetition and enabled flag, a localized start printed as wall-clock time and never as UTC, an unknown kind or a record running past the blob stopping the decode with the stop stated; a paged-out value reported as incomplete; up to 16,384 tasks); and `MemoryTrueCrypt` (the driver's presence from the module list, a partial list unable to clear the machine, and when present each verified key schedule's address, size and SHA-256 only — the key bytes never on the record — with adjacent AES-256 schedules reported as a possible XTS pair labelled an inference, and, where the driver's container (`CRYPTO_INFO`) has one of the layouts read from the VeraCrypt and TrueCrypt captures, its cipher id, mode id and which schedule is primary and which secondary); and `MemoryConsoleHistory` (per console host its pid, and per recognised history the client application name, the command limit, and each stored command in stored order with its length, a command whose characters would not read reported as unreadable and never dropped; the bytes swept split into not resident, paged out to a pagefile the evidence does not hold, and unreadable, with only the last two making the host incomplete; and the console clients on the list, so a client with no host is visible).

**Cannot.** It cannot report network endpoints at all on a modern build unless a lab supplies `tcpip.sys`'s own symbols: `_TCP_ENDPOINT`, `_TCP_LISTENER` and `_UDP_ENDPOINT` are not in `ntoskrnl`'s PDB, so the stage refuses by name and states the GUID and age of the pack that would unblock it. It cannot report a process's session id on Windows 11 24H2 and later: `_EPROCESS.Session` points at a `_PSP_SESSION_SPACE` no ISF declares, and it will not read a number at an offset nobody can check against the build, so the column is `not_declared` on every process with a session (125 of 129 on the build 26200 capture) and the process list states it once, with that count, under `undescribed`. That gap misses no process and no bytes, so it does not make the process inventory a floor, and the per-process records judge their completeness on their own work; a session whose layout is declared but whose bytes will not read still does. It is bounded rather than exhaustive: 65,536 processes, 65,536 timers, 262,144 threads walked for the thread groups, 4,096 processes assessed for the ETW patch, 512 unloaded-driver rows, 2,048 processor blocks, 4,194,304 big-pool slots walked and 50,000 published, 32,768 images for version info, 16,384 tasks with 256 actions and 64 KiB strings each, and no reconstruction larger than 256 MiB or containing a single gap is handed to a parser. Of the kernel-structure dumps: the virtual map reads nothing before Windows 10's `MiState` and publishes `SystemVaTypeCount` only in the unit its own dynamic bitmaps give (2 MiB on 26200) and only when no count falls below its bitmap, cannot check the non-paged pool's count, which has no bitmap, and has established that unit on one build; version info does not read a resource whose section is marked `IMAGE_SCN_MEM_DISCARDABLE` — deciding from the flag alone, without checking the bytes at the directory — nor one that is paged out, and says which; the scheduled-task stage decodes `Triggers` from a public description checked only on build 26200's 246 blobs, cannot say when a task fires whose trigger kind it does not know, and has not yet been graded task by task against the disk's task XML; the TrueCrypt stage never reads a volume and decodes the driver's key container (`CRYPTO_INFO`) from the layouts read from the captures (Windows 11 25H2, XTS; four layouts: VeraCrypt 1.26.29 with the schedules at +0x10 and the tweak keys 5,312 bytes on; 1.19, 1.21, 1.22, 1.23, 1.23-Hotfix-2, 1.24, 1.24-Hotfix1, 1.24-Update2, 1.24-Update4, 1.24-Update5, 1.24-Update6, 1.24-Update7, 1.25, 1.25.4, 1.25.7, 1.25.9, 1.26.7, 1.26.14, 1.26.15, 1.26.18, 1.26.20, 1.26.24 and 1.26.28 Beta4 at +0x0c and 5,304, of which 1.22, 1.23, 1.24-Update7 and 1.26.7 to 1.26.24 load a driver still named `truecrypt.sys` on the Windows 11 captures (fresh installs of 1.23-Hotfix-2, 1.24 to 1.24-Update6, 1.26.14, 1.26.18 and 1.26.28 Beta4 on Server 2019 and 2022 loaded `veracrypt.sys`), 1.26.7 to 1.26.28 Beta4 pair that layout with 1.26.29's cipher ids; 1.0f, 1.0f-1, 1.0f-2, 1.12, 1.13, 1.14, 1.16, 1.17 and 1.18 at +0x0c and 5,324, with TrueCrypt's ids to 1.17 and the later ids from 1.18; and VeraCrypt 1.0e and TrueCrypt 6.0, 6.0a, 6.1, 6.1a, 6.2, 6.2a, 6.3, 6.3a, 7.0, 7.0a, 7.1, 7.1a and 7.2 at +0x08 and 5,324, with TrueCrypt's own ids; each container says which layout it matched) and names only the ids those captures explain, so on any other version or cipher it states nothing about the cipher, the mode or which key is which, publishes an unexplained id raw, and leaves an adjacent AES-256 pair without a container as only a possible XTS pair; the sweep also recognises Serpent-256 schedules (the key is the schedule's first eight words, and the rest is recomputed and compared) and Twofish-256 schedules (the four S-box tables then the 40 subkeys, in VeraCrypt 1.21 and later; the 40 subkeys then the tables, in 1.19; and TrueCrypt's own order, which VeraCrypt 1.0e to 1.18 keep, with the key recovered from the subkeys by inverting the key schedule, then the whole structure recomputed and compared), Camellia-256 key tables (the key recovered from the three key-dependent subkey pairs, `ke1`-`ke6`, which are all that is checked of the table, stored as 32-bit word pairs in 1.21 and later and as 64-bit words in 1.18 and 1.19) and Kuznyechik round keys (the first 32 bytes are the key and all ten round keys are recomputed and compared), and decodes the containers of a Serpent volume, a Twofish volume, a Camellia volume, a Kuznyechik volume and the cascades AES-Twofish, AES-Twofish-Serpent, Serpent-AES, Serpent-Twofish-AES, Twofish-Serpent, Camellia-Kuznyechik, Kuznyechik-Twofish, Camellia-Serpent, Kuznyechik-AES and Kuznyechik-Serpent-Camellia with every layer's primary and tweak key hash, graded on one capture per version with those volumes mounted (every key of every volume, against headers decrypted on the host or known by construction; the drivers of VeraCrypt 1.0e, 1.13, 1.14, 1.16 and 1.17 refused a Camellia and a Kuznyechik volume, 1.18 mounted them, and no Camellia or Kuznyechik cascade was mounted on any version before 1.22), a container id naming a different cipher on each of the versions seen; TrueCrypt 6.0 to 7.2 are read (the container, with TrueCrypt's own algorithm ids 1 to 8, and the Twofish structure, which is laid out in another order than VeraCrypt 1.21's), graded on a capture per version with eight volumes mounted by the real driver; a TrueCrypt or VeraCrypt build not in the list above is not recognised; it sweeps only when the driver is listed, skips a hit whose key bytes cannot be re-read without counting it, cannot tell VeraCrypt's schedules from other AES-256 schedules in the pool, and its positive path has been graded on captures with `veracrypt.sys` loaded and AES, Serpent and cascade volumes mounted (every master key, known from its container header, was reported) on twenty-four VeraCrypt versions, thirteen TrueCrypt versions and one Windows 11 build and on no other; the console-history stage decodes one layout — a vector of MSVC wide strings followed by a command limit and the client's application name — derived in-house from the bytes of one capture in which the typed commands were known, on one build of the console host (Windows 11 26200.6584), so a host built differently yields nothing and nothing found is not evidence that nothing was typed; it finds hosts by image name only, does not read the screen buffer (what a command printed), does not report a line being edited, cannot see a history whose vector is empty, reports a stale copy in freed heap like a live one, and has not met `OpenConsole.exe`, whose host layout is assumed to match and is unverified; the big-pool stage reads `ExpPoolBigEntriesInUse`, which the ISF gives no type, as a 32-bit value on the record's own stated basis and compares it with the walk without ever preferring it; the region-naming-by-type-map property of the virtual map is pinned only by the release-only real-image test, since the unit fixture places types 2 and 3 in slots 2 and 3; and every one of the eight has been measured on exactly one build, 26200. It cannot analyse an ARM64 Windows capture: `seance_memory` now translates VMSAv8-64 descriptors — the valid bit, the type bit and the 48-bit output address under 4, 16 and 64 KiB granules and the TTBR0/TTBR1 regimes, refusing FEAT_LPA output-address bits (and LPA2 ones except under a recorded `TCR_EL1.DS = 1` with a 16 KiB granule, which is decoded), tagged pointers and reserved block encodings — but this tier drives none of it: an image whose header states arm64 is refused before discovery, and a headerless arm64 capture is swept with Intel rules that find no DTB, with nothing naming the architecture as the reason. It cannot read the skeleton key's stronger `CSystems` descriptor route on any build, because nobody publishes that structure's layout, and it cannot answer the system-call question at all on a 32-bit image, where the kernel is not entered by a `syscall` instruction. And it cannot show most of its kernel-side signals firing when something is wrong: `MEM-020` records that one of the seven tamper groups has met a known answer, and only as an observation — `orphan_kernel_threads` publishes the orphan system thread Ligh's write-up names on the Malware Cookbook's `tigger.vmem` (Tid 1648, start 0xf2edd150) but grades nothing on Windows XP, which declares no `_ETHREAD.StartAddressInvalid` — that the other six have never been seen produce a true positive, on any of the eight Cookbook captures or any other held here, and that no test-signed lab driver will be built to make one — and that on every Windows XP capture measured one `winlogon.exe` thread's own flag confirms `Dr7`-armed slots whose every address is in the null page, which `debugregisters` publishes with its addresses and does not grade: a breakpoint is graded only when at least one armed address is at or above 0x10000 (`MM_LOWEST_USER_ADDRESS`), so it cannot grade a breakpoint on memory a pre-Windows 8 32-bit process deliberately mapped at page 0 (a base of 1, or NTVDM). The legacy `KiTimerTableListHead` table has been read from real evidence only in its NT 5.1 form — bare `_LIST_ENTRY` buckets, on nine XP SP2 and SP3 captures, agreeing with Volatility 3 on every DPC timer once Volatility's own rows are reconciled (on `prolaco.vmem` it prints 55 against Séance's 50: four timers twice, and one bucket head, 0x80552408, read as a timer) — with its length derived from the bytes and bounded by the next symbol the build declares, a torn bucket head inside that bound (a timer relinked while the image was taken, 12 of 256 on `prolaco.vmem`) counted as a bucket only when a well-formed head follows it and named rather than read as the end of the table, a torn run that no well-formed head follows named as not walked and not counted, so it cannot say whether those heads were buckets, and without a symbol bound a torn head still ends it — and on a Server 2003 RTM capture of the same bare form; the form with a declared `_KTIMER_TABLE_ENTRY` has been read from a Server 2008 SP1 x86 PAE capture and a Vista SP2 x86 non-PAE capture: 512 buckets, equal to the image's own `KiTimerTableSize`, which is the extent whenever the build declares that variable and the image holds a power of two that fits the room the next symbol leaves (a capture taken while the system ran, with 56 torn heads, would otherwise end the derived extent at 353 of 512); an item reached from the table is a timer only if its dispatcher header's type is 8 or 9, so a torn list that runs into other memory publishes no junk row. On the Server 2008 capture the 14 timers Volatility 3 prints are those Séance reaches from buckets 0 to 255 (Volatility 3 reads only those 256), the further 41 from buckets 256 to 511 being pinned and not graded; on the Vista capture all 51 timers Volatility 2 prints are reached with the same routine and period, and one more is pinned and not graded (`MEM-XP-4`, `MEM-XP-5`). It has not been read on Server 2003 SP1+ or XP x64 (`MEM-021`, `MEM-059`). On an x64 build that declares `KiWaitNever` and `KiWaitAlways` a timer's `Dpc` field is decoded with them and the timer's address and must land on a structure whose `Type` is one of the build's `_KOBJECTS` DPC values; a field that does not is published as unreadable with the reason, and nothing is said about where that timer would call — so it cannot see a DPC on a key-declaring build that lacks `_KDPC.Type` or those constants (54 of 3,015 kernel ISFs). A timer with the shape of PatchGuard's own — a `_KTIMER` not aligned to the pointer width, a routine in no loaded module on a complete list and a non-canonical `DeferredContext`, all three — is published with `patchguard_shaped` and counted apart, and is not graded (its routine is still offered to the unloaded-driver cross-reference); that is a shape and not an identification, so it cannot tell PatchGuard's timer from a rootkit that imitates all three conditions, and no capture held has a timer rootkit to test that against. A timer reached from more than one bucket list is reported once with every place it was reached, and its counts are of distinct timers; a list that leads into another bucket's head stops there, and a repeated `_KPRCB` pointer is walked once. Where neither of those shows why a timer was reached twice it says the reason is not established, and on the modern captures held most such timers say so (`MEM-057`). Where a build declares `ActiveDR7`, only that bit confirms a thread's debug registers, and a confirmed thread with Tid 0 or a non-canonical armed address is published and not graded. The suspicious-thread stage (`MemorySuspiciousThreads`) cannot attribute a user-mode start address that falls in no VAD, nor an x64 one in the non-canonical hole — it counts it and marks the process incomplete — and cannot judge a kernel-mode start. On a thread whose `SystemThread` bit is set that start is counted apart (whether it lies in a loaded module is the orphan-thread group's question); on a thread whose bit is clear, unreadable or not declared no stage judges it, the orphan-thread group setting such threads aside as user threads, so it is counted and the process is marked incomplete — 76 of the 78 kernel starts on the build-26200 capture, which is therefore reported incomplete. It does not judge a process whose VAD tree holds fewer than five ranges, and sets aside unjudged every process whose Peb is null, which includes a WSL1 pico process that has user threads. It cannot tell a JIT's or any other legitimate private executable code from injected code: a start in a private range is a place to look, not a verdict. It has been measured on four captures only — the clean build-26200 capture (123 processes judged, no finding, 2 kernel starts on kernel threads) and three Windows XP captures with Volatility 3's `suspicious_threads` as the oracle (be2 1, zeus 10, stuxnet 9 findings, every one also a Volatility row) — and no published answer names an injected user thread on any of them, so none is graded against ground truth.

**Refuses.** It refuses to touch any `ParsedRecord` that is not a `MemoryImage`, and any image record whose container stage reported `decode_failed`, producing nothing at all rather than a second opinion on a format it did not decode; an image record carrying no decoded address space, or a `backed_ranges` geometry that will not parse in full, is an error rather than a wider coverage claim. It refuses to run at all on an image whose layer metadata states a non-Intel architecture — an ARM64-stamped crash dump is refused as `UnsupportedArchitecture` before any directory-table-base sweep, naming the tool's limit rather than reporting "no DTB", and the sweep's self-reference rules return nothing under an ARM64 paging mode rather than borrowing Intel's. It refuses to run at all when `SEANCE_MEM_DTB` names something that is not a physical address, emitting only the stage manifest and a discovery-failure record, because an examiner who named an address space and silently got the swept one would read a profile of a machine they did not ask for. It refuses to fall back to the kernel's symbol table when a named `SEANCE_MEM_TCPIP_ISF` will not compile, since the resulting refusal would send the examiner to fetch a pack they already have while the real fault went unnamed. It refuses to attach two pagefiles under one index, or to resolve a case-held pagefile reference to a path on the host, because either would answer a page fault from another file's bytes with nothing in the case saying so. It refuses to hand a part-recovered cached file to a parser, since a parser given a database full of holes produces records indistinguishable from real ones, it refuses to put a recovered AES key's bytes on any record, publishing only their hash, it refuses to judge a Windows XP or Server 2003 thread's `Win32StartAddress` when that thread's `LpcReceivedMsgIdValid` bit says the field holds an LPC message id (Volatility 3 reports those small integers as threads started in private memory), or at all when that bit cannot be read, and it refuses to run the pattern scan with no rule named — reporting the stage as not having run, with that reason, rather than an empty match list that reads identically to a scan which had a rule and found nothing.

### `plugin.messaging.android_sms`

**Reads.** The Android telephony provider store, `mmssms.db`, selected loosely by name and strictly by schema. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `SystemArtifact` with `InputCapability::Stream`, lower-cases the artifact's `name` and opens any file whose name ends `mmssms.db` or contains `mmssms`, so a renamed or path-prefixed copy is still tried. A directory entry yields nothing. An artifact with no data source is not opened at all and leaves an identification record. A source whose first 16 bytes did not all arrive is a short read of this tool's, never a finding about the file: it yields only the stager's `SqliteSpillIncomplete` record (`content_incomplete_reason: short_read`) where the source declared more than arrived (the shared gate `stage_named_store`, ROADMAP §5.11). Otherwise the whole file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 2 GiB cap (`MAX_DB_BYTES`) with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one; the staged copy's first 16 bytes must be `SQLite format 3\0` or the file is passed over in silence as not this database. The copy is opened read-only and the authoritative claim is made through the catalogue: `probe_table` must list a table or view named `sms` — WhatsApp's `msgstore.db` and iMessage's `chat.db` have none — and a catalogue that will not answer is an error, not an absence. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the connection and compared with the validated window `57..=67`, both endpoints read from real stores: 57 from plaso's `test_data/mmssms.db` and 67 from the Magnet 2022 CTF Pixel 3 `com.android.providers.telephony/databases/mmssms.db`. Every table is read through a `FieldMap` resolved against `PRAGMA table_info`, each logical field from a single candidate name: `sms` (`_id`, `thread_id`, `address`, `date`, `read`, `status`, `type`, `body`, `subject`), `pdu` (`_id`, `thread_id`, `date`, `msg_box`, `read`, `sub`, `st`), `part` (`mid`, `ct`, `text`, `name`, `cl`, `fn`), `addr` (`msg_id`, `address`, `type`), `threads` (`_id`, `recipient_ids`) and `canonical_addresses` (`_id`, `address`); a column list that will not read is an error for the whole parse, not an empty map. Correspondents are resolved by joining `threads.recipient_ids` (space-separated canonical ids) to `canonical_addresses.address`, when both tables exist. `sms` is walked `ORDER BY <date> DESC` and, when `pdu` exists, so is `pdu`, after `part` rows (`text/plain` parts concatenated with newlines into the body, every other non-`application/smil` part contributing an attachment label from `name`, else `cl`, else `fn`, else the content type) and `addr` rows (type 137 the `from` address, type 151 the `to` addresses, `insert-address-token` and empty addresses skipped) have been loaded whole. Every timestamp's unit is judged by magnitude through the shared band table: at or above 10^15 microseconds, at or above 10^12 milliseconds, otherwise seconds. The walk stops at 50,000 records (`MAX_MESSAGE_ENTRIES`) across SMS and MMS together.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per `sms` row and per `pdu` row, both `type: "AndroidSms"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `service: "SMS"` or `"MMS"`, with `rowid`, `thread_id`, `contact`, `chat_identifier` and `chat_display_name` (the row's `address`, else the thread's resolved recipient addresses joined by `, `, else the thread id as text with `Thread <id>` as the display name, else `unknown`), `text` (the SMS `body` as stored, or the concatenated `text/plain` MMS parts), `subject` when non-empty, `read` as a boolean, `status` (`sms.status` or `pdu.st`) as stored, and the direction pair only when the store's code is one the platform defines: for SMS `type` 1 is `received` (`is_from_me: false`), 2 `sent`, 3 `draft`, 4 `outbox`, 5 `failed`, 6 `queued` (all five with `is_from_me: true` — authored by the device owner, but only `sent` was delivered); for MMS `msg_box` 1 `received`, 2 `sent`, 3 `draft`, 4 `outbox`; the raw code is always written back as `sms_type` or `msg_box`, NULL included. An MMS record also carries `has_attachments` (a genuine `true`/`false`), `attachment_names` when any, and `peer_undetermined: true` when the direction that selects the `addr` row could not be read — the peer is the type-137 address on a received PDU and the first type-151 address on an outgoing one, never the owner's own `from` row. `date` is whole Unix seconds with `date_rfc3339` beside it; a column holding 0 or a negative value writes neither and instead `date_unusable: true` with `date_raw`, and a NULL column writes nothing at all. The `name` is `<direction or "message">: <contact> — <first 80 characters, or "(no text)" / "(MMS attachment)">`. Between the records and the summary sit the schema findings, all `type: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `app: "android-sms"`: `SchemaOutsideValidated` (the shared `StaleWarning` marker with `seen_schema_version`, `supported_range: "57..=67"`, `message`, `detail` and `name`; a disclosure with no incompleteness claim) when the version is outside the window and the rows still parse; `SchemaVersionUndetermined` with the pair `content_incomplete: true` / `content_incomplete_reason: unresolved_structure` when the pragma would not read — never spent as in range; `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` with no incompleteness pair when `PRAGMA user_version` is 0, the parse being unranked rather than stale — each of the three carrying `validated_against` naming plaso's `mmssms.db` (57) and the Magnet 2022 Pixel 3 `mmssms.db` (67); and one `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` per table (`source_table`, `unresolved_fields` naming the logical fields, `records_recovered`, `content_incomplete` pair with reason `unresolved_structure`) whenever any of that table's fields had no column — the rows are still walked with the field omitted, never guessed. Then one `AndroidSmsSummary` (`subtype: "summary"`) with `message_count`, `thread_count`, `sms_count`, `mms_count`, `file_name`, and, at the cap, `truncated: true`, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `cap_reached`, `max_entries` as the budget the walk actually ran under, and a sentence saying the oldest messages were not extracted; where any `sms`, `pdu`, `part`, `addr`, `threads` or `canonical_addresses` row would not decode, `rows_dropped`, `inventory_incomplete: true` and `content_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` (a cap's reason is not overwritten). An artifact with no data source yields one `AndroidSms` record with `status: "Identified"` and no messages; a file carrying the SQLite header that would not open, whose catalogue would not read, whose column list would not read, or whose `sms`/`pdu` query would not prepare or run yields one `AndroidSms` record with `status: "ParseFailed"`, the error, and both incompleteness pairs under `unresolved_structure`. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event of its own.

**Cannot.** It cannot see past the fiftieth thousand message: both walks are newest-first, so the cap drops the oldest, and the summary says so with the pair. It cannot name a contact beyond a number: the telephony store holds addresses, not the address book, and nothing here joins to `contacts2.db`. It cannot say who a group MMS went to beyond the first `to` address, and cannot attribute an MMS whose `msg_box` is NULL or undefined to either party — it says `peer_undetermined` and falls back to the thread's addresses. It recovers an MMS attachment's label and nothing else: the `part._data` path is not read, the bytes are not carried, and a part row with no `mid` is skipped uncounted. It cannot tell a schema of version 68 from one of 67 except by the number: a store outside `57..=67` is parsed on the assumption its columns mean what they meant, with the `SchemaOutsideValidated` finding beside the rows, and the candidate list holds exactly one physical name per field, so any rename is an unresolved field until a candidate is added. A `PRAGMA user_version` of 0 is not compared to anything. The `threads`/`canonical_addresses` join is best effort: a `recipient_ids` token that is not an integer, or a canonical id with no row, silently thins the address list, and a thread with no resolvable address is named by its number. A `sms.status` or `pdu.st` value is passed through as an integer with no decoding. Third-party SMS apps' own stores, the `words` and `sr_pending` tables, drafts held elsewhere, RCS (`bugle_db`) and the carrier's own MMS notification indications are not read. It has never been validated on a store whose `type`/`msg_box` codes differ from AOSP's, and reads any code other than the six / four it knows as no direction. It recovers no deleted rows. The 2 GiB spill cap is applied to the file and a larger one is staged as a prefix and stamped `cap_reached`.

**Refuses.** It refuses to file a corrupt telephony store as a phone that exchanged no messages: a catalogue that will not answer, a column list that will not read, and a query that will not prepare or run all reach the `ParseFailed` record carrying both incompleteness pairs, and only a file with no SQLite header, or a readable catalogue with no `sms` table, is passed over in silence. It refuses to assert a direction the store did not record: a NULL or undefined `type`/`msg_box` writes neither `direction` nor `is_from_me`, because an absent key is what the viewers render as "not determinable" while a literal `"unknown"` string rendered as received. It refuses to label a draft, outbox, failed or queued message `sent`. It refuses to use an outgoing PDU's `from` row as the correspondent, since that row is the device owner. It refuses to place an unset or negative date at the epoch or in the 1960s, keeping the raw value under `date_unusable`/`date_raw` where no consumer can read it as a time, and refuses to write a `1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00` string beside an omitted `date`. It refuses to read a 16-digit microsecond value as milliseconds — the local two-branch normaliser that dated a message to the year 55840 is gone. It refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as "older than 57", and refuses to spend a pragma that would not read as in range. It refuses to substitute a guess for a column no candidate matched: the field is omitted and named on a `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` finding with the count of records that lack it. It refuses to let a dropped row vanish: every undecodable `sms`, `pdu`, `part`, `addr`, `threads` or `canonical_addresses` row is counted into `rows_dropped` on the summary with the `inventory_incomplete` pair. And it refuses to report the module constant as the cap when a caller supplied its own — `max_entries` is the budget the walk actually ran under.

### `plugin.messaging.fb_messenger`

**Reads.** Facebook Messenger's message stores in three shapes, selected by basename and by nothing else. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the artifact's `name`, takes the part after the last `/`, and recognises exactly `threads_db2` (the legacy Android store), any `lightspeed-*.db` or `msys*.db` (the newer msys/lightspeed store, Android or iOS, decrypted), and `lightspeed-*.db.enc` (the iOS store encrypted at rest); a directory entry yields nothing. An encrypted-suffix name is answered from the filename alone, before any read. For the other two the shared gate `stage_sqlite_db` skips an artifact with no data source, reads the first 16 bytes with a looping `read_full`, and where they are `SQLite format 3\0` spills the file under the shared 512 MiB `MAX_DB_BYTES` cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one; a full 16-byte header that is not SQLite's is taken as an encrypted msys store only for the msys shape (a non-SQLite `threads_db2` yields nothing), and fewer than 16 bytes delivered yields nothing. The copy is opened read-only; `probe_catalogue` must answer; `probe_table` asks for `messages` (an absent table in a readable catalogue yields nothing); `probe_columns` reads its column list. Four logical fields are resolved by `FieldMap::resolve`, candidates in preference order: `text`; `timestamp` from `timestamp_ms` then `timestamp`; `thread` from `thread_key` then `thread_id`; `sender` from `sender` (a JSON object carrying `user_key` and `name`) then `sender_id` (a bare id). Which of those two resolved decides the shape: with `sender_id` a `contacts` table, when present, is read through its own map (`id` from `id` or `contact_id`; `name` from `name`, `display_name` or `normalized_name_for_search`) into an id-to-name map, and only when both fields resolved. The walk is one statement `SELECT rowid, <thread>, <sender>, <text>, <timestamp> FROM messages ORDER BY <timestamp>` with every unresolved field the literal `NULL` and no row limit; `thread` and `sender` are read as text with an integer coerced to decimal, the timestamp as an integer with a numeric string parsed, and it is divided by 1,000 unconditionally as milliseconds. No schema-version window is declared (`facebook-messenger`): no real `threads_db2`, `msys_database_*.db` or `lightspeed-*.db` has been observed on any corpus this parser was run against, and `PRAGMA user_version` is not read.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per `messages` row through the shared `ChatMessage` shell: `type: "FacebookMessenger"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `service: "Facebook Messenger"`, `platform: "Android"` for `threads_db2` and the literal `"msys/lightspeed"` for the newer store, `text` (omitted when empty), `date` in whole Unix seconds (omitted when 0 or negative), `contact` as the sender's name — from the `sender` JSON's `name`, or the `contacts` row for a `sender_id` — else the sender key, `chat_identifier` as the thread key, `rowid`, `sender_key` (the JSON's `user_key` or the raw `sender_id`) when known, and a `name` of `message: <contact> — <first 80 characters or "(no text)">`. `is_from_me` and `direction` are never written: neither schema carries a per-row direction flag this parser reads and the owning account is not established. After the rows, in this order: a `FacebookMessengerIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker (`subtype: parse_incomplete`, `source_table: "messages"`, `rows_dropped`, `records_recovered`, `first_error`, both incompleteness pairs with reason `unresolved_structure`) when the engine refused to step a row; a `FacebookMessengerContactIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker when a `contacts` row would not decode, with `records_recovered` the number of names loaded; then `type: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `status: "SchemaFieldsUnresolved"`, `app: "facebook-messenger"` findings — one for `messages` naming in `unresolved_fields` any of `text`, `timestamp`, `thread`, `sender` that no column carried, with `records_recovered` and the `content_incomplete` pair under `unresolved_structure` (the rows are still walked with the field omitted), and one for `contacts` when that table is present and either of its fields did not resolve (in which case no name is resolved and messages are attributed by id). When the `contacts` lookup could not be made the messages are still walked, attributed by id, beside one `FacebookMessengerContactIncomplete` record: `StoreUnreadable` when the table could not be looked for or its column list would not read, `DatabaseUnreadable` (`source_table: "contacts"`, SQLite's message as `sqlite_error`, both pairs, `records_recovered: 0`) when its query would not prepare or run. An absent `contacts` table carries no record. A `lightspeed-*.db.enc`, or an msys-shaped file whose full header is not SQLite's, yields one `EncryptedMessengerDatabase` record (`subtype: "encrypted_database"`, `app: "Facebook Messenger"`, `status: "Encrypted"`, `encryption: "iOS Data Protection (per-file key in the keychain)"`, a `note` saying the file must be decrypted and re-ingested, `store: "msys/lightspeed"`, `name: "Facebook Messenger store (encrypted): <name>"`). A store that would not open, whose catalogue would not read, whose `messages` table could not be looked for, or whose column list would not read yields one `FacebookMessengerIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` marker (both pairs, reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`); a file carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged yields the same marker naming the I/O error. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event, thread, participant, reaction or attachment record is produced.

**Cannot.** It has never been run against a real Messenger store: no `threads_db2`, `msys_database_*.db` or `lightspeed-*.db` has been observed on any corpus this project holds, so the column candidates are the parser's reading of documented schemas, no schema-version window exists, `PRAGMA user_version` is not even read, and every drift finding is by field alone. It cannot say who sent a message relative to the device owner — no direction is ever written — nor, on the msys shape, name a sender when `contacts` is absent, has a column it does not know, or holds no row for the id: the record then carries the bare numeric key as `contact`. It cannot decrypt an iOS `.db.enc` store or name its per-file key, and it labels a non-SQLite msys file `iOS Data Protection` whether or not that is the cause — a corrupt copy on Android receives the same record. It reads every timestamp as milliseconds unconditionally, so a store holding seconds would place every message in January 1970. Its `platform` for the newer store is the literal string `msys/lightspeed`, not `Android` or `iOS`, because the same schema is used on both and the file path is not consulted. It does not read `msg_type`, `threads`, `thread_participants`, `attachments`, `reactions`, `messages_v2` or any msys table other than `messages` and `contacts`, so media, stickers, calls, reactions and thread names are not recovered and a non-text message is a row with no body. It has no row cap and no `CapCounter`. Where `conn.prepare` or `query_map` fails on a store whose `messages` table and columns were already established it yields one `FacebookMessengerIncomplete` record with `status: DatabaseUnreadable`, `source_table: "messages"`, SQLite's message as `sqlite_error` and both incompleteness pairs (reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`) beside any column-drift finding, never an empty list (pinned by `a_messages_table_whose_query_will_not_run_is_reported_unreadable_not_empty`). It recovers no deleted rows and reads no `-journal` sibling.

**Refuses.** It refuses to spend a short read as an encryption finding — a four-byte file once produced an `EncryptedMessengerDatabase` record asserting an encrypted Messenger store was on the device — so only a full 16-byte non-SQLite header on an msys-shaped file reaches that record, and the two answers are separate variants a caller cannot spend as one another. It refuses to answer "no messages" from a read error: a store that will not open, a catalogue that will not answer, a `messages` lookup that will not run and a column list that will not read each produce `StoreUnreadable`, never silence. It refuses to let a renamed `text` or timestamp end the walk with an empty list: the rows are read for what resolves and the finding names the field. It refuses to infer direction from the sender key, and refuses to invent a name for an id `contacts` does not hold. It refuses to declare a schema-version window nobody has read from a real file. It refuses to place an unset timestamp at the epoch, and refuses to write an empty `text`, `contact` or `chat_identifier`. It refuses to count a lost `contacts` row as a sender with no name, tallying it under `FacebookMessengerContactIncomplete` instead. It refuses to drop an encrypted store from the case file: `lightspeed-*.db.enc` is recorded as present and what would open it, rather than nothing. And it refuses to file any marker under the message type `FacebookMessenger`, because `seance_db` groups conversations on that key.

### `plugin.messaging.instagram`

**Reads.** Instagram's Android Direct store, selected by file name and by nothing else: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the artifact's `name`, takes the part after the last `/` and acts only on exactly `direct.db`; the path is never consulted, so it fires the same on a raw file system or an extracted backup. Everything after that gate is the shared entry path `seance_sqlite_util::process_named_sqlite_db`: a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing; the first 16 bytes are read with a looping `read_full`; fewer than 16 bytes, or 16 bytes that are not `SQLite format 3\0`, yield nothing and no record; a file carrying the header is spilled to a temporary copy under the shared 512 MiB `MAX_DB_BYTES` cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one. The copy is opened read-only; `probe_catalogue` must answer; `probe_table` asks for `messages`; `probe_columns` reads its column list. Six logical fields are resolved by `FieldMap::resolve`, each from one candidate: `sent_at` from `timestamp`, `text`, `account` from `user_id`, `thread` from `thread_id`, `message_json` from `message`, `message_type`; `message_id` is used when present, else `rowid`. The candidate names were checked once against the `messages` table of a Hickman Android 14 image (`_id`, `user_id`, `thread_id`, a string `message_type`, direction inside the `message` JSON as `is_sent_by_viewer`, microsecond timestamps), but that image is not on disk and no `PRAGMA user_version` was ever read from a real store, so the declared bound `instagram-android` is `Unranged`. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the open connection, 0 meaning "not recorded". The walk is one statement, `SELECT <id>, <sent_at>, <text>, <account>, <thread>, <message_json>, <message_type> FROM messages ORDER BY <sent_at>`, every unresolved field the literal `NULL`, with no row limit; every text column is read as TEXT and, failing that, as a BLOB decoded as lossy UTF-8, because real installs store the `message` JSON as a BLOB. The `message` column is parsed as JSON; `is_sent_by_viewer` is taken from it as a boolean, and where the row has no `text` a media URL is looked for under `url`, `media_url`, `playable_url`, `media.url`, `media.media_url` or `media.image_versions2.candidates[0].url`. The timestamp's unit is judged by magnitude — at or above 10^15 microseconds, at or above 10^12 milliseconds, otherwise seconds. The iOS store (`DirectSQLiteDatabase/<userid>.db`, bodies as `NSKeyedArchiver` blobs) is deliberately not selected, and `threads` is not read.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per `messages` row through the shared `ChatMessage` shell: `type: "Instagram"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `service: "Instagram Direct"`, `platform: "Android"`, `text` when the row's `text` column was non-empty, `date` in whole Unix seconds (omitted when 0 or negative), `is_from_me` and its derived `direction` only when the JSON carried a boolean `is_sent_by_viewer`, `chat_identifier` and `thread_id` both the thread id, `source_table: "messages"`, `message_id`, `account_user_id` (the owning account's `user_id`), `message_type` as the store's string, `media_url` when a URL was found in the JSON of a row with no text, `has_attachments` as a genuine `true`/`false` on every row (true exactly when a `media_url` was found), and a `name` of `<direction or "message">: <first 60 characters of the text, else the media URL, else the message type, else "message">`. No `contact` is ever written: the table names no counterparty. After the rows, in this order: an `InstagramIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker (`subtype: parse_incomplete`, `source_table: "messages"`, `rows_dropped`, `records_recovered`, `first_error`, both incompleteness pairs with reason `unresolved_structure`) when the engine refused to step a row; then the schema notes `assess` entitles the parse to, each of `type: "InstagramIncomplete"` with `warning_class: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `app: "instagram-android"`, `store: "direct.db"`, `table: "messages"`, `schema_version_locator: "PRAGMA user_version"`, the version as `schema_version_seen` / `schema_version_not_recorded: true` / `schema_version_undetermined`, `schema_unranged_reason`, `records_recovered`, `detail` and `name`, and never `schema_version_supported`. Every readable store carries one disclosure note (`subtype: "parser_stale"`, no incompleteness pair): `SchemaNotRanged` with the version seen "compared against nothing", or `SchemaVersionUndetermined` when the pragma would not read. Incompleteness is claimed (`subtype: "parser_stale"`, both pairs, reason `unvalidated`) by `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` when any of `sent_at`, `text`, `thread`, `message_json` has no column — all four missing yields the note alone, no rows — and by `SchemaTableAbsent` when the catalogue read and `messages` was not in it; `SchemaOptionalFieldsUnresolved` (disclosure) names `account` or `message_type` when only those failed. A `direct.db` that would not open, whose catalogue would not read, whose table could not be looked for, or whose column list would not read yields one `InstagramIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` marker (both pairs, reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`); one carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged yields the same marker naming the I/O error. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event, no thread, participant or media record is produced.

**Cannot.** It has never read a real Instagram Direct database on this tree: the column names were confirmed on a Hickman Android 14 image that is no longer on disk, no version was read from it, and no `direct.db` exists in `test_data/`, `reference/`, `~/forensic_corpora` or `~/ctf-evidence` , so every readable store carries a `SchemaNotRanged` note and `PRAGMA user_version` is compared to nothing. It cannot name a counterparty: `threads` is never read, `recipient_ids` is not selected, and the record carries the thread id and the owning account only, so a Conversations view groups by thread and shows no participant. It cannot read the iOS store at all — the archived bodies are not decoded, so `<userid>.db` is not selected and leaves no record. It recovers a media message's URL and nothing else: no bytes, no caption, no thumbnail, and only from the six JSON paths it tries, so a media message whose JSON nests differently is a row with `has_attachments: false` and a name of its type. Its direction is only as good as the JSON: a row whose `message` blob will not parse, or carries no `is_sent_by_viewer`, has no direction, and a row whose text lives only inside that JSON (a share, a reaction, a story reply) has no `text`. A `text` or `message` column that is a BLOB of non-UTF-8 bytes is decoded lossily with replacement characters and nothing on the record says so. It has no row cap and no `CapCounter`. Where `conn.prepare` or `query_map` fails on a store whose table and columns were already established it yields one `InstagramIncomplete` record with `status: DatabaseUnreadable`, `source_table: "messages"`, SQLite's message as `sqlite_error` and both incompleteness pairs (reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`) beside the schema note, never an empty list (pinned by `a_messages_query_that_will_not_run_is_reported_unreadable_not_empty`). It recovers no deleted rows and reads no `-journal` sibling.

**Refuses.** It refuses to answer "no messages" from a read error: a store that will not open, a catalogue that will not answer, a `messages` lookup that will not run and a column list that will not read each produce `StoreUnreadable`, and an absent `messages` table in a catalogue that read produces `SchemaTableAbsent`, never silence. It refuses to let a renamed column read as an empty account: a `messages` whose `timestamp`, `text`, `thread_id` or `message` no longer resolves is walked for what resolves and the note names the logical fields with both incompleteness pairs, and a table with none of the four yields the note alone with no manufactured row. It refuses to declare a schema range it did not read from a real file, and refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as version 0 or an unreadable pragma as in range. It refuses to assert direction where the JSON did not record it, leaving `is_from_me` and `direction` absent rather than writing a null a consumer could read as received. It refuses to read a 16-digit microsecond timestamp as milliseconds — the two-branch normaliser that placed messages in the year 55840 is replaced by the shared three-band one — and refuses to place an unset timestamp at the epoch. It refuses to write an empty `text`: a media message's body is absent, with its URL and a genuine `has_attachments: false` where none was found, rather than a message that said nothing. And it refuses to select the iOS store it cannot decode, rather than emit records with no text.

### `plugin.messaging.kik`

**Reads.** Kik for Android's message store, selected by name: the artifact's `name`, lower-cased and taken after the last `/`, must be exactly `kikdatabase.db`. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess` and then runs the shared `process_named_sqlite_db` gate — directory or no data source yields nothing, a looping 16-byte header read, nothing for fewer than 16 bytes or for bytes that are not `SQLite format 3\0`, and a spill of the database with its `-wal` sibling under the 512 MiB `MAX_DB_BYTES` cap. On the staged copy, opened read-only: `probe_catalogue` must answer, `probe_table` looks for a table or view named `messagesTable`, `probe_columns` reads its columns, and `FieldMap::resolve` binds five logical fields — `id` from `_id`, `text` from `body`, `sent_at` from `timestamp`, `partner` from `partner_jid`, `from_me` from `was_me` — each with exactly one candidate name. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the connection with 0 as "not recorded". A second statement, `SELECT jid, display_name FROM KIKcontactsTable WHERE jid IS NOT NULL`, is run to build a JID-to-display-name map, after `probe_table` found the table and `probe_columns` listed it; an absent table leaves the map empty with no record, because that is a store shape. The message walk is `SELECT <id>, <text>, <sent_at>, <partner>, <from_me> FROM messagesTable ORDER BY <sent_at or id>`, unresolved fields as the literal `NULL`, with no `LIMIT`.

**Produces.** One `ChatMessage`-shaped `ParsedRecord` per `messagesTable` row: `type: "Kik"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `platform: "Android"`, `service: "Kik"`, `text` (empty omitted), `date` as whole Unix seconds from `timestamp` read as milliseconds (`div_euclid(1000)`, zero or negative omitted), `is_from_me`/`direction` only when `was_me` held a value (1 is sent, anything else received), `chat_identifier` set to the partner JID, `contact` set to the display name `KIKcontactsTable` gave that JID or, failing that, the JID itself, the raw `rowid`, and the derived `name` `<direction or "message">: <contact> — <preview or "(no text)">`. Then, in order: a `KikIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker if any message row would not decode; a `KikContactIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker against `KIKcontactsTable` if any contact row would not decode (its `records_recovered` is the number of names mapped); one `KikContactIncomplete` record when the contacts lookup could not be made — `StoreUnreadable` when `KIKcontactsTable` could not be looked for or its column list would not read, `DatabaseUnreadable` (`source_table: "KIKcontactsTable"`, SQLite's message as `sqlite_error`, both pairs, `records_recovered: 0`) when its query would not prepare or run, a renamed `display_name` included; and exactly one schema-support record per parsed store, `type: "KikIncomplete"`, `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `warning_class: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `app: "kik-android"`, `source_table: "messagesTable"`, `schema_version_locator: "user_version"`, the version as seen (`schema_version_seen`/`schema_version_recorded: true`), as absent (`schema_version_recorded: false`) or as unreadable (`schema_version_detail`), and `status: SchemaNotRanged` on every readable store because `SCHEMA_SUPPORT` is `Unranged` with the reason "no reference database of this app is held by this project" — the record never carries `schema_version_supported`. That record claims `content_incomplete`/`inventory_incomplete` (reason `unvalidated`, `schema_unresolved_fields`) only when `text` or `sent_at` did not resolve, with `status: SchemaFieldsUnresolved`. Staging shortfalls are stamped by `TempDb::stamp_incompleteness` (`content_incomplete_reason` `cap_reached`/`short_read`, `wal_incomplete_reason`) onto every record with one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker. A named store that would not open, whose catalogue would not read, whose `messagesTable` could not be looked for or whose columns would not list yields exactly one `KikIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` marker with both incompleteness pairs; a header-bearing file that would not stage yields the same from the shared gate. No timeline event is emitted here.

**Cannot.** It has never been run against a real Kik Android store. The one real Kik database in reach, `reference/plaso/test_data/kik_ios.sqlite`, is an iOS Core Data store (`ZKIKMESSAGE`, `PRAGMA user_version` 0, model version in `Z_METADATA`) and is not the schema this parser reads, so `SCHEMA_SUPPORT` is `Unranged`, every store reads `SchemaNotRanged`, and each column name in the candidate lists is a single reading of the documented Android schema with no second candidate to absorb a rename. It cannot tell a group chat from a one-to-one: the partner JID is used as the thread key whatever it names, and no group table is read. It cannot name a sender inside a group, only the partner. It reads `timestamp` as milliseconds without checking magnitude, so a store holding seconds dates every message to 1970 with nothing on the record saying so. It has no row cap, so a large table is walked whole into memory. It cannot recover attachments, media, or deleted rows. The contact names are read from `jid` and `display_name` only, with no second candidate: a store that renamed either shows every sender as the bare JID, and the `KikContactIncomplete` `DatabaseUnreadable` record names SQLite's error. When the message query itself fails, the contact-lookup record is not emitted beside it. A message query that fails at `prepare` or `query_map` after the table and columns were established yields one `KikIncomplete` record with `status: DatabaseUnreadable`, `source_table: "messagesTable"`, SQLite's message as `sqlite_error` and both incompleteness pairs (reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`) beside the schema-support record, never an empty list (pinned by `a_messages_table_whose_query_will_not_run_is_reported_unreadable_not_empty`).

**Refuses.** It refuses to walk a store in which neither `text` nor `sent_at` resolved, emitting instead the schema-support record with `status: SchemaFieldsUnresolved` and `records_recovered: 0`, because a message with neither body nor time is not one. It refuses to return nothing for a store it identified and could not read: a failed open, an unanswering catalogue, an undeterminable `messagesTable` lookup and an unreadable column list each become a `StoreUnreadable` marker with the engine's reason; only a catalogue that answered and held no `messagesTable` is silence, because that is what "not a Kik message schema" looks like. It refuses to treat a renamed `body` or `timestamp` as an empty result — the pre-adoption shape that rendered identically to a phone with no messages — walking the rows for what resolves and naming the missing field on the record. It refuses to spend `user_version` 0 as version 0 and refuses to compare the version it saw against a range nobody read from a real file. It refuses to write `false` for an unrecorded direction, and refuses to let an app-specific extra overwrite the shared chat keys, because the `ChatMessage` shell writes `type`, `subtype`, `direction` and `date` before any extra and drops a null extra rather than writing it.

### `plugin.messaging.line`

**Reads.** LINE for Android's message store, selected by file name and by nothing else: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the artifact's `name`, takes the part after the last `/` and acts only on exactly `naver_line`. The shared gate `stage_sqlite_db` skips a directory entry or an artifact with no data source, reads the first 16 bytes with a looping `read_full`, and where they are `SQLite format 3\0` spills the file to a temporary copy under the shared 512 MiB `MAX_DB_BYTES` cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one. A full 16-byte header that is not SQLite's is taken as LINE's app-encrypted store and recorded as such; fewer than 16 bytes delivered yields nothing, because a short read cannot support an encryption claim. The copy is opened read-only; `probe_catalogue` (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master`) must answer; `probe_table` asks the catalogue for `chat_history`; `probe_columns` reads its column list through `PRAGMA table_info`. Four logical fields are resolved by `FieldMap::resolve`, each from one candidate — `conversation` from `chat_id`, `sender` from `from_mid`, `text` from `content`, `sent_at` from `created_time` — and the candidate list is the parser's reading of the documented schema, confirmed by no real store. `id` is used when present, else `rowid`. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the open connection, 0 meaning "not recorded". The walk is one statement, `SELECT <id>, <conversation>, <sender>, <text>, <sent_at> FROM chat_history ORDER BY <sent_at>`, every unresolved field the literal `NULL`, with no row limit; `chat_id` and `from_mid` are read as text with an integer or real coerced to its decimal form (several LINE generations store the conversation id as an integer), and `id` and `created_time` as integers with a real truncated and a numeric string parsed. The declared bound `line-android` is `Unranged`: no real LINE database is held by this project, so no version was ever read out of one.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per `chat_history` row through the shared `ChatMessage` shell: `type: "LINE"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `service: "LINE"`, `platform: "Android"`, `text` (omitted when empty), `date` in whole Unix seconds from `created_time` read as milliseconds by `div_euclid(1000)` (omitted when 0 or negative), `contact` as the sender's `from_mid` (omitted when empty), `chat_identifier` as `chat_id` (omitted when empty), `rowid`, and a `name` of `message: <from_mid> — <first 80 characters or "(no text)">`; `is_from_me` and `direction` are never written, because `chat_history` has no direction column. After the rows, in this order: a `LineIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker (`subtype: parse_incomplete`, `source_table: "chat_history"`, `rows_dropped`, `records_recovered`, `first_error`, both incompleteness pairs with reason `unresolved_structure`) when the engine refused to step a row; then the schema notes `assess` entitles the parse to, each of `type: "LineIncomplete"` with `warning_class: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `app: "line-android"`, `store: "naver_line"`, `table: "chat_history"`, `schema_version_locator: "PRAGMA user_version"`, `schema_version_seen` or `schema_version_not_recorded: true` or `schema_version_undetermined`, `schema_unranged_reason`, `records_recovered`, `detail` and `name` — and never a `schema_version_supported` key. On every readable store one disclosure note is present: `SchemaNotRanged` (`subtype: "parser_stale"`, no incompleteness pair), whose sentence says this parser declares no validated schema range and gives the version seen "compared against nothing", or `SchemaVersionUndetermined` where the pragma would not read. A second note claims incompleteness with `subtype: "parser_stale"` and both pairs under reason `unvalidated`: `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` when `text` or `sent_at` has no column (a table with neither yields the note alone, no rows); `SchemaOptionalFieldsUnresolved` (disclosure only) when only `conversation` or `sender` failed to resolve; and `SchemaTableAbsent` (incomplete, both pairs) when the catalogue read and `chat_history` was not in it, with the version seen. A `naver_line` whose full header is not SQLite's yields one `EncryptedMessengerDatabase` record (`subtype: "encrypted_database"`, `app: "LINE"`, `status: "Encrypted"`, `encryption: "not identified (a full non-SQLite header; the scheme was not established)"`, a `note` saying app-level decryption is required, `name: "LINE database (encrypted)"`). A `naver_line` that would not open, whose catalogue would not read, whose table could not be looked for, or whose column list would not read yields one `LineIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` marker (both pairs, reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`); one carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged yields the same marker naming the I/O error. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with `content_incomplete_reason` / `wal_incomplete_reason` and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event, contact, group or media record is produced.

**Cannot.** It has never read a real LINE database: none exists in `test_data/`, `reference/`, `~/forensic_corpora` or `~/ctf-evidence` , so the four column names are the parser's own reading of the documented schema, `PRAGMA user_version` on a real store is recorded on the note and compared to nothing, and every readable store carries a `SchemaNotRanged` note saying so. It cannot say who sent a message relative to the device owner: no direction is ever written, `from_mid` is an opaque LINE identifier that is surfaced as `contact` without being resolved to a name, and the `contacts`, `groups` and `chat` tables are never opened. It cannot decrypt LINE's encrypted store, and cannot name the scheme: the encryption record says only that a full non-SQLite header was seen. It reads `created_time` as milliseconds unconditionally, so a store holding seconds would place every message in January 1970 and one holding microseconds in the far future, with nothing on the record to say so. It has no row cap and no `CapCounter`, so a store of any size is walked whole. It does not read the message `type` column, so stickers, images, calls and system messages are indistinguishable from text rows with an empty body, and a media message's location is not recovered. Where `conn.prepare` or `query_map` fails on a store whose table and columns were already established it yields one `LineIncomplete` record with `status: DatabaseUnreadable`, `source_table: "chat_history"`, SQLite's message as `sqlite_error` and both incompleteness pairs (reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`) beside the schema note, never an empty list (pinned by `a_chat_history_whose_query_will_not_run_is_reported_unreadable_not_empty`). It recovers no deleted rows and reads no `-journal` sibling.

**Refuses.** It refuses to spend a short read as an encryption finding: only a full 16-byte header that is not SQLite's yields the `EncryptedMessengerDatabase` record, and a source that delivered fewer bytes yields nothing. It refuses to name a cipher it did not establish — the encryption field says the scheme was not identified rather than guessing from the file name. It refuses to answer "no messages" from a read error: a store that will not open, a catalogue that will not answer, a `chat_history` lookup that will not run and a column list that will not read each produce `StoreUnreadable`, and an absent `chat_history` in a catalogue that read produces `SchemaTableAbsent`, never silence. It refuses to let a renamed column read as an empty device: a `chat_history` whose `content` or `created_time` no longer resolves is walked for what resolves and the note names the logical field with both incompleteness pairs, and a table with neither yields the note alone with no manufactured row — naming a column the schema lacks would fail `prepare()` and drop the whole conversation instead. It refuses to declare a schema range it did not read from a real file, and refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as version 0 or an unreadable pragma as in range. It refuses to infer direction from the sender id, because attributing a message to the wrong party is the most consequential error this tool can make. It refuses to place an unset `created_time` at the epoch, and refuses to write an empty `text`, `contact` or `chat_identifier`.

### `plugin.messaging.signal`

**Reads.** Signal's Android artifacts, and it probes far more than its name gate admits. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::Stream`. An artifact with no data source is answered with a `SignalIdentified` record only when its name ends `signal.db`, `plaintext.db`, contains `signal` with a `.db`/`.sqlite` extension, or is `signal*.backup`. Otherwise up to 8,192 bytes are read from offset 0 in a **single** `read_at`; a source that errors there and is Signal-named yields a `SignalIncomplete` `SourceUnreadable` record (reason `short_read`). If the first 16 bytes are `SQLite format 3\0` the file is treated as a candidate database **whatever its name**: a size of 0 or over 2 GiB (`MAX_DB_SIZE`) is refused with a `StoreUnreadable` marker when Signal-named (silence otherwise), else the source is spilled by `TempDb::spill` with its `-wal` under the 2 GiB cap and opened. The Signal schema is then required — `recipient`, `thread`, and one of `message`, `sms`, `mms` — through `sqlite_master`; a file lacking it yields nothing, and a catalogue that will not answer is examined for a SQLCipher-with-plaintext-header signature (a 32-byte header with a valid page size, file-format versions 1 or 2, and a non-zero reserve byte at offset 20) before being reported. If the head is not SQLite but its first four bytes frame a length under 4,096 followed by a parseable backup `Header` frame with a 16-byte IV, the whole file is read under a 4 GiB cap (`MAX_BACKUP_SIZE`) as a Signal Android backup: with a passphrase — which arrives only as the credential supplied for this file through `POST …/credential` with kind `signal_backup_passphrase`; the artifact's metadata is not read for one, because the ingest field `signal_backup_password` is replaced by the redaction marker at ingest, before any module runs — the key is stretched by 250,000 SHA-512 rounds over the salt and the space-stripped passphrase, split by HKDF-SHA256 (zero salt, info `Backup Export`) into an AES-256-CTR key and an HMAC-SHA256 key, and every frame's 10-byte truncated MAC is checked over the ciphertext before decryption; `statement` frames are replayed into a fresh SQLite file, the `DatabaseVersion` frame becomes that file's `PRAGMA user_version`, and attachment, avatar and sticker blobs are skipped while keeping the counter aligned. On a database with the schema it reads `recipient` (up to thirteen name/identifier columns, whichever exist), `thread` (`_id` plus `recipient_id`, `thread_recipient_id` or `recipient_ids`), the attachment index from `attachment.message_id` or `part.mid`, and the message table — `message` when present, else `sms` then `mms` — through a `FieldMap` of ten logical fields (`thread`/`thread_id`, `from`/`from_recipient_id`, `to`/`to_recipient_id`, `address`, `text`/`body`, `date`, `sent_at`/`date_sent`, `received_at`/`date_received`, `type`, `read`), newest first by whichever of `date_received`, `date_sent`, `date` resolved, under a bound `LIMIT`. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the connection with 0 as "not recorded".

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per message, `type: "Signal"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `service: "Signal"`, `store` naming the table, `rowid`, `thread_id`, `text`, `message_type`, `read`, `is_from_me` and `direction` only when the row's `type` bitmask decoded — base type `type & 0x1F` in 21..=26 is outgoing, anything else recorded is received — `contact`/`chat_display_name` (the thread's recipient resolved through the recipient map by system name, profile name, given/family names, username, nickname, E.164, phone or group id, in that order, else `Recipient <id>`; where no recipient resolves, the row's `address` text, else `thread:<id>`, else `unknown`), `chat_identifier` (E.164, phone, username or group id, else `recipient:<id>`), `sender` (`Me` for outgoing), `has_attachments`, `is_group`, `date` in whole Unix seconds judged by magnitude from `date_received`, `date_sent` or `date` with `date_rfc3339` beside it, or `date_unusable: true` with `date_raw` when the value could not be placed; a row with columns that would not decode is stamped `content_incomplete` with `undecoded_columns`. One `SignalContact` record (`subtype: "contact"`) per recipient up to 100,000 (`MAX_CONTACT_ENTRIES`). One `SignalIncomplete` schema-support record **per message table walked** whose column list read — so a legacy `sms`+`mms` store carries two — with `warning_class: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `app: "signal-android"`, `source_table`, `status: SchemaNotRanged` on every readable store because `SCHEMA_SUPPORT` is `Unranged`, no `schema_version_supported` key, the `user_version` seen (a replayed backup carries its `DatabaseVersion` frame's value), and `status: SchemaFieldsUnresolved` with the incompleteness pair only when `text` or `type` did not resolve. Beside those: `CapReached` markers (`SignalIncomplete` per table at 500,000 messages, `SignalContactIncomplete` at 100,000 contacts), one `RowsUndecodable` marker per source with dropped rows, a `TableUnreadable` record listing every table or query that failed, and always one `SignalSummary` (`message_count`, `contact_count`, `contacts_emitted`, `thread_count`, `rows_dropped` with `counts_are_floor`, `threads_with_unresolved_recipient` with an attribution sentence, `load_errors`, and a name prefixed "at least" when any gap exists). Where rows were dropped, every `Signal` and `SignalContact` record is stamped `inventory_incomplete`. Refusals are their own records: `StoreNotSqlite` for a Signal-named file whose first 16 bytes are not the header (with `size` and `sqlcipher_consistent`, true when the size is a whole number of 4,096-byte pages), `StoreEncrypted` (reason `encrypted`, `reserved_bytes_per_page`, `scheme: sqlcipher4_raw_key_plaintext_header`) for a plaintext-header SQLCipher store with no key supplied — and, when its raw key spec is supplied for that file (`POST …/credential`, kind `signal_ios_key_spec`, `x'…'` or bare hex, parsed straight into a zeroizing `RawKeySpec`), the store and its committed WAL frames decrypted by `seance_sqlcipher` and Signal for iOS's GRDB schema read by `ios_grdb`: `Signal` records (`platform: ios`, `unique_id`, `record_type_code`, `text`, `date` from `timestamp`, `received_at`, `thread_unique_id`, `author`, `read`, and a `direction_basis` saying no direction is stated) from `model_TSInteraction`, `SignalThread` from `model_TSThread`, `SignalContact` from `model_SignalRecipient` joined to `model_OWSUserProfile` (profile name and username;
