the profile key is not read), a `SignalSummary` (`platform: ios`, `pages`, `integrity_verified`, the WAL frame counts and their authentication, `grdb_migrations`, `grdb_last_migration`, `schema_grading: structural`, `credential_kind`), and a `SignalIncomplete` schema record (`app: signal-ios`, unranged, version located in `grdb_migrations`) that supersedes the `StoreEncrypted` one on the re-run; a spec that does not decrypt page 1 is reported back rejected and nothing from that run is recorded; `BackupHeaderUnrecognised` for a `signal*.backup` whose first frame will not parse, and a `SignalBackup` record (`subtype: "summary"`) for every recognised backup saying `decrypted` true or false, the passphrase requirement, `frames_replayed`, `ended_cleanly`, `rows_lost`, `schema_statements_failed`, and on a partial replay the reason (`cap_reached` at 20,000,000 frames, `short_read` when the stream ended without its `End` frame, `unresolved_structure` when statements would not apply). Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused store is stamped by `TempDb::stamp_incompleteness`.

**Cannot.** It has never read a real plaintext Signal store, and no validated schema range exists. Two real stores are held and neither was read, for two different reasons that are not "no key": the android2022 `signal.db` is SQLCipher under a keystore-wrapped key this project does not hold in usable form, and the ios2022ffs `grdb/signal.sqlite` — whose raw key spec *is* in the same export's keychain plist — is a SQLCipher 4 raw-key / HMAC-SHA512 store with a 32-byte plaintext header that `seance_sqlcipher` now decrypts (every page and WAL frame authenticates under that key), but it carries Signal for iOS's GRDB schema, not this module's Android schema, so it validates nothing here; the `SCHEMA_SUPPORT` reason says exactly that. That iOS store is read by the GRDB reader once its key spec is supplied, and the reader is graded **structurally only**: on the real store every page and committed WAL frame authenticates and every column it resolves is present, but the store holds no messages, so no app-written message row has been read, `recordType` codes are unconfirmed, and no message direction is stated; its rows are exercised on a GRDB-shaped store this project encrypts. It does not find the key in the case's keychain itself. It cannot decrypt an Android SQLCipher `signal.db`: the key for it is not accepted, and such a store leaves only a `StoreNotSqlite` or `StoreEncrypted` record. Its backup decryption has been validated end to end only against a backup its own tests wrote with a mirror of `FullBackupExporter` and against RFC 5869 for the HKDF half; the 250,000-round stretch has never been checked against a real Signal-produced `.backup`, and a real backup that decrypts wrongly would fail its first MAC and be reported as the passphrase rejected (wrong, or the first frame corrupt), never as garbage. It cannot tell a wrong passphrase from a corrupt first frame: both fail the same MAC, and the rejection says so. It reads the head of a file with one unlooped `read_at`, so a windowed source that answers 8,192 with fewer than 16 bytes makes a real Signal database read as "not SQLite" and, if Signal-named, files a `StoreNotSqlite` record asserting its first 16 bytes are not the header — a claim about the evidence made from a short read; no test pins that path. It spills **every** SQLite file in a case up to 2 GiB before deciding it is not Signal, because the schema, not the name, is the gate. It cannot attribute a message whose thread's recipient reference will not resolve except by fallback, and says so per thread on the summary. It cannot read attachments beyond their existence, reactions, mentions, quotes, calls, group membership, disappearing-message timers, or the `groups` table, and it cannot recover deleted rows. Its direction reading is the `MmsSmsColumns.Types` base-type convention of the Android client; a store from a different client that reused `type` differently would be read wrong with no check. Its ceilings are 500,000 messages across all tables, 100,000 contacts, 2 GiB of database, 4 GiB of backup, 100 MiB per frame and 20,000,000 frames, each stated on a record when hit.

**Refuses.** It refuses to read a SQLCipher store's header bytes 60..63 as a schema version: `PRAGMA user_version` is read only through an open connection, because on the iOS store those bytes are ciphertext (they read 360,193,054) and on a WAL-mode store the header predates the last migration. It refuses to report a plaintext-header SQLCipher store as damaged: a genuine header with a non-zero reserve byte behind which nothing will read is `StoreEncrypted` with reason `encrypted`, never `unresolved_structure`. It refuses to say what an unreadable Signal file held — every such record ends with the sentence that its absence from the message list is not evidence of absence. It refuses to decrypt a backup without the passphrase, recording the backup as locked rather than trying anything. It refuses a frame whose truncated HMAC does not verify, ending the replay with the error rather than decrypting unauthenticated bytes; a MAC failure on the first frame is reported as the passphrase rejected — in words that name a corrupt first frame as the other cause — and no records are returned, while a failure after a MAC has verified, or a header that does not parse, is a module error — not a verdict on the passphrase. It refuses to report a passphrase accepted that no MAC tested: a backup that ends after its header reports no verdict (`not_used`). It refuses to present a partial replay as whole: a capped, truncated or lossy replay marks the `SignalBackup` record and the replayed database `content_incomplete` with the reason. It refuses to count a message row twice or a marker as a message, taking `records_recovered` before markers join the list. It refuses to spend `user_version` 0 as version 0, and refuses to compare a version to a range nobody read from a real file. And it refuses to walk a file that carries the SQLite header but not the Signal schema, yielding nothing, because a database that is not Signal's is not a finding about Signal.

### `plugin.messaging.skype`

**Reads.** The classic desktop Skype `main.db`, selected by a generic file name and confirmed only by content. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the artifact's `name`, takes the part after the last `/`, and acts only on exactly `main.db`. The shared gate `stage_sqlite_db` skips a directory entry or an artifact with no data source, reads the first 16 bytes with a looping `read_full`, and where they are `SQLite format 3\0` spills the file to a temporary copy under the shared 512 MiB `MAX_DB_BYTES` cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one; any other outcome of the gate — not SQLite, header unreadable, staging failed — yields nothing, deliberately, because the name alone does not say this is Skype's file. The copy is opened read-only and treated as Skype's only when `PRAGMA table_info(Accounts)` lists a `skypename` column and `PRAGMA table_info(Messages)` lists at least one column; the signature is deliberately not the body column, so a store whose `body_xml` was renamed is still recognised. The owning account is `SELECT skypename FROM Accounts WHERE skypename IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1`. Six logical fields are resolved against `Messages` through `FieldMap::resolve`, each from one candidate: `author`, `sent_at` from `timestamp`, `body` from `body_xml`, `display_name` from `from_dispname`, `partner` from `dialog_partner`, `chat` from `chatname`; `id` is used when present, else `rowid`. The schema version is Skype's own, not SQLite's: `AppSchemaVersion` is looked for through `probe_table`, and `SELECT SQLiteSchemaVersion FROM AppSchemaVersion LIMIT 1` is read three-valued — an integer, or text that parses as one, is the version; an absent table, a NULL, or no row is "not recorded"; a catalogue that will not answer, a value of any other type, or a query error is "undetermined". The declared bound `skype-desktop` is `Validated` on the single-point range `66..=66`, the value read from the one real store on file — plaso's test database `skype_main.db` (ClientVersion `0/6.6.0.106//_checksum_3768521794`, 15 `Messages` rows), on which `PRAGMA user_version` is 0. The walk is one statement, `SELECT <id>, <author>, <sent_at>, <body>, <display_name>, <partner>, <chat> FROM Messages ORDER BY <sent_at>`, every unresolved field the literal `NULL`, with no row limit. `body_xml` is reduced to text by dropping every character between `<` and `>` and decoding `&lt;`, `&gt;`, `&quot;`, `&apos;` and, last, `&amp;`.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per `Messages` row through the shared `ChatMessage` shell: `type: "Skype"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `service: "Skype"`, `platform: "Desktop"`, `text` (the stripped body, omitted when empty), `date` in whole Unix seconds straight from `timestamp` (omitted when 0 or negative), `is_from_me` and `direction` only when both the row's `author` and the account's `skypename` were read — equal is `sent`, unequal `received` — `contact` as `from_dispname`, else `author`, else `dialog_partner`, `chat_identifier` as `chatname`, else `dialog_partner`, omitted when neither is present, `rowid`, `author` when non-empty, and a `name` of `<direction or "message">: <contact> — <first 80 characters or "(no text)">`. After the rows, in this order: a `SkypeIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker (`subtype: parse_incomplete`, `source_table: "Messages"`, `rows_dropped`, `records_recovered`, `first_error`, both incompleteness pairs with reason `unresolved_structure`) when any fetched row would not decode; then the schema notes `assess` entitles the parse to — at most one about the version and one about the fields, each of `type: "SkypeIncomplete"` with `warning_class: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `app: "skype-desktop"`, `store: "main.db"`, `table: "Messages"`, `schema_version_locator: "AppSchemaVersion.SQLiteSchemaVersion"`, `schema_version_seen` or `schema_version_not_recorded: true` or `schema_version_undetermined`, `schema_version_supported: "66..=66"` with `schema_version_evidence` naming plaso's `skype_main.db`, `records_recovered`, `detail` and `name`. Disclosure notes carry `subtype: "parser_stale"` and no incompleteness pair: `SchemaOutsideValidated`, `SchemaVersionNotRecorded`, `SchemaVersionUndetermined` (never spent as in range), and `SchemaOptionalFieldsUnresolved` naming in `schema_unresolved_fields` any of `author`, `display_name`, `partner`, `chat` that no column carried — a missing `chatname` is disclosed this way because without it every message lands in one thread. One note claims incompleteness, `SchemaFieldsUnresolved`, with `subtype: "parser_stale"` and both pairs under reason `unvalidated`, when `body` or `sent_at` has no column; a `Messages` with neither yields that note alone and no rows. A store on version 66 whose six fields all resolved gets no note. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with `content_incomplete_reason` / `wal_incomplete_reason` and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended — but only when at least one record was produced or the main file itself was cut short, so a foreign `main.db` staged whole leaves nothing. No timeline event, no contact records, no call records, no file transfers are produced.

**Cannot.** It cannot tell you a Skype store was present and unreadable. Because `main.db` is the name dozens of applications use, a `main.db` carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged, one that will not open, one whose `Accounts` has no `skypename`, one whose `Messages` column list will not read, and one whose `SELECT` will not prepare or run all yield nothing and no record — and a damaged Skype store is indistinguishable from any of those. It cannot establish direction without both halves: a store with no `Accounts` row, or a `Messages` row with a NULL `author`, leaves `is_from_me` and `direction` off the record rather than guessing, and a multi-account `main.db` is judged against whichever account `LIMIT 1` returned. Its schema knowledge is one point wide: version 66 from one plaso fixture, and every other version is disclosed as beyond or below that point while the store is still parsed on the assumption its columns mean the same thing; the candidate list holds exactly one physical name per field, so any rename at all is an unresolved field. The body is de-tagged by a character-level bracket count that knows nothing of XML: a literal `<` inside an entity-decoded body or a quoted attribute containing `>` mis-nests, and Skype's `<ss>` emoticons, `<a href>` links, `<quote>` blocks and `<partlist>` call records are flattened to their inner text with no marker of what they were. It reads `timestamp` as Unix seconds unconditionally. It has no row cap and no `CapCounter`. It reads only `Messages` and one row of `Accounts`: `Contacts`, `Calls`, `CallMembers`, `Transfers`, `Chats`, `Conversations` and `Participants` are never opened, so no contact list, call log or file-transfer record comes from this module, and a message's counterparty is only what the row itself names. It does not read the modern Skype (UWP / Electron `skype.db`, `s4l-*.db`) stores at all, and recovers no deleted rows.

**Refuses.** It refuses to assert a Skype store on the strength of a generic filename: no `StoreUnreadable`, encrypted or staging-failure marker is ever filed for a `main.db` that was not shown by content to be Skype's, because a marker that fired on every application's `main.db` would teach an examiner to skip the markers that matter. It refuses to read a renamed body column as "not Skype": the signature is `Accounts.skypename`, and a `Messages` whose `body_xml` or `timestamp` no longer resolves is reported by logical field name with both incompleteness pairs, walked for what resolves, and with neither field yields the note alone rather than manufactured rows. It refuses to compare `PRAGMA user_version` to anything — Skype does not keep its version there and it reads 0 on the real store — and refuses to spend an absent `AppSchemaVersion`, a NULL, a non-numeric value or a failed read as in range. It refuses to widen the validated range past the one file opened. It refuses to claim incompleteness for a version outside `66..=66` — that is a disclosure — reserving the incompleteness pair for a required field that is not there. It refuses to invert direction silently: with either the author or the owner unknown, direction is absent, never `received`. It refuses to place an unset `timestamp` at the epoch, and refuses to write an empty `text`, `contact`, `chat_identifier` or `author` where the store held an empty string.

### `plugin.messaging.snapchat`

**Reads.** Snapchat's two SQLite stores, selected by file name and then by content. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the artifact's `name`, takes the part after the last `/`, and acts only on exactly `arroyo.db` (the Arroyo chat store, the same schema on Android and iOS) or `main.db` (the friends list); every other name yields nothing. The shared gate `stage_sqlite_db` then skips a directory entry or an artifact with no data source, reads the first 16 bytes with a looping `read_full` — so a windowed source that answers 16 with 8 does not file a real store as "not SQLite" — and, where they are `SQLite format 3\0`, spills the file to a temporary copy under the shared 512 MiB `MAX_DB_BYTES` cap together with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one (a WAL over 512 MiB is not staged and is recorded as `cap_reached`). The platform is read from the artifact's `name`, `path`, `parent_path` and `container_path` strings: `com.toyopagroup.picaboo`, `toyopagroup`, `picaboo` or `/var/mobile` is iOS; `com.snapchat.android`, `/data/data` or `/data/user` is Android; anything else is `Unknown`. For `arroyo.db` it opens the copy read-only, requires `probe_catalogue` (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master`) to answer, asks the catalogue for `conversation_message`, reads that table's column list with `PRAGMA table_info`, and resolves seven logical fields through `FieldMap::resolve` from single candidates — `conversation` from `client_conversation_id`, `server_message_id`, `sender` from `sender_id`, `sent_at` from `creation_timestamp`, `read_at` from `read_timestamp`, `content_type`, `content` from `message_content` — then walks `SELECT … FROM conversation_message ORDER BY <conversation>, <sent_at>` with every unresolved field as the literal `NULL` and no row limit. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the open connection, 0 meaning "not recorded", and compared with the declared bound: `snapchat-arroyo` is `Validated` on the single-point range `102..=102`, both endpoints being the value read from two real stores — the Magnet Virtual Summit 2022 Android CTF (Pixel 3) `data/data/com.snapchat.android/databases/arroyo.db` (2022-02-13, 7 rows) and the Magnet User Summit 2022 iOS CTF (iPhone 8) full-file-system `…/user_scoped/…/arroyo/arroyo.db` (2022-01-30, 2 rows). The message body is looked for inside the `message_content` protobuf by `seance_core::blob_text::recover_protobuf_text`, which walks length-delimited (wire type 2) fields and keeps the best-scoring printable UTF-8 field, and is kept only when the row's `content_type` is 1 (`text`) or an integer this parser has no label for. For `main.db` the copy is opened, `Friend`'s columns are read with `table_columns`, and the file is treated as Snapchat's only when that table exists and carries a `username` column; the fields `user_id` (`userId`), `display_name` (`displayName`) and `added_at` (`addedTimestamp`) are resolved beside the required `username`, and the bound `snapchat-friends` is `Validated` on `427..=427`, read from the one real `main.db` with its `-wal` in the same Android image (3 `Friend` rows).

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per `conversation_message` row through the shared `ChatMessage` shell: `type: "Snapchat"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `service: "Snapchat"`, `platform` as detected, `chat_identifier` and `conversation_id` (the conversation string), `source_table: "conversation_message"`, `server_message_id`, `sender_id`, `date` in whole Unix seconds (`creation_timestamp` ÷ 1000, omitted when 0 or negative), `read_timestamp` likewise in seconds and omitted when 0, `read` (true when `read_timestamp` > 0, false when it is 0, absent when NULL), `content_type` as the label `unknown`/`text`/`snap`/`media`/`status`/`reaction` for 0/1/2/3/5/6 or `type <n>` for any other integer, `text` only where a body was recovered, `body_recovered` written as a genuine `true`/`false` on every row, and a `name` of the form `snap <label>: <first 60 characters of the text, or [<label>]>`. No `is_from_me`, `direction`, `contact` or `sender` name is ever written: Arroyo records no owner account to compare `sender_id` against. One `SnapchatContact` (`subtype: "contact"`) per `Friend` row with `platform`, `source_table: "Friend"`, `service`, `username`, `user_id`, `display_name`, `added_date` in seconds (omitted when 0) and a `name` of the display name, else the username, else empty. After the rows of either table, in this order: a `RowsUndecodable` marker (`SnapchatIncomplete` or `SnapchatContactIncomplete`, `subtype: parse_incomplete`, `rows_dropped`, `records_recovered`, `first_error`, both incompleteness pairs with reason `unresolved_structure`) when any fetched row would not decode; then the schema notes `assess` entitles the parse to — at most one about the version and one about the fields, each a record of the same `*Incomplete` type with `warning_class: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `app`, `store`, `table`, `schema_version_locator: "PRAGMA user_version"`, `schema_version_seen` or `schema_version_not_recorded: true` or `schema_version_undetermined`, `schema_version_supported` (`102..=102` / `427..=427`) with `schema_version_evidence` naming the files above, `records_recovered`, `detail` and `name`. Disclosure notes carry `subtype: "parser_stale"` and no incompleteness pair: `SchemaOutsideValidated` (the version seen is outside the point, with `StaleWarning::message`), `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` (`PRAGMA user_version` 0), `SchemaVersionUndetermined` (the pragma would not read; never spent as in range), `SchemaOptionalFieldsUnresolved` (only non-required fields failed to resolve, listed in `schema_unresolved_fields`). Two notes claim incompleteness, with `subtype: "parser_stale"` and both pairs under reason `unvalidated`: `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` when any of `conversation`, `sender`, `sent_at` (Arroyo) or `username` (Friend) has no column, and `SchemaTableAbsent` when the catalogue read and `conversation_message` was not in `arroyo.db`. A store whose version is in range and whose every field resolved gets no note at all. An `arroyo.db` that would not open, whose catalogue would not read, whose table could not be looked for or whose column list would not read yields one `SnapchatIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` marker (both pairs, reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`) as the whole output; an `arroyo.db` carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged yields the same marker naming the I/O error. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with `content_incomplete_reason` / `wal_incomplete_reason` and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended — for `main.db` only when at least one record was produced or the main file itself was cut short. Nothing else: no timeline event of its own, no media, no snap content.

**Cannot.** It cannot recover most message bodies, and says so on every row: Snapchat keeps the body inside the `message_content` protobuf and deletes it by design after viewing or 24 hours, so `body_recovered: false` is the ordinary case and the record is metadata — who, in which conversation, when, what type, whether read. Where a body is recovered it is the best-scoring string field of the blob, not a decoded schema; a text field that shares the blob with a longer printable field yields the wrong one, a body under 2 bytes is never found, and a body on a row whose `content_type` is 0 or NULL (`unknown`), `snap`, `media`, `status` or `reaction` is discarded even when present. It cannot say who sent a message relative to the device owner — no direction is ever written — nor name a sender: `sender_id` is an opaque identifier and this module never joins it to `Friend`, which lives in a different file. It cannot tell `main.db` is Snapchat's until it has opened it: a `main.db` that will not open, or whose `Friend` table is absent or lacks `username`, yields nothing and no record, because dozens of apps use that name and a marker would assert a Snapchat store on a generic filename — so a damaged Snapchat `main.db` is silent; one whose `Friend` carries `username` and whose `SELECT` will not prepare or run yields one `SnapchatContactIncomplete` record with `status: DatabaseUnreadable`, `source_table: "Friend"` and SQLite's message as `sqlite_error`. Its schema knowledge is one point wide on each store: `102..=102` and `427..=427` are the only versions ever read from a real file, and a real store on any other version is disclosed as beyond or below that point while still being parsed on the assumption its columns mean the same thing. It reads `creation_timestamp`, `read_timestamp` and `addedTimestamp` as milliseconds unconditionally. It has no row cap and no `CapCounter`, so a store of any size is walked whole. Where `conn.prepare` or `query_map` fails on an `arroyo.db` whose table and columns were already established it yields one `SnapchatIncomplete` record with `status: DatabaseUnreadable`, `source_table: "conversation_message"`, SQLite's message as `sqlite_error` and both incompleteness pairs (reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`) beside the schema note, never an empty list (pinned by `a_conversation_message_query_that_will_not_run_is_reported_unreadable_not_empty` and `a_friend_query_that_will_not_run_is_reported_unreadable_not_empty`). It does not read `conversation`, `snap`, `story`, memories or any other Arroyo or `main.db` table, does not open `-journal` siblings, and recovers no deleted rows.

**Refuses.** It refuses to fabricate a body where none survived: `text` is absent and `body_recovered` is a literal `false`, so a report cannot read an ephemeral snap as a message that said nothing. It refuses to place an unset timestamp at the epoch — a 0 `creation_timestamp`, `read_timestamp` or `addedTimestamp` is an absent key, never 1970-01-01. It refuses to infer direction: with no owner column in Arroyo, `is_from_me` and `direction` are left off rather than derived from `sender_id`. It refuses to let a renamed column read as an empty device: a `conversation_message` whose `creation_timestamp`, `sender_id` or `client_conversation_id` no longer resolves is still walked for what resolves and the `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` note names the logical field with both incompleteness pairs, and a table carrying none of the three yields the note alone with no manufactured row. It refuses to answer "no messages" from a read error on `arroyo.db`: a catalogue that will not answer, a table that cannot be looked for and a column list that will not read each produce `StoreUnreadable`, while an absent `conversation_message` in a catalogue that read produces `SchemaTableAbsent` rather than silence. It refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as version 0 or an unreadable pragma as in range, and refuses to widen either validated range past the files actually opened. It refuses to claim incompleteness for a version merely outside the point — that is a disclosure with `subtype: parser_stale` — reserving the incompleteness pair for a required field or table that is not there. And it refuses to file a marker against a `main.db` it has not shown to be Snapchat's, for the reason above.

### `plugin.messaging.telegram`

**Reads.** Telegram for Android's `cache4.db`, selected by name: the artifact's `name`, lower-cased, must end in the path segment `cache4.db`. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, calls `stage_sqlite_db` itself rather than the shared dispose helper, and handles each outcome: `Staged` is parsed; `StagingFailed` (the header matched, the spill did not) becomes a `TelegramMessageIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` marker; `NoContent`, `NotSqlite` and `HeaderUnreadable` yield nothing. Staging is a 512 MiB-capped spill with the `-wal` sibling. On the read-only connection it first requires `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master` to answer; it then chooses the message table by asking `table_columns` for `messages_v2` and, if that returns no columns, `messages`. Because `table_columns` folds "no such table" and "the pragma failed" into one empty set, an empty result is disambiguated by a direct `sqlite_master` lookup for the chosen name. `FieldMap::resolve` binds `id` from `mid`, `dialog` from `uid`, `sent_at` from `date`, `from_me` from `out` and `body` from `data`, each with one candidate. `PRAGMA user_version` is read with 0 as "not recorded". The walk is `SELECT <id>, <dialog>, <sent_at>, <from_me>, <body> FROM <table> ORDER BY <sent_at or id>` with no `LIMIT`; the `data` cell is taken only when it is a BLOB. The message text is recovered from that TL-serialised blob by `tl::message_text`: the row's own `date` (as a little-endian `i32`) is searched for at every 4-byte-aligned offset from 4 on, and the bytes immediately after each hit must frame as a TL string — one-byte length, or `0xFE` and a three-byte length for 254 bytes and over, zero-padded to a 4-byte boundary, inside the blob, valid UTF-8, non-empty, and free of control characters other than tab, newline and carriage return. Nothing else in the blob is decoded: no layout is assumed, no sender, media, forward header or reply reference is read.

**Produces.** One `ChatMessage`-shaped `ParsedRecord` per row: `type: "TelegramMessage"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `platform: "Android"`, `service: "Telegram"`, `text` only where the anchored recovery produced one, `date` as whole Unix seconds taken directly from `date` (Telegram stores seconds; zero or negative omitted), `is_from_me`/`direction` only when `out` held a value (1 sent, otherwise received), `chat_identifier` as the decimal `uid`, `mid`, `content_encoding` — `"TL-serialized (message text recovered)"` or `"TL-serialized (not decoded)"` — and `text_recovered` as a boolean, with a bespoke `name` `Telegram <direction or "message"> in dialog <uid or "?">[: <first 60 characters>]`. Then a `TelegramMessageIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker if any fetched row would not decode, and exactly one schema-support record per parsed store: `type: "TelegramMessageIncomplete"`, `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `warning_class: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `app: "telegram-android"`, `source_table` naming `messages_v2` or `messages`, the `user_version` as seen, not recorded or unreadable, `status: SchemaNotRanged` on every readable store because `SCHEMA_SUPPORT` is `Unranged` ("no reference database of this app is held by this project") and no `schema_version_supported` key; `status: SchemaFieldsUnresolved` with both incompleteness pairs (reason `unvalidated`, `schema_unresolved_fields`) only when `dialog` or `sent_at` — the two required fields — did not resolve. Unlike the Viber and Kik parsers, a query that will not prepare or run after the table and columns were established produces a `StoreUnreadable` marker naming the engine's reason rather than an empty list. Staging shortfalls and a refused WAL are stamped on every record by `TempDb::stamp_incompleteness` with one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker.

**Cannot.** It has never been validated against a real `cache4.db`: none exists in `test_data/`, `reference/plaso/test_data`, `~/forensic_corpora` or `~/ctf-evidence` (the Hickman Android 14 image the Telegram counts came from is not on disk), so `SCHEMA_SUPPORT` is `Unranged`, every store reads `SchemaNotRanged`, and each candidate column name is a single reading of the documented schema. It cannot name a correspondent: `uid` is published as `chat_identifier` and never resolved through `users`, `chats` or `dialogs`, so every thread is a number and no record carries `contact`. It cannot say who sent a message inside a group beyond the `out` flag. It cannot recover a body whose text does not follow the row's date in the TL object — a message whose `date` value appears at two aligned offsets followed by two different well-formed strings (a forwarded message whose header carries its own date, a media caption) is left with no text and `text_recovered: false` rather than a guess; a message whose `date` is zero, NULL, or outside `i32` gets no text at all; a text that begins at an unaligned offset is never found. It cannot read media, stickers, reactions, edits, deletions, secret chats or the `enc_chats`/`media_v4` tables. It has no row cap. And it reads `text` only as the second candidate's absence — a store whose `data` column was renamed loses every body while the schema record names only `body` as an optional unresolved field with no incompleteness claim, since `body` is not in `REQUIRED_FIELDS`.

**Refuses.** It refuses to decode the TL object by an assumed layout, because the `TLRPC.Message` layout is version-specific and a layout guessed wrong surfaces the wrong text under a real date; the body is anchored on the row's own `date` column and taken only where every anchor that decodes agrees. It refuses to publish text at all when two anchors disagree — the record then says `text_recovered: false` — because recovering the wrong message text is worse than recovering none. It refuses to walk a store in which neither `dialog` nor `sent_at` resolved, emitting the `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` record with `records_recovered: 0` instead. It refuses to let a header-bearing file that would not stage, an unanswering catalogue, a present table whose columns would not list, a query that would not prepare or a walk that would not run pass as "no messages": each becomes a `StoreUnreadable` marker with the reason, and only a catalogue that answered and held neither `messages_v2` nor `messages` is treated as "not a Telegram schema" and yields nothing. It refuses to spend `user_version` 0 as version 0, refuses to compare a version against a range nobody read from a real file, and refuses to write `false` where the store recorded no direction.

### `plugin.messaging.twitter`

**Reads.** Twitter/X for Android's per-account databases, selected by Twitter's own naming pattern and by nothing else. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the artifact's `name`, takes the part after the last `/`, and acts on two shapes: `<digits>-<digits>.db` is the per-account main store (the second number is an app-version schema revision, matched by pattern rather than a fixed value) and `<digits>-search.db` the search history; the leading digits are the account owner's numeric id and are parsed from the evidence name, never from the staged copy's path. Everything after that gate is the shared entry path `seance_sqlite_util::process_named_sqlite_db`: a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing; the first 16 bytes are read with a looping `read_full`; fewer than 16 bytes, or 16 bytes that are not `SQLite format 3\0`, yield nothing; a file carrying the header is spilled under the shared 512 MiB `MAX_DB_BYTES` cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one. The copy is opened read-only and `probe_catalogue` must answer. For the main store `probe_table` must list `conversation_entries` (a view counts) or the file is treated as not the DM schema and yields nothing; `PRAGMA user_version` is then read and compared with the validated window `7..=59`, every endpoint read from a real store — 7 in plaso's `test_data/twitter_android.db`, 59 in both Magnet 2022 CTF Pixel 3 stores (`com.twitter.android/databases/0-61.db` and `1489429766507835392-61.db`). Columns are resolved through a `FieldMap` against `PRAGMA table_info`, candidates in preference order: `conversation_entries` — `entry_id`; `conversation_id`; `sender_id` from `user_id` then `sender_id`; `created` from `created`, `created_at`, `timestamp`, `sort_timestamp`; `entry_type` from `entry_type` then `type`; and the body from a `text` column or from the serialised `data` blob (`data`, `request_body`, `attachment`); `users` — `user_id` from `user_id`, `_id`, `id` and `screen_name` from `username`, `screen_name`, `handle`. Both real stores carry the first candidate of every entry. The DM walk is one statement `ORDER BY <conversation_id>, <created>` with every unresolved field the literal `NULL` and no row limit; the body is the `text` column when non-empty, else the best-scoring length-delimited string field of the `data` protobuf recovered by `seance_core::blob_text::recover_protobuf_text`; the timestamp's unit is judged by magnitude (microseconds ≥ 10^15, milliseconds ≥ 10^12, else seconds); direction is computed as sender id equals owner id — there is no stored flag. `users` is read (`WHERE <screen_name> IS NOT NULL`) only when the table is present and both its fields resolved. For the search store `search_queries` must be present; `time` and `query` (from `query` then `name`) are resolved and walked `ORDER BY <time> DESC`. No version window is declared for the search store (`twitter-android-search`): no real `-search.db` has been observed, both real accounts keeping `search_queries` inside the main database — so the main store's own `search_queries` is read too, when `probe_table` lists it, through the same two fields and the same ordering, its drift filed under the main schema (`twitter-android`, `7..=59`); both real main stores carry it (plaso's `twitter_android.db`, one search; the Magnet 2022 CTF Pixel 3 `1489429766507835392-61.db`, two).

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per `conversation_entries` row through the shared `ChatMessage` shell: `type: "TwitterDM"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `service: "Twitter/X DM"`, `platform: "Android"`, `text` when a body was found, `date` in whole Unix seconds (omitted when 0 or negative), `is_from_me` and its derived `direction` only when both the row's sender id and the filename's owner id were read, `chat_identifier` and `conversation_id` (the conversation string), `contact` and `sender_screen_name` (the `@handle` from `users`, when resolved), `source_table: "conversation_entries"`, `entry_id`, `sender_id` as a decimal string, `entry_type` as stored, `text_recovered` — a genuine `true` when the body came out of the protobuf blob rather than a `text` column, `false` when it came from `text`, absent when there is no body — and a `name` of `<direction or "dm">: <first 60 characters of the body, or "(dm)">`. One `TwitterSearch` (`subtype: "search"`, `platform`, `source_table: "search_queries"`, `service: "Twitter/X"`, `query`, `date` or null, `name: "search: <first 60 characters>"`) per `search_queries` row with a non-NULL query, from a `-search.db` or from the main store alike; a main store's searches follow its DMs. After the DM rows, in this order: a `TwitterIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker (`subtype: parse_incomplete`, `source_table`, `rows_dropped`, `records_recovered`, `first_error`, both incompleteness pairs with reason `unresolved_structure`) when the engine refused to step a row; a `TwitterUserIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker when a `users` row would not decode, with `records_recovered` the number of handles resolved; then the schema findings, all `type: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `subtype: "parser_stale"`: `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` (`app`, `source_table`, `unresolved_fields`, `records_recovered`, the `content_incomplete` pair with reason `unresolved_structure`) for `conversation_entries` when any of its five fields did not resolve, for the body only when neither `text` nor `data` resolved, and for `users` when either of its fields did not (in which case no handle is resolved and DMs are attributed by numeric id); `SchemaOutsideValidated` (the shared marker with `seen_schema_version`, `supported_range: "7..=59"`, `message`, detail and name post-stamped; a disclosure with no incompleteness claim) when `PRAGMA user_version` is outside the window and the rows still parse; `SchemaVersionUndetermined` with `content_incomplete: true`, reason `unresolved_structure`, when the pragma would not read; `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` with no incompleteness pair when it is 0 — each of the three carrying `validated_against` naming plaso's `twitter_android.db` (7) and the two Magnet 2022 Pixel 3 `-61.db` stores (59). The search walk files its own `TwitterSearchIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` and a `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` under `twitter-android-search` (under `twitter-android` for the main store's table); a main-store `search_queries` whose presence could not be established, whose column list would not read, or whose query would not prepare or run yields one `TwitterSearchIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` marker naming SQLite's error, beside the DMs. A store that would not open, whose catalogue would not read, whose required table could not be looked for, or whose column list would not read yields one `TwitterIncomplete` or `TwitterSearchIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` marker (both pairs, reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`); a file carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged yields the same marker naming the I/O error. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event, tweet, follower or media record is produced.

**Cannot.** It cannot read a body it was not given plainly: on every real store observed the DM text lives inside the `data` protobuf, and the recovery is the best-scoring string field of that blob, not a decoded schema — so an entry whose longest printable field is a URL, a display name or a reaction yields that instead of the message, and `text_recovered: true` is the only warning. It cannot say who a conversation is with: `conversation_id` is Twitter's own string, participants are not read, and `contact` is the sender's handle only when `users` resolved it — otherwise the record carries a bare numeric `sender_id`. Its direction is only as good as the filename: a store renamed away from `<ownerId>-<NN>.db` has no owner id and no direction on any record, and the `0-61.db` shape (owner id 0) compares every sender against zero. It cannot distinguish a DM from a join, leave, reaction or read-receipt entry except by the raw `entry_type` integer, which is passed through undecoded, so a conversation's non-message entries are emitted as `TwitterDM` records with no body and the label `(dm)`. Its schema window is two points wide (7 and 59), so a store on any other version is disclosed as outside it and parsed on the assumption its columns mean the same; and the search store has no window at all, drift there being caught only by the column map. It has never read a real `<userId>-search.db`. Of a search row it reads only `time` and `query`: `type`, `query_id`, `latitude`/`longitude`/`radius`/`location` (a geo-scoped search), `priority` and the suggestion blobs are not on the record, so a saved search and a recent one read alike. A main store whose `conversation_entries` query fails is returned before its searches are read. It has no row cap and no `CapCounter`. Where `conn.prepare` or `query_map` fails on a store whose table and columns were already established it yields one `DatabaseUnreadable` record naming the table and carrying SQLite's message as `sqlite_error` and both incompleteness pairs (reason `unresolved_structure`) — `TwitterIncomplete` for `conversation_entries` (beside the schema findings already made), `TwitterSearchIncomplete` for `search_queries`, and `TwitterUserIncomplete` for the `users` handle lookup, whose failure leaves the DMs attributed by numeric id and now says so — never an empty list or a silent lookup (pinned by the three `*_query_that_will_not_run_*` tests). A `users` table that could not be looked for, or whose column list would not read, is a `TwitterUserIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` record beside the DMs, not a store without handles; only an absent `users` table carries no record . It does not read tweets, timelines, followers, media, `cursors`, `notifications` or `drafts`, and recovers no deleted rows.

**Refuses.** It refuses to answer "no DMs" from a read error: a store that will not open, a catalogue that answers `SQLITE_CORRUPT`, a `conversation_entries` lookup that will not run and a column list that will not read each produce `StoreUnreadable`, and only a readable catalogue with no such table is treated as not the DM schema and yields nothing. It refuses to file a marker against a database it does not recognise, because a finding on every foreign file teaches the examiner to skip the findings that matter. It refuses to let a renamed `created` or `conversation_id` end the walk with an empty list: the row is read for what resolves and `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` names the field. It refuses to present a blob-recovered body as a verbatim field — `text_recovered` says which it was. It refuses to assert direction without both the owner id and the sender id, leaving `is_from_me` and `direction` absent rather than writing a null. It refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as "older than 7", refuses to spend a pragma that would not read as in range, and refuses to declare a window for the search store nobody has opened. It refuses to widen the validated range past the files actually read. It refuses to place an unset timestamp at the epoch and refuses to read a 16-digit microsecond value as milliseconds. It refuses to count a lost `users` row as an account with no handle, tallying it under `TwitterUserIncomplete` instead of flattening it to NULL. And it refuses to file a DM marker and a search marker under one type, since the two walks emit different record types and a search failure must not join the DM conversation grouping.

### `plugin.messaging.viber`

**Reads.** Viber for Android's message store, selected by file name and by nothing else: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent`, declares `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the artifact's `name` metadata, takes the part after the last `/` and accepts it only when it is exactly `viber_messages` or `viber_data`. Everything after that gate is the shared SQLite entry path `seance_sqlite_util::process_named_sqlite_db`: a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing; the first 16 bytes are read through a looping `read_full`, so a windowed source that answers a 16-byte request with 4 does not file the store as "not SQLite"; fewer than 16 bytes delivered, or 16 bytes that are not `SQLite format 3\0`, yields nothing and no record; and a file carrying the header is staged whole to a temporary file under the shared 512 MiB cap (`MAX_DB_BYTES`) together with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one, the rollback journal deliberately not. The staged copy is opened read-only. `probe_catalogue` (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master`) must answer; `probe_table` then asks the catalogue for a table or view named `messages`; `probe_columns` reads its column list through `PRAGMA table_info`. Five logical fields are resolved against that list by `FieldMap::resolve`, first present candidate winning: `id` from `_id`, `text` from `body`, `sent_at` from `date`, `from_me` from `send_type` then `type`, and `conversation` from `conversation_id`. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the open connection, never from the header bytes, with 0 read as "not recorded". The walk is one statement — `SELECT <id>, <text>, <sent_at>, <from_me>, <conversation> FROM messages ORDER BY <sent_at or id>` — in which every unresolved field is the literal `NULL`, and no row limit. Contacts are not read: `participants` and `participants_info` are never opened.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per `messages` row, built through the shared `ChatMessage` shell: `type: "Viber"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `platform: "Android"`, `service: "Viber"`, `text` (an empty body is omitted, not written as an empty string), `date` in whole Unix seconds from `date` read as milliseconds by `div_euclid(1000)` with a zero or negative value omitted, `is_from_me` and its derived `direction` (`sent`/`received`) only when the direction column held a value — `send_type`/`type` equal to 1 is sent, any other integer received, a NULL leaves both keys off the record — the raw `rowid`, `conversation_id` where the row had one, and a `name` of the form `<direction or "message">: <first 80 characters or "(no text)">`; no `contact` and no `chat_identifier` are ever set, so the record carries neither. After the rows, in this order: one `ViberIncomplete` record with `status: RowsUndecodable` when any row the query returned would not decode (`rows_dropped`, `records_recovered`, `first_error`, both incompleteness pairs with reason `unresolved_structure`, the sentence on `content_incomplete_detail`, `inventory_incomplete_detail` and `detail`); then exactly one schema-support record on every parsed store — `type: "ViberIncomplete"`, `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `warning_class: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `app: "viber-android"`, `source_table: "messages"`, `records_recovered`, `schema_version_locator: "user_version"`, `schema_version_seen` with `schema_version_recorded: true` when the pragma was non-zero, `schema_version_recorded: false` when it was 0, `schema_version_detail` when it would not read, and a `status` that is `SchemaNotRanged` on every readable store because the declaration is `SchemaBound::Unranged` — the record carries **no** `schema_version_supported` key, and its sentence says this parser has not been validated against a real Viber database and why ("no reference database of this app is held by this project; the schema version is recorded, not ranged"). That record stamps the incompleteness pair (`content_incomplete` and `inventory_incomplete`, reason `unvalidated`, `schema_unresolved_fields` naming the logical fields) in exactly one case: a required field — `text` or `sent_at` — that no column resolved, with `status: SchemaFieldsUnresolved`; a version outside any range is never claimed because no range exists. A store the shared gate stages short carries `content_incomplete: true` with `content_incomplete_reason` (`cap_reached` or `short_read`) and, where the `-wal` sibling was refused, `wal_incomplete_reason`, stamped by `TempDb::stamp_incompleteness` onto every record plus one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker. Where the store was named and would not open, its catalogue would not read, `messages` could not be looked for, or its column list would not read, one `ViberIncomplete` record with `status: StoreUnreadable` and both incompleteness pairs (reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`) is the whole output; where the SQLite header was present but staging failed, the shared gate emits the same marker naming the error. No timeline event is produced by this module; the chat records reach the unified timeline only through `seance_db`'s `chat_message` projection, so a row with no `date` never appears there.

**Cannot.** It cannot name a correspondent: Viber keeps the counterparty in `participants`/`participants_info` with version-specific joins that this build does not read, so no record carries `contact` or `chat_identifier`, the Conversations view groups these rows only by the numeric `conversation_id`, and a store whose `conversation_id` column was renamed produces messages that belong to no thread at all with only the schema-support record naming `conversation` as unresolved. It cannot tell you a message was received: a NULL or absent direction column leaves the record with no direction, and `send_type`/`type` values other than 1 — including a value from a schema this parser was never validated against — read as received. It has never been validated against a real Viber store: no `viber_messages` or `viber_data` exists in `test_data/`, `reference/plaso/test_data`, `~/forensic_corpora` or `~/ctf-evidence` , so `SCHEMA_SUPPORT` is `Unranged`, every store's schema-support record reads `SchemaNotRanged`, and the column candidate lists are the parser's own reading of the documented schema, not something a device confirmed — the `PRAGMA user_version` a real store carries is recorded on that record and compared to nothing. It reads the `date` column as milliseconds unconditionally, so a store that held seconds would place every message in January 1970 and one that held microseconds in the far future, with nothing on the record to say so. It has no row cap and no `CapCounter`, so a store of ten million rows is walked whole and held in memory as artifacts. It cannot recover attachments, media, deleted rows, or the WAL's uncheckpointed frames when the source cannot open a sibling — a WAL-mode database whose source cannot enumerate neighbours carries `wal_incomplete_reason: wal_not_reachable` on every record. Where `conn.prepare` or `query_map` fails on a store whose table and columns were already established — a collation the store declares and stock SQLite lacks (Android's `LOCALIZED`), a view that will not compile — it yields one `ViberIncomplete` record with `status: DatabaseUnreadable`, `source_table: "messages"`, SQLite's own message as `sqlite_error` and both incompleteness pairs (reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`) beside the schema-support record, never an empty list (pinned by `a_messages_table_whose_query_will_not_run_is_reported_unreadable_not_empty`); it cannot say what the rows it did not read held.

**Refuses.** It refuses to read a store with neither a text column nor a time column: when both `text` and `sent_at` are unresolved it emits the schema-support record with `status: SchemaFieldsUnresolved`, `records_recovered: 0` and the incompleteness pair, and walks no rows, because a row with neither a body nor a time carries nothing evidentiary and inventing one would be a message the device never held. It refuses to let a renamed column read as an empty device : a store whose `body` or `date` column no longer resolves is still walked for what does resolve, and the record names the logical field rather than returning nothing. It refuses to answer "no messages" from a read error: a catalogue that will not answer, a `messages` lookup that will not run and a column list that will not read each produce a `StoreUnreadable` marker rather than the silence a clean, empty store would produce — only a catalogue that answered and held no `messages` table is treated as "not a Viber message schema" and yields nothing. It refuses to compare a version to a range nobody read out of a real file, and refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as version 0. It refuses to claim `content_incomplete` for a schema version merely outside a validated range — there is none — reserving that flag for an unresolved required field. And it refuses to assert direction where the store did not record it, leaving `is_from_me` and `direction` absent rather than writing `false`.

### `plugin.messaging.wechat`

**Reads.** WeChat for Android's `EnMicroMsg.db`, selected by file name and by nothing else: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the artifact's `name`, takes the part after the last `/` and acts only on exactly `enmicromsg.db`. The shared gate `stage_sqlite_db` skips a directory entry or an artifact with no data source, reads the first 16 bytes with a looping `read_full`, and where they are `SQLite format 3\0` — the examiner has already removed the SQLCipher layer — spills the file to a temporary copy under the shared 512 MiB `MAX_DB_BYTES` cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one. A full 16-byte header that is not SQLite's is taken as the still-encrypted SQLCipher store: the ciphertext is then read by this module itself under the same 512 MiB cap, and if the artifact's metadata carries a non-empty `sqlcipher_key` (used as the passphrase bytes) or both `wechat_imei` and `wechat_uin` (the passphrase is the first seven hex characters of MD5(IMEI ‖ uin)), `seance_sqlcipher::decrypt_with_provenance` is asked to decrypt it under the WeChat profile — 1,024-byte pages, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 with 4,000 iterations over the file's first 16 bytes as salt, AES-256-CBC per page with the IV in the page's reserve, and a per-page HMAC-SHA1 checked before decryption — which succeeds only when the ciphertext is a whole number of pages and the decrypted first page's page-size field matches. The plaintext is written to a temporary file and parsed exactly as a decrypted store would be. Fewer than 16 header bytes delivered yields nothing. The copy is opened read-only; `probe_catalogue` must answer; `probe_table` asks for `message`; `probe_columns` reads its column list. Four logical fields are resolved by `FieldMap::resolve`, each from one candidate — `peer` from `talker`, `text` from `content`, `sent_at` from `createTime`, `is_sent` from `isSend` — from the documented schema, confirmed by no real store; `msgId` is used when present, else `rowid`. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the open connection, 0 meaning "not recorded". The walk is one statement, `SELECT <id>, <peer>, <text>, <sent_at>, <is_sent> FROM message ORDER BY <sent_at>`, every unresolved field the literal `NULL`, with no row limit. The declared bound `wechat-android` is `Unranged`: no real WeChat database is held by this project (the gated test `decrypts_real_fixture_when_present` looks for `test_data/EnMicroMsg_encrypted.db` plus `SEANCE_WECHAT_IMEI`/`SEANCE_WECHAT_UIN` and has nothing to run against).

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per `message` row through the shared `ChatMessage` shell: `type: "WeChat"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `service: "WeChat"`, `platform: "Android"`, `text` (omitted when empty), `date` in whole Unix seconds from `createTime` read as milliseconds by `div_euclid(1000)` (omitted when 0 or negative), `is_from_me` and its derived `direction` only when `isSend` held a value — 1 is `sent`, any other integer `received`, NULL or no column leaves both off — `chat_identifier` and `contact` both set to `talker` (WeChat's peer or chatroom id is the only identity the table carries, so it serves as both; omitted when empty), `rowid`, and a `name` of `<direction or "message">: <talker> — <first 80 characters or "(no text)">`. Every record recovered through decryption additionally carries `decryption: "SQLCipher"`, `decrypted_pages`, `integrity_verified` (true only when every page's HMAC verified), `integrity_statement` in words either way, and `integrity_failed_pages` listing the 1-based page numbers that failed when any did — the rows on those pages still parse and are named, not dropped. After the rows, in this order: a `WeChatIncomplete` `RowsUndecodable` marker (`subtype: parse_incomplete`, `source_table: "message"`, `rows_dropped`, `records_recovered`, `first_error`, both incompleteness pairs with reason `unresolved_structure`) when any fetched row would not decode; then the schema notes `assess` entitles the parse to, each of `type: "WeChatIncomplete"` with `warning_class: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `app: "wechat-android"`, `store: "EnMicroMsg.db"`, `table: "message"`, `schema_version_locator: "PRAGMA user_version"`, the version as `schema_version_seen` / `schema_version_not_recorded: true` / `schema_version_undetermined`, `schema_unranged_reason`, `records_recovered`, `detail` and `name`, and never `schema_version_supported`. Every readable store carries one disclosure note (`subtype: "parser_stale"`, no incompleteness pair): `SchemaNotRanged` with the version seen "compared against nothing", or `SchemaVersionUndetermined` when the pragma would not read. Incompleteness is claimed (`subtype: "parser_stale"`, both pairs, reason `unvalidated`) by `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` when `text` or `sent_at` has no column (neither: the note alone, no rows) and by `SchemaTableAbsent` when the catalogue read and `message` was not in it; `SchemaOptionalFieldsUnresolved` (disclosure) names `peer` or `is_sent` when only those failed. A still-encrypted store with no key, a wrong key, or ciphertext that is not a whole number of 1,024-byte pages yields one `EncryptedMessengerDatabase` record (`subtype: "encrypted_database"`, `app: "WeChat"`, `encryption: "SQLCipher"`, `status: "Encrypted"`, a `note` naming the device-key derivation, `name: "WeChat database (encrypted)"`); a key that decrypted to a valid header is never reported that way, even when the parse then produced nothing. A store that would not open, whose catalogue would not read, whose `message` table could not be looked for, whose column list would not read, whose query would not prepare or whose walk would not run yields one `WeChatIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` marker (both pairs, reason `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`); a store carrying the SQLite header that could not be staged yields the same marker naming the I/O error. Every record from a short-staged, WAL-refused, or short-read ciphertext is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event, contact, chatroom or media record is produced.

**Cannot.** It has never read a real WeChat database: none is held, so the four column names are the parser's own reading of the documented schema, `PRAGMA user_version` is recorded and compared to nothing, and every readable store carries a `SchemaNotRanged` note; the SQLCipher 3 framing is validated in `seance_sqlcipher` against a database written by SQLCipher 4.6.1 built from upstream with SQLCipher-3 parameters (`tests/interop_test.rs`), and the end-to-end decryption of a real `EnMicroMsg.db` under the MD5(IMEI+uin) key has never been confirmed on this tree. It cannot obtain a key: the IMEI and uin, or a raw passphrase, must arrive in the artifact's metadata, and no path in the product derives them from the device. It cannot decrypt a WeChat store written under a SQLCipher profile other than the one hard-coded here — a different page size, KDF iteration count or HMAC setting fails the header check and is reported as encrypted with the right key, indistinguishable from a wrong one. It cannot decrypt a truncated ciphertext at all, failing closed rather than opening a database missing its last page; and a ciphertext cut short by the 512 MiB cap or a short read is a whole number of pages only by chance. It cannot name the other party beyond `talker`: `rcontact`, `chatroom` and `userinfo` are never opened, so no display name, no chatroom membership and no owner identity comes from this module, and a group message's individual sender — which WeChat keeps as a prefix inside `content` — is not separated from the body. It reads `createTime` as milliseconds unconditionally. It does not read `type`, so images, voice, video, calls and system notices are indistinguishable from text rows with an XML or empty body. It has no row cap and no `CapCounter`. It recovers no deleted rows, no attachments, no `-journal` sibling, and does not read `MicroMsg.db`, `SnsMicroMsg.db` or the iOS `MM.sqlite` store.

**Refuses.** It refuses to spend a short read as an encryption finding: only a full 16-byte non-SQLite header reaches the SQLCipher path, and a source that delivered fewer bytes yields nothing. It refuses to report a store it did decrypt as one it could not — a key that produced a valid SQLite header returns the parse even when empty, never the `Encrypted` record — and refuses to yield wrong rows from a wrong key, because a wrong key fails the page-size check and produces no database. It refuses to hand over decrypted messages without their provenance: every record says `SQLCipher`, whether the pages authenticated, and which pages did not, so a tampered page's rows are named rather than blended into sound ones. It refuses to answer "no messages" from a read error: a store that will not open, a catalogue that will not answer, a table that cannot be looked for, a column list, a query or a walk that fails each produce `StoreUnreadable`, and an absent `message` table in a catalogue that read produces `SchemaTableAbsent`, never silence. It refuses to let a renamed `talker` or `isSend` fail the whole store — they were once hard-coded into the SELECT, and a rename returned an empty list — and refuses to let a renamed `content` or `createTime` read as an empty device: the note names the logical field with both incompleteness pairs and the rows are still read for what resolves. It refuses to declare a schema range it did not read from a real file, and refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as version 0 or an unreadable pragma as in range. It refuses to assert direction where `isSend` was NULL or absent, and refuses to place an unset `createTime` at the epoch.

### `plugin.messaging.whatsapp`

**Reads.** WhatsApp's message stores, selected first by name and then by schema. The artifact's `name`, lower-cased, ending in `chatstorage.sqlite` names the iOS store, ending in `msgstore.db` names the Android store, and any other name merely *containing* `whatsapp` is treated as a candidate iOS store; it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `SystemArtifact` with `InputCapability::Stream`. A directory entry yields nothing. An artifact with no data source whose name ends in one of the two exact suffixes yields a bare `WhatsApp` record with `status: Identified` and nothing else; a `whatsapp`-substring name with no data yields nothing. Otherwise the shared gate `stage_named_store` reads the first 16 bytes; fewer than 16 delivered is a short read of this tool's, never a finding about the file, and yields only the stager's `SqliteSpillIncomplete` record (`content_incomplete_reason: short_read`) where the source declared more than arrived (ROADMAP §5.11). Otherwise the whole source is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 2 GiB cap (`MAX_DB_BYTES`, four times the shared default) with its `-wal` sibling, the copy opened read-only, and `probe_catalogue` asked to answer; where it will not, the staged file's own first 16 bytes decide whether this was a database at all. The variant is then re-established from the schema, the name-guess discarded: `ZWAMESSAGE` present means iOS; else `message` present, or `messages` present, means Android — each through the three-valued `probe_table`, so a lookup that could not be answered is not read as absence. On iOS it reads `ZWAMESSAGE` through a `FieldMap` of nine logical fields (`pk`/`Z_PK`, `text`/`ZTEXT`, `sent_at`/`ZMESSAGEDATE`, `from_me`/`ZISFROMME`, `message_type`/`ZMESSAGETYPE`, `starred`/`ZSTARRED`, `from_jid`/`ZFROMJID`, `to_jid`/`ZTOJID`, `chat_session`/`ZCHATSESSION`), left-joins `ZWACHATSESSION` on `ZCHATSESSION = Z_PK` for `ZCONTACTJID`, `ZPARTNERNAME` and `ZSESSIONTYPE` where that table and the `chat_session` field exist, and `ZWAPROFILEPUSHNAME` on `ZFROMJID = ZJID` for `ZPUSHNAME`, ordering by the resolved date column descending under a bound `LIMIT` of 500,001 rows; media come from `ZWAMEDIAITEM` (`ZMESSAGE`, `ZMEDIALOCALPATH`, `ZFILESIZE`) under the same cap. On Android with a `message` table it reads `key_id`, `text` (`text_data` then `data`), `sent_at` (`timestamp`), `from_me` (`from_me` then `key_from_me`), `status`, `media_type` (`media_wa_type` then `message_type`), `media_size` and `starred`, and chooses among four join shapes by probing columns: `message.chat_row_id` → `chat._id` → `jid._id`; an INTEGER `key_remote_jid` (declared type containing `INT`, or `typeof()` of a sample row when the declaration is empty) → `jid._id`; a TEXT `key_remote_jid` → `jid.raw_string` and `chat.jid`; or the bare `key_remote_jid`; a `sender_jid_row_id` → `jid` join names a group sender where those columns exist. A legacy `messages` table is read through `_id`, `key_remote_jid`, `key_from_me`, `data`, `timestamp`, `media_wa_type`, `media_size`. Android media come from `message_media` (`message_row_id`, `file_path`, `file_size`) or, failing that table, from `message.media_name`/`media_size`. `PRAGMA user_version` is read on Android with 0 as "not recorded"; on iOS the version is deliberately **not read** — the store is Core Data and its model version lives in `Z_METADATA.Z_PLIST`, which this build does not decode.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per message, `type: "WhatsApp"`, `subtype: "chat_message"`, `platform` `"iOS"` or `"Android"`. It does **not** use the shared `ChatMessage` shell: the record is a `json!` literal, so an unknown value is written as JSON `null` rather than omitted — `is_from_me: null` and `direction: null` where `ZISFROMME`/`key_from_me` was NULL or its column unresolved, `text: null` for a media message, `date: null` where no timestamp decoded, `contact_name: null` where no partner name or push name was found — and `contact` falls back to the literal string `"Unknown"`, `starred` to `false` when NULL, `is_group` to `false` when no JID was read. iOS records carry `pk`, `source_table: "ZWAMESSAGE"`, `date` as whole Unix seconds converted from Cocoa seconds and `date_ns` where the REAL column held a fraction, `message_type`, `from_jid`, `to_jid`, `contact_jid`, `remote_jid` (the counterparty chosen by direction: `to_jid` for sent, `from_jid` for received, `contact_jid` when direction is unknown), `contact` (partner name, then the push name of the sender when the sender is the counterparty, then the JID), `phone_number` (the part of the JID before `@`), `is_group` (`ZSESSIONTYPE` 2 or a JID containing `@g.us`) and `session_type`. Android records carry `id`, `key_id`, `date` from `timestamp` milliseconds by integer division with 0 omitted-as-null, `timestamp_ms` raw, `status`, `media_type`, `media_size`, `remote_jid`, `chat_subject`, `phone_number`, `sender_jid`, `sender_phone` and `is_group`. Media rows become `WhatsAppAttachment` records (`subtype: "chat_attachment"`, `source_table`, `message_rowid`, `filename`, `transfer_name`, a `mime_type` guessed from the extension over a fixed list of fourteen, `total_bytes`). Around them: a `WhatsAppIncomplete` `CapReached` marker naming the table when 500,000 messages were read and a 500,001st was present, a `RowsUndecodable` marker when a fetched row would not decode, a `SchemaUndetermined` marker when any table or column probe would not answer, and the same three shapes under `WhatsAppMediaIncomplete` for the media walks (a `ZWAMEDIAITEM` that is absent or will not query yields a `SchemaUndetermined` marker with `records_recovered: 0`). Then exactly one schema-support record per message table walked: `type: "WhatsAppIncomplete"`, `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `warning_class: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `app` `whatsapp-android` or `whatsapp-ios`, `source_table`, `status: SchemaNotRanged` on every readable store — both declarations are `SchemaBound::Unranged` with the reason "no reference database of this app is held by this project" and neither record carries `schema_version_supported` — with `schema_version_locator: "user_version"` and the version seen or not recorded on Android, and `schema_version_locator: "coredata_model"` with `schema_version_detail` saying the model version lives in `Z_METADATA` and was not read on iOS; `status: SchemaFieldsUnresolved` with both incompleteness pairs (reason `unvalidated`) when `text`, `sent_at` or `from_me` did not resolve — a renamed `from_me` that once made every message direction-unknown in silence is now named. A store whose catalogue would not read, or whose message tables could not be looked for, yields one `StoreUnreadable` marker; a parse that fails after that — a query that will not prepare, a bind error — yields one `WhatsAppIncomplete` record with `status: ParseFailed`, the error, both incompleteness pairs and a sentence that the absence of messages here is not evidence of their absence from the device. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused store is stamped by `TempDb::stamp_incompleteness`.

**Cannot.** It has never been validated against a real WhatsApp store of either platform: `test_real_whatsapp_db` has skipped for want of `test_data/whatsapp_chat.db` since it was written. A real Android store is now held — the Pixel 7a `msgstore.db` (230 messages) and its `-wal`, from Josh Hickman's Android 14 image into `test_data/whatsapp_android14/` — and `the_real_android14_msgstore_resolves_every_field` reads it to 230 messages with no field unresolved, but its `PRAGMA user_version` is a constant 1 so it cannot range the schema (`props.msgtore_db_schema_version` is not read), and no iOS `ChatStorage.sqlite` is held — so both schema declarations are `Unranged`, every store reads `SchemaNotRanged`, and the join-shape probing is the parser's reading of the schema generations, not a device's confirmation. It cannot read the iOS store's schema version at all, and says so on the record rather than reporting `PRAGMA user_version` (0 on every Core Data store) as a version. It cannot write an unknown as an absence: because the record is built as a `json!` literal rather than through `ChatMessage`, an unrecorded direction reaches the case as `is_from_me: null` / `direction: null`, an unnamed counterparty as the string `"Unknown"`, and consumers that test `is_from_me == false` or key on `contact` cannot tell those from findings — this is the drift `seance_sqlite_util::chat` was written to end and this parser has not adopted it. It decrypts a `crypt14` backup only when the phone's key file (`/data/data/com.whatsapp/files/key`) is read in the same case during the same run, paired in either order and only where the key's server salt is the backup's, or when the key is supplied for that one backup as the `whatsapp_key` credential (the key file as hex, or the bare 32-byte key as 64 hex digits; salt, then GCM tag, decide; a key that does not open it is rejected and nothing is filed; the record names `key_source: credential` and the SHA-256 of what was supplied, never the key); the decrypted store is parsed as a store and every record is stamped `provenance: decrypted_backup` with the backup's and key's paths and SHA-256 (graded on the real Pixel 7a backups, `VALIDATION.md` `WHATSAPP-CRYPT14-1`: 197 of 197 backup messages filed, each a row of the live store). A `crypt15` (end-to-end encrypted) backup is decrypted the same way with its 32-byte root key — `files/encrypted_backup.key` read in the same case, or the 64 hex digits the phone showed supplied as `whatsapp_key` — the AES key being HKDF-SHA256 of the root and the GCM tag deciding; a crypt14 key is never tried on a crypt15 backup nor the reverse (graded on the published backups of `VALIDATION.md` `WHATSAPP-CRYPT15-1`: `msgstore.db.crypt15` inflates to the published `msgstore.db` and `stickers.backup.crypt15` decrypts to the published `test9.zip`, SHA-256 for SHA-256; the only crypt15 message store held has one sentinel row and the others are sanitised, so no crypt15 message content has been graded). A crypt15 that holds a ZIP archive (a multi-file or incremental backup) has the archive filed beneath it as a file for the archive expander, held in memory only: it and its entries cannot be read after the run. It cannot derive a crypt15 root from a backup password (that needs WhatsApp's server-side HSM). A key read from the evidence is held in process memory for its case for the unlock lifetime (8 hours, `SEANCE_UNLOCK_TTL_SECS`), zeroed when dropped, and never written; it cannot pair a backup with a key read in another case, after a restart or that lifetime, or past 64 held backups or 16 held keys per case — the backup stays `AwaitingKey`, content incomplete, until a key is supplied for it; it does not read a backup over 1 GiB; and a backup's messages repeat those of the live store they were copied from, so the two are not merged. `crypt12` and older are refused by name, each with a `NotDecrypted` record, as is a crypt14 or crypt15 whose header will not read or whose supplied key does not open it. It cannot read reactions, edits, revoked messages, calls, statuses, group participants, quoted messages or `message_quoted`; a group message's sender is named only where `sender_jid_row_id` exists. It cannot recover a deleted row or read journal pre-images. It reads Android `timestamp` as milliseconds without a magnitude check. It cannot say which 500,000 messages it kept when the cap fires — the query is newest-first, so the oldest are lost, and the marker says so — and it holds up to 2 GiB of database and 500,000 message artifacts in memory. Its attachment `mime_type` is an extension guess over fourteen extensions and is written as `null` for any other. And a name that merely contains `whatsapp` — a log, a backup manifest, a thumbnail directory — is spilled up to 2 GiB before the header check rejects it.

**Refuses.** It refuses to decide the platform from the file name: the name's guess is overwritten by which message table the schema actually holds, so a `ChatStorage.sqlite` that is really an Android export is read as Android. It refuses to read a `messages` lookup that could not be answered as "no WhatsApp schema": only `probe_table` answering `Absent` for both `ZWAMESSAGE` and `message`/`messages` yields the silence reserved for a database that is not WhatsApp's; an undetermined lookup is a `StoreUnreadable` marker. It refuses to return nothing for a store it named and could not parse — every failure after staging is a `ParseFailed` or `StoreUnreadable` record carrying both incompleteness pairs. It refuses to let a read error substitute NULL for a message's text or direction and present the parse as complete: every column is bound through the `FieldMap`, every `NULL` substitution is a recorded unresolved field, a table or column probe that failed is a `SchemaUndetermined` marker, and a renamed required column is `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` with the incompleteness pair. It refuses to compare a version to a range nobody read out of a real file, refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as version 0 on Android, and refuses to report any version at all for the iOS Core Data store. It refuses to count a message it did not see: `records_recovered` on every marker is the count of `chat_message` records taken before the marker joins the list. And it refuses to walk past 500,000 rows of any table without saying so on a `CapReached` marker that names the table and the cap.

### `plugin.mobile.android_accounts`

**Reads.** Android's AccountManager stores, selected by exact file name: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the artifact's `name` and acts only on `accounts_de.db` (device-encrypted) or `accounts_ce.db` (credential-encrypted); an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The first 16 bytes are read with a looped read (`read_full`, re-asking a source that answers short) and must be `SQLite format 3\0`. The file is then spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 64 MiB cap (`MAX_DB_BYTES`) with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one, and the copy opened read-only. The `accounts` table's columns are read through `PRAGMA table_info` before any query is written, and the two required fields `name` and `type` are resolved from single candidates of the same names. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the connection, 0 meaning "not recorded", and compared with a single-point range read from one real device — the android2022 (Pixel, Android 12) full-file-system tar: `accounts_de.db` `3..=3` from `data/system_de/0/accounts_de.db` and `accounts_ce.db` `10..=10` from `data/system_ce/0/accounts_ce.db`, the two stores being versioned independently by the framework's `AccountsDb`. The walk is `SELECT <name>, <type> FROM accounts ORDER BY _id LIMIT 501`, an unresolved field the literal `NULL`, one row past the 500-account cap (`MAX_ACCOUNTS`) so the cap can be told from an exact fit. Nothing else in the store — `authtokens`, `extras`, `grants`, `shared_accounts`, `visibility` — is read.

**Produces.** Exactly one `MobileDeviceInfo` record per store read (`platform: "android"`, `source_kind: "android_accounts"`, `source_file`, `name: "Android accounts from <file>"`), preceded by any schema findings. Its `facts` object carries `google_account` — the list of `name` values whose `type` is `com.google`, case-insensitively — and `account`, every row as `<name> (<type>)`, with `fact_sources` naming `accounts.name` and `accounts.name + accounts.type`; several accounts are several readings of a multi-valued fact, which the device-facts compiler knows not to report as sources disagreeing. It also carries `accounts_read`, `rows_undecodable` (rows the store would not yield or that carried a NULL or empty `name` with both columns resolved) and `rows_field_unresolved` (rows read intact from a table whose `name` or `type` column did not resolve).
