One incompleteness is stamped, the most specific first: `content_incomplete: true` with reason `cap_reached` when more than 500 accounts were present, `unvalidated` when rows were read but a required column did not resolve, `unresolved_structure` when rows would not decode, or the spill's own reason when the database was not staged in full (`cap_reached` over the 64 MiB staging ceiling, `short_read` for a source that stopped early) — each with a `content_incomplete_detail` sentence; a write-ahead log that was refused or could not be looked for adds `content_incomplete: true` and `wal_incomplete_reason` beside whichever reason stands. Before that record: a `ParserStaleWarning` with `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `status: "SchemaFieldsUnresolved"`, `app: "android-accounts"`, `store`, `source_table: "accounts"`, `unresolved_fields`, `present_columns`, `supported_range`, `validated_against`, `records_recovered: 0`, both incompleteness pairs under reason `unvalidated`, and a `message` when `name` or `type` had no column; and one of `status: "SchemaOutsideValidated"` (the shared `StaleWarning` marker — `seen_schema_version`, `supported_range`, `message`; a disclosure with no incompleteness claim — when the version is outside the point), `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` (no incompleteness claim: `PRAGMA user_version` is 0 and nothing was compared), or `SchemaVersionUndetermined` (`content_incomplete: true`, reason `unresolved_structure`: the pragma would not read), each carrying `store`, `parser_record_type: "MobileDeviceInfo"`, `validated_against` naming the android2022 file, `content_incomplete_detail` and a `name`. A file named as an accounts store whose header probe came back short of 16 bytes yields one `accounts_unreadable` record with reason `short_read` and a sentence saying only that many bytes could be read — a short read is not evidence about the header. One whose first 16 bytes are not the SQLite header, or that could not be staged, opened, whose column list would not read, or whose query would not prepare or run, yields one `MobileDeviceInfo` record with `subtype: "accounts_unreadable"`, empty `facts`, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` and a sentence saying the accounts signed in to this device could not be read — because "nobody was signed in" and "we could not read who was" are different answers. A SQLite file with no `accounts` table at all yields nothing. No timeline event.

**Cannot.** It cannot see past the five-hundredth account, and says so. It cannot say which account is the device owner: the Google accounts are lifted out as `google_account` because they are the owner in all but name, but nothing here ranks them, and an app account can be the identity a case turns on. It cannot read a token, password, or the `extras` that hold a Google account's `gaia` id, nor the `previous_name`, `last_password_entry_time_millis_epoch` or any column beyond `name` and `type`, so when the account was added, whether it was removed, and what it was authorised for are not on the record. Its schema knowledge is one point wide per store (3 and 10, from one Pixel), so a real store on any other version is disclosed as outside the validated range and parsed on the assumption `name` and `type` mean the same; each field has exactly one candidate name, so any rename is an unresolved field. It reads a credential-encrypted `accounts_ce.db` only as the plaintext SQLite an examiner has already unlocked; the file as it sits in FBE storage is not decrypted here. A row whose `name` is empty is counted as undecodable, not as an account. It recovers no deleted rows.

**Refuses.** It refuses to render an unreadable account list as a phone with no accounts: a non-SQLite header, a header probe that came back short (stated as `short_read`, never as "not SQLite"), a store that will not stage or open, a column list that will not read, and a query that will not prepare or run each yield `accounts_unreadable` with the incompleteness pair, never an empty result; only a SQLite file with no `accounts` table at all is left unclaimed. It refuses to let a renamed column fail the whole store: the column set is read before the query is written, so a rename yields the `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` finding and the rows are still walked for what resolves, and rows read intact from such a table are counted under `rows_field_unresolved`, apart from damage, so the record does not send an examiner looking for corruption in a table whose schema simply moved. It refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as "older than 3" — it is stated as not recorded, with no incompleteness claim — and refuses to spend a pragma that would not read as in range, stating that as an incompleteness. It refuses to widen a single-point range downward. It refuses to report the cap as an exact fit, fetching one row past it. And it refuses to merge several accounts into one fact, listing every one so a second Google account or an app account is not averaged away.

### `plugin.mobile.android_bluetooth`

**Reads.** The Android Bluetooth stack's own record of remembered devices, `/data/misc/bluedroid/bt_config.conf`, and its `bt_config.bak`, selected by exact file name (case-insensitively) and corroborated by shape: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, and an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The file is read from offset 0 with a looped read (`read_capped`, re-asking a source that answers short) of at most 4 MiB (`MAX_BYTES`), decoded as lossy UTF-8, and parsed as INI text: blank lines and `#` comments are skipped, `[section]` lines open a section, and `key=value` lines (both sides trimmed) are kept in file order under the current section — a value line before any section is dropped. The file is claimed only when some section is named `Adapter` (case-insensitively) or is a Bluetooth address of the form `XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX` in hex. Within an address section it reads, case-insensitively by key and ignoring empty values: `Name`, `Timestamp` (parsed as Unix seconds), `DevClass`, `DevType`, `Manufacturer`, `AddrType`, `LinkKeyType` (each parsed as an integer), the presence of `LinkKey`, and `Service` split on whitespace. From `Adapter` it reads `Address`.

**Produces.** One `BluetoothPairing` record per address-shaped section, in file order: `platform: "android"`, `address` (the section name), `source_file`, `order` (the section's position among the address sections, from 0 — Android appends a device when it is first remembered, so the first section is the earliest pairing, the only thing that answers "which device was connected first" for an entry with no timestamp), `device_name` when the stack recorded a name, `name` as `<device name> (<address>)` or the address alone, `last_seen_recorded` as a genuine `true`/`false`, `last_seen` as an RFC 3339 string only when `Timestamp` was present and parsed, `device_class`, `device_type`, `manufacturer_id`, `address_type` and `link_key_type` as integers when present, `link_key_present` as `true`/`false`, and `services` as the list of UUIDs when present. One `MobileDeviceInfo` (`platform: "android"`, `source_kind: "android_bluetooth"`, `source_file`, `facts: {bluetooth_address}`, `fact_sources: {bluetooth_address: "Adapter.Address"}`) when the `Adapter` section carries an `Address` — the phone's own radio, which corroborates the address in `settings_secure.xml`. When fewer bytes were read than the file holds, every record carries `content_incomplete: true` with reason `short_read` (the source delivered less than it declared) or `cap_reached` (the file is over 4 MiB) and a `content_incomplete_detail` giving the byte counts, so a pairing list cut short cannot read as the whole list. A file whose name matches, was read in full and holds neither an `Adapter` nor an address section yields nothing; one read short whose bytes hold neither yields one `MobileDeviceInfo` with `subtype: "bluetooth_config_unidentified"`, empty `facts` and the incompleteness pair. No timeline event of its own.

**Cannot.** It cannot say a device was ever connected, only that the stack remembered it: a section is written on pairing or on a bond attempt, and nothing here distinguishes a completed bond from a failed one beyond `link_key_present`. It cannot date a pairing that carries no `Timestamp` — the stack began keeping them only in later releases — and it says so with `last_seen_recorded: false` rather than a date; where a timestamp exists it is when the device was last seen, not when it was first paired. It reads only the first 4 MiB, and the pairings past that point are not listed (the records say so). It does not decode `device_class` into a category, `manufacturer_id` into a company name, or a service UUID into a profile — they are passed through as integers and strings. It does not read the adapter's own `Name`, `ScanMode` or `DiscoveryTimeout`, nor the `Metrics` section, nor `bt_config.conf.encrypted-checksum`. It does not read the LE-specific keys (`LE_KEY_PENC`, `LE_KEY_PID`, `LE_KEY_LID`) beyond ignoring them, so an LE bond's identity-resolving key and its resolvable-address behaviour are not on the record. It does not read the AOSP `bt_config.xml` of older releases or a Samsung-modified layout.

**Refuses.** It refuses to copy the link key: it secures the bond and decrypts that device's traffic, its presence and type are findings and its value is a secret, and writing it into artifact metadata would put it in the search index and every export drawn from the case — the record names the file so an examiner who needs the key knows where to get it. It refuses to invent a date for a device the stack never timestamped, leaving `last_seen` off and `last_seen_recorded: false` on, because a date invented here would put a pairing on the timeline the phone never recorded. It refuses to claim a file on its name alone, requiring an `Adapter` or an address-shaped section. It refuses to present a short or capped read as the whole pairing list, stamping the reason on every record. And it refuses to renumber the sections: `order` is the file's own order, because that order is evidence in its own right.

### `plugin.mobile.android_calendar`

**Reads.** The Android calendar provider's store, selected by name or path: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess` and acts on a file named `calendar.db` (case-insensitively) or whose path contains `com.android.providers.calendar`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 64 MiB cap (`MAX_CONTENT_BYTES`) with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one, and the copy opened read-only; a copy that will not open is reported when it carries the SQLite header and passed over in silence as not a database when it does not. `probe_table` must list `Events`: absent in a readable catalogue means not the calendar store, and a catalogue that will not answer is reported, not spent as absence. The `Events` columns are read through `PRAGMA table_info` before any query is written and nine fields resolved from single candidates — `title`, `description`, `eventLocation`, `dtstart`, `dtend`, `allDay`, `calendar_id`, `organizer`, `rrule` — with the event's identity read as SQLite's `rowid` (which a declared `_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` aliases), so a table without an `_id` column still reads; `Calendars` is looked for through a `SchemaProbe` and, when present, its `_id` and `calendar_displayName` resolved and read into a name map. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the connection, 0 meaning "not recorded", and compared with the single-point range `600..=600`, read from the one real `calendar.db` this project holds — android2022 (Pixel, Android 12) `data/data/com.android.providers.calendar/databases/calendar.db`. The walk is `SELECT rowid, … FROM Events ORDER BY <dtstart>` with every unresolved field the literal `NULL`, stopping at 100,000 events (`MAX_EVENT_ENTRIES`); `dtstart`/`dtend` are read as Unix milliseconds.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per `Events` row in the iCalendar plugin's `CalendarEvent` shape so both share the calendar viewer: `type: "CalendarEvent"`, `source: "android_calendar"`, `rowid`, `summary` (the title), `description`, `location`, `dtstart` and `dtend` as RFC 3339 UTC strings to the second (a stored 0, the provider's unset value, is omitted, never written as 1970), `all_day` as a boolean (`false` when `allDay` is NULL), `recurrence` (the `rrule`), `organizer`, `calendar` (the joined display name, when the calendar id resolved to one), and a `name` of the title or `(no title)`; absent fields are omitted, never null, and no `subtype` is written on an event. Then one `AndroidCalendarSummary` (`subtype: "android_calendar_summary"`, `event_count` as extracted, `source`, `event_rows_dropped`, `calendar_names_dropped`; at the cap `truncated: true`, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `cap_reached`, `max_entries: 100000` and a message; where any `Events` row or `Calendars` row would not decode, `content_incomplete: true` (reason `cap_reached` if also capped, else `unresolved_structure`) and `inventory_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` — a dropped calendar name re-attributes every event on that calendar to no calendar, which is a change to what the record says). Then an `AndroidCalendarIncomplete` `SchemaUndetermined` marker (both pairs, `schema_probe_failed`, `schema_probe_detail`, `records_recovered`) when the `Calendars` probe, query or walk could not be answered; then `ParserStaleWarning` findings with `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `app: "android-calendar"`, `store: "calendar.db"`, `parser_record_type: "CalendarEvent"`, `validated_against`, `content_incomplete_detail` and `name`: `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` per table (`source_table`, `unresolved_fields`, `present_columns`, `records_recovered`, both pairs under `unvalidated`) when an `Events` field or a `Calendars` field did not resolve — a moved `Events` column is read as NULL and the events still listed, a moved `Calendars` column skips the join — and one of `SchemaOutsideValidated` (the shared marker; a disclosure with no incompleteness claim), `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` (no incompleteness claim) or `SchemaVersionUndetermined` (`content_incomplete: true`, reason `unresolved_structure`). A `calendar.db` that could not be staged yields one `AndroidCalendarEvent` `StoreUnreadable` marker; one carrying the SQLite header that would not open, whose catalogue would not read, or whose `Events` column list, prepare or query failed yields one `AndroidCalendarIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` marker (both pairs under `unresolved_structure`, `records_recovered: 0`, a `detail` naming the table and SQLite's error) instead of a module error. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended, including on the otherwise-empty output for a short copy with no `Events` table. No timeline event of its own.

**Cannot.** It cannot see past the hundred-thousandth event, and says so. It cannot tell you an event was deleted, cancelled or declined: `deleted`, `eventStatus`, `selfAttendeeStatus`, `lastSynced` and `dirty` are not read, so a soft-deleted row is listed as a live appointment. It does not read `Attendees`, `Reminders`, `Instances`, `ExtendedProperties`, `eventTimezone`, `duration`, `rdate`, `exrule`, `exdate` or `original_id`, so an event's guests, its alarms, its time zone and a recurring event's exceptions are not on the record and a recurrence is only its raw `rrule` string; nor `Calendars.account_name`/`account_type`, so which account a calendar syncs from is not stated. A `Calendars` column list that will not read is reported as the whole store unread, not as events without calendar names. A negative `dtstart` is converted as a pre-1970 date, not judged. `Connection::open` is lazy, so the will-not-open branch is pinned by a test of its own body rather than by a fixture that reaches it. Its schema knowledge is one point wide (600 from one Pixel), so any other version is disclosed as outside the validated range and parsed on the assumption the columns mean the same; every field has exactly one candidate name. It recovers no deleted rows.

**Refuses.** It refuses to file a corrupt provider store as a device whose owner kept no appointments : a catalogue that answers `SQLITE_CORRUPT` yields `StoreUnreadable`, and a `Calendars` probe, query or walk that fails is declared as `SchemaUndetermined` rather than spent as "one unnamed calendar". It refuses to return nothing when the name already established the store and the spill failed for an environmental reason. It refuses to let a renamed column fail the whole calendar: the column set is read first, a moved `Events` column is read as NULL and declared by name, and a moved `Calendars` column skips the join and is declared. It refuses to present a capped or lossy walk as the whole calendar, and refuses to let a dropped `Calendars` row pass uncounted, because it changes what every event on that calendar says. It refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as "older than 600", refuses to spend a pragma that would not read as in range, and refuses to widen the single-point range past the one file read. It refuses to write the provider's unset 0 as a 1970 date, and refuses to turn an `Events` table it could not query into a module error with no artifact. It refuses to emit a null field. And it refuses to conclude "not the calendar store" from a copy staged short whose `Events` table may lie past the bytes held, stamping the incompleteness pair on that otherwise-empty result.

### `plugin.mobile.android_properties`

**Reads.** Android's property files — the `key=value` text the framework's property service reads `ro.*` values from — selected by exact file name and corroborated by content. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, lower-cases the artifact's `name` and acts only on `build.prop`, `default.prop`, `prop.default`, `vendor.prop` or `odm.prop`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The file is read from offset 0 with a looped read (`read_capped`, re-asking a source that answers short) of at most 1 MiB (`MAX_PROPERTY_BYTES`). The bytes are decoded as lossy UTF-8 and walked line by line: blank lines and `#` comments are skipped, a line with no `=` is counted as unparsed, and each `key=value` pair (both sides trimmed) is kept in key order up to 4,000 properties (`MAX_PROPERTIES`), after which the collection stops and is marked capped. The file is claimed as Android's only when at least one key begins `ro.`. Twenty-two facts are then read, each from a candidate list most authoritative first, the first non-empty value winning: `manufacturer` (`ro.product.manufacturer`, `ro.product.system.manufacturer`, `ro.product.vendor.manufacturer`), `model` (`ro.product.model`, `ro.product.system.model`, `ro.product.vendor.model`), `device`, `product_name`, `android_version` (`ro.build.version.release`, `ro.system.build.version.release`), `sdk_level`, `security_patch`, `build_id`, `build_fingerprint`, `build_display_id`, `build_date_utc`, `build_type`, `build_tags`, `serial_number` (`ro.serialno`, `ro.boot.serialno`), `hardware`, `bootloader`, `cpu_abi` (`ro.product.cpu.abi`, `ro.product.cpu.abilist`), `locale`, `timezone` (`persist.sys.timezone`), `encryption_state` (`ro.crypto.state`), `encryption_type`, `verified_boot_state` — the per-partition prefixes being where Android 10 moved `ro.product.*`. The artifact's `path` is taken for the record, falling back to its name.

**Produces.** Exactly one `ParsedRecord` per property file claimed: `type: "MobileDeviceInfo"`, `platform: "android"`, `source_kind: "android_properties"`, `source_file` (the path), `name: "Android device facts from <file>"`, `properties_read` (the count kept), `unparsed_lines`, a `facts` object holding whichever of the twenty-two facts were present, and a `fact_sources` object naming, for each fact, the exact property key it was read from — because an examiner asked to stand over "the model is Pixel 7a" needs the key as much as the value, and the keys moved between Android versions. Nothing is reconciled: a device has several property files (`/system/build.prop`, `/vendor/build.prop`, `/odm/etc/build.prop`, `default.prop`) and they can disagree, so each yields its own record and the disagreement survives. Where the source delivered fewer bytes than it declared, the record carries `content_incomplete: true`, `content_incomplete_reason: short_read` and a detail sentence giving the byte count read; where the file is larger than 1 MiB, reason `cap_reached` with the file size and the ceiling named; where the 4,000-property cap stopped the collection, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `cap_reached` and the cap named. A file whose name matches, that was cut short, and whose delivered bytes hold no `ro.` key yields one `MobileDeviceInfo` record with `subtype: "properties_unidentified"`, empty `facts`, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `short_read` (or `cap_reached` when the byte ceiling, not the source, stopped the read) and a sentence saying whether it holds this device's identity could not be established from what is here. A file whose name matches, was read whole, and holds no `ro.` key yields nothing — it is not claimed. A read error ends the read where it happened and is stated as a `short_read`. No timeline event.

**Cannot.** It cannot say which of several disagreeing property files is the device's truth — that is deliberately left to the reader — and it cannot read any property the framework composes at boot rather than stores: `ro.serialno` is often absent from the files and set from the bootloader, so a device summary with no serial here is not a device with no serial. It reads only the first 1 MiB, and says so. It reads only the five file names listed; `/system/etc/prop.default`, `/vendor/default.prop`, `/product/build.prop` and the `*.prop` overlays under `/vendor/odm/etc/` are picked up only when their basename is one of the five, and the system property store itself (`/dev/__properties__`, `persist.sys.*` values written at runtime) is not read, so a `persist.sys.timezone` seen here is the file's default, not necessarily the running value. It decodes the text as lossy UTF-8 with no record of replacement characters. It reads exactly the twenty-two facts and their listed keys — any other `ro.*` value is counted in `properties_read` and not carried, so the record is not a dump of the file. The corroboration is one `ro.` key, so an unrelated file named `build.prop` holding a single `ro.` line is claimed. It does not read `getprop` output, `default.prop` from a boot image, or an iOS device's equivalents.

**Refuses.** It refuses to claim a file on its name alone: without an `ro.` property, a `build.prop` that was read whole is not Android device facts and yields nothing, because a file of unrelated `key=value` text claimed as a device's identity would put invented facts on a device summary. It refuses to stay silent about one it could not read enough of, filing `properties_unidentified` with the byte count so the summary is not silent about the one file that would have filled it in. It refuses to reconcile or average disagreeing property files, emitting one record per file. It refuses to present a fact without its provenance — every fact carries the key it came from — and refuses an empty value as a fact, falling through to the next candidate. It refuses to drop an unparsed line silently, counting it on the record. And it refuses to present a truncated or capped read as the whole file, stamping the incompleteness pair with the number read or the cap that stopped it — and refuses to call the parser's own ceiling a short read.

### `plugin.mobile.android_settings`

**Reads.** The Android framework's settings files — `settings_global.xml`, `settings_secure.xml` and `settings_system.xml` under `/data/system/users/<id>/` — selected by exact file name (case-insensitively) and by nothing else: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, and an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The file is read with a single `read_at` from offset 0 of `min(size, 8 MiB)` bytes (`MAX_SETTINGS_BYTES`); a source that answers short is recorded as such, not re-asked. If the bytes begin `ABX\0` — Android 12 and later write these as Android Binary XML — they are decoded by `seance_xml_util::abx::decode` (bounded at 256 levels of depth, 65,535 interned strings and 256 MiB of decoded output) and rendered back to text XML; otherwise they are taken as lossy UTF-8 text. The text is walked event by event with `quick_xml` under an `XmlGuard` (256 attributes per element), and every `<setting>` element's `name` and `value` attributes are read. Eleven settings are carried, each to a named fact: `device_name`, `bluetooth_name`, `android_id`, `bluetooth_address`, `adb_enabled`, `development_settings_enabled` (as `developer_options_enabled`), `install_non_market_apps` (as `sideloading_allowed`), `auto_time` (as `clock_set_automatically`), `auto_time_zone` (as `time_zone_set_automatically`), `location_mode`, `user_setup_complete`; a setting with an empty value is skipped. Every other setting is counted and not carried.

**Produces.** Exactly one `MobileDeviceInfo` record per settings file that held at least one `<setting>` element, or that was cut short or would not parse: `platform: "android"`, `source_kind: "android_settings"`, `source_file` (the path, else the name), `name: "Android device facts from <file>"`, `encoding` (`abx` or `text`), `settings_read` (every `<setting>` element seen, carried or not), a `facts` object holding whichever of the eleven facts were present with the value exactly as the file stored it — `auto_time` as `"1"` or `"0"`, not a boolean — and `fact_sources` naming for each fact the setting key it came from. A device whose `clock_set_automatically` reads `0` is a device whose every timestamp is an assertion by whoever set the clock, which is why that fact belongs on the device summary. Where the file was larger than 8 MiB or the source delivered fewer bytes than asked, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `short_read` and the byte count; where the ABX decoder stopped before the end, reason `unresolved_structure` with its error; where the XML reader errored, reason `unresolved_structure` naming the setting count reached — each with a sentence saying a fact missing here may be one that was never reached. A file whose name matches, was read whole, parsed to its end and held no `<setting>` element yields nothing — it is not claimed. A read error is a `ParsingError` and no record. No timeline event.

**Cannot.** It cannot tell you what a setting the device never wrote would have defaulted to: an absent `adb_enabled` is an absent fact, not `0`, because a default invented here would be a statement about Android, not about this phone. It reads only the eleven settings listed; the hundreds of others — `screen_off_timeout`, `lock_screen_*`, `mock_location`, `wifi_*`, `airplane_mode_on`, the enabled accessibility and notification-listener services — are counted in `settings_read` and not carried. It reads only the first 8 MiB with one unlooped `read_at`, and does not distinguish a file over the cap from a source that answered short: both are `short_read`. It cannot say which user the file belonged to — the `/users/<id>/` segment is not parsed out of the path — so on a multi-user device two `settings_secure.xml` records carry no user id. It does not read the `package`, `id` or `defaultValue` attributes, so which app last wrote a setting and whether the value is the default are not on the record. It reads the value as the file stored it, so a `bluetooth_address` or `android_id` is passed through unvalidated. A text-XML file with a lossy UTF-8 decode is not marked. It does not read the older `settings.db` SQLite store that Android 4.x wrote, nor `locksettings.db`.

**Refuses.** It refuses to claim a file on its name alone: a `settings_*.xml` read whole with no `<setting>` element is not claimed, because an unrelated XML claimed as a device's settings would put invented facts on a device summary. It refuses to stay silent about one it could not read to the end: a short read, an ABX decode that stopped, or an XML error each yield the record with the incompleteness pair and the point reached, so a missing fact reads as possibly unreached rather than absent. It refuses to invent a default for a setting the device did not write, and refuses to carry an empty value as a fact. It refuses to coerce a value — `"1"` stays `"1"` — so the record shows what the framework stored. And it refuses to present a fact without the setting key it came from.

### `plugin.mobile.android_telephony_device`

**Reads.** The Android telephony provider's `telephony.db`, selected by exact file name (compared case-insensitively) and by nothing else: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess`, and an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 128 MiB cap with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one, and the copy opened read-only; no header probe precedes the spill, so a file of that name that is not SQLite reaches the column list and is reported there. The `siminfo` table's columns are read through `PRAGMA table_info` before any query is written, and only those that exist are selected: the required `number` and `icc_id`, and the optional `carrier_name`, `display_name` and `imsi` — `imsi` being absent from the real validated store, so its absence is not drift. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the connection, 0 meaning "not recorded", and compared with the single-point range `1703944..=1703944`, read from the one real `telephony.db` this project holds — the android2022 (Pixel, Android 12) full-file-system tar's `data/user_de/0/com.android.providers.telephony/databases/telephony.db`. The walk is `SELECT <present columns> FROM siminfo LIMIT 51`, one row past the 50-SIM cap (`MAX_SIMS`); each value is read as whatever SQLite type it holds — text as text, an INTEGER or REAL in its decimal form — and a blank one is treated as absent; a row the engine will not step is counted, and rusqlite ends the walk there. No other table — `carriers`, `sms`, `mms`, `threads` — is read here; the SMS/MMS tables are the Android SMS module's.

**Produces.** One `MobileDeviceInfo` record per store (`platform: "android"`, `source_kind: "android_telephony"`, `source_file`, `name: "Android telephony facts from telephony.db"`, `sims_read`, `rows_undecodable`), preceded by any schema findings. Its `facts` object carries, each as a list with one entry per SIM row that held a value: `phone_number` from `number`, `iccid` from `icc_id`, `carrier` from `carrier_name`, `sim_name` from `display_name`, `imsi` from `imsi`; `fact_sources` names `siminfo.<column>` for each. A dual-SIM phone yields two of each, emitted as several readings of a multi-valued fact rather than as sources disagreeing. Where a row would not decode, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` and a sentence saying the SIM records after it are not listed; where more than 50 rows were present, reason `cap_reached` and the cap named; where a value was held as a BLOB or as text that is not UTF-8, `values_not_rendered` counting them by `siminfo.<column>` and, when no other shortfall applies, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` and a sentence saying those facts are missing though the device recorded them; where the database was not staged in full, `content_incomplete: true` with the spill's own reason (`cap_reached` over the 128 MiB staging ceiling, `short_read` for a source that stopped early) and `staging_incomplete_reason`; where the write-ahead log was refused or could not be looked for, `content_incomplete: true` and `wal_incomplete_reason`. A `siminfo` table that is present and empty yields one `MobileDeviceInfo` with `subtype: "no_sim_recorded"`, `sims_read: 0`, empty `facts` and a `message` saying this device has no record of a SIM having been inserted — said rather than nothing, which reads as "not examined" — qualified by the same staging and WAL stamps. A `telephony.db` that would not stage or open, whose `siminfo` column list would not read, whose query would not prepare or run, or whose walk stopped on an undecodable row before any SIM was read yields one `MobileDeviceInfo` with `subtype: "telephony_unreadable"`, empty `facts`, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure`, a `content_incomplete_detail` carrying SQLite's error, and any `staging_incomplete_reason` / `wal_incomplete_reason`. A readable catalogue with no `siminfo` table yields nothing. Before the record: a `ParserStaleWarning` with `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `status: "SchemaFieldsUnresolved"`, `app: "android-telephony"`, `store: "telephony.db"`, `source_table: "siminfo"`, `unresolved_fields`, `present_columns`, `supported_range`, `validated_against`, `records_recovered: 0`, both incompleteness pairs under reason `unvalidated` and a `message`, when `number` or `icc_id` had no column (the remaining columns are still read); and one of `status: "SchemaOutsideValidated"` (the shared marker with `seen_schema_version`, `supported_range`, `message`; a disclosure with no incompleteness claim), `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` (no incompleteness claim), or `SchemaVersionUndetermined` (`content_incomplete: true`, reason `unresolved_structure`), each carrying `store`, `parser_record_type`, `validated_against`, `content_incomplete_detail` and `name`. No timeline event.

**Cannot.** It cannot read past a row the engine refuses to step: rusqlite ends the walk at the first such error, so the SIM rows after it are unread — counted as a shortfall, not recovered. A value held as a BLOB, or as text that is not UTF-8, is counted and not rendered: no encoding is guessed for it. An INTEGER `number` loses any leading `+` or zero the device never stored. It cannot report a phone number the carrier never provisioned onto the SIM: `number` is what the card carries, empty on many cards, and an empty value simply leaves `phone_number` off the facts with nothing to say a SIM row existed without one. It cannot pair a number with its ICCID: the facts are per-column lists, so on a dual-SIM device the first `phone_number` and the first `iccid` are not stated to belong to the same card. Its schema knowledge is one point wide (1703944 from one Pixel), so any other version is disclosed as outside the validated range and parsed on the assumption the columns mean the same; each field has exactly one candidate name. It does not read `carrier_id`, `mcc`/`mnc`, `sim_slot_index`, `is_embedded` (eSIM), subscription state or the `carriers` APN table, so which slot a SIM sat in and whether it was an eSIM profile are not on the record. It recovers no deleted rows.

**Refuses.** It refuses to render an unreadable `telephony.db` as a device with no telephony store: every failure after the name match is the `telephony_unreadable` record, never silence, and a row that would not decode is counted, never flattened away. It refuses to fail the whole store over one renamed column: the table's columns are read first and only those present are selected, so a phone's number is not reported absent because an unrelated column moved, and a missing `number` or `icc_id` is declared on the `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` finding while the rest is still read. It refuses to render an empty `siminfo` as silence, filing `no_sim_recorded` so "never had a SIM" and "not examined" read differently. It refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as "older than the validated version", refuses to spend a pragma that would not read as in range, and refuses to widen the single-point range past the one file read. It refuses to treat a blank value as a fact, and refuses to reconcile two SIMs into one number. And it refuses to report the cap as an exact fit, fetching one row past it.

### `plugin.mobile.call_history`

**Reads.** Mobile call logs from two platforms, selected loosely by name and strictly by schema. It subscribes to `FileEntry` with `InputCapability::Stream`, lower-cases the artifact's `name` and opens any file whose name ends `callhistory.storedata`, `contacts2.db` or `calllog.db`, or contains `callhistory` or `calllog` — `contacts2.db` is shared with the contacts parser, and the schema decides. An artifact with no data source is not opened and leaves an identification record. Otherwise the whole file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 2 GiB cap (`MAX_DB_BYTES`) with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one; the staged copy's first 16 bytes must be `SQLite format 3\0` or the file is passed over in silence. The copy is opened read-only and dispatched on the catalogue: a table or view named `ZCALLRECORD` is the iOS `CallHistory.storedata` Core Data store; failing that, `calls` is an Android log, classified as `contacts2.db` (the ContactsProvider's pre-4.2 home, app `android-contacts2-calls`) when the name ends so and `calllog.db` (`android-calllog`) otherwise; a catalogue that will not answer is an error, not an absence. For the Android stores `PRAGMA user_version` is read and compared with a window read from one real file each: `calllog.db` `5..=5` (Magnet 2022 CTF Pixel 3) and `contacts2.db` `1..=1` (Magnet 2019 Android CTF, the acquisition agent's store; plaso's `test_data/contacts2.db` reads 0, which is the absence of a version, not an endpoint). No window is declared for the iOS store, whose `PRAGMA user_version` was 0 on the one real file observed (Magnet 2022 CTF iPhone 8) and whose model version lives as hashes in `Z_METADATA.Z_PLIST`, not as a number. Both walks resolve their columns through a `FieldMap` against `PRAGMA table_info` — Android `calls`: `id` from `_id` or `id` (the Magnet 2019 agent store keys the table that way), `number`, `date`, `duration`, `type`; iOS `ZCALLRECORD`: `Z_PK`, `ZADDRESS`, `ZDATE`, `ZDURATION`, `ZORIGINATED`, `ZANSWERED`, `ZCALLTYPE` — and a column list that will not read is an error for the parse. Each walk is one statement `ORDER BY <date> DESC` with every unresolved field the literal `NULL`, stopping at 200,000 records (`MAX_CALL_ENTRIES`). `number`/`ZADDRESS` is read whether stored as TEXT, BLOB (trimmed of NULs), integer or real. Android `date` is placed by magnitude through the shared band table (microseconds ≥ 10^15, milliseconds ≥ 10^12, else seconds) keeping the sub-second part; iOS `ZDATE` is a REAL of seconds since 2001-01-01 converted with its fraction, a non-finite, zero, negative or overflowing value being "unset".

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per call, `type: "CallLog"`, `subtype: "call"`, `platform: "iOS"` or `"Android"`, `rowid`, `number` (null when absent) and `contact` (the number, else the literal `Unknown`), `direction`, `duration_seconds` (null when the column was NULL — never 0), `timestamp` in whole Unix seconds with `timestamp_rfc3339` rendered to the nanosecond and `timestamp_ns` when the fraction is non-zero, or, where the column held a value no reading of which is an instant, `timestamp_unusable: true` with `timestamp_raw` as stored (Cocoa seconds on iOS) and no timestamp keys at all — a NULL column writes none of these — and a `name` of `<direction> call: <contact> (<n>s or "duration unknown")`. Android direction is `incoming`/`outgoing`/`missed`/`voicemail`/`rejected`/`blocked` for `type` 1–6 and the literal `unknown` for NULL or any other code, with `call_type` written as stored, null included. iOS direction is `outgoing` when `ZORIGINATED` is 1, `missed` when it is 0 and `ZANSWERED` is 0, `incoming` when it is 0 and `ZANSWERED` is non-zero or NULL, and `unknown` when `ZORIGINATED` is NULL or another value; `answered` and `originated` are written as booleans only when recorded, `call_type` as stored. Between the records and the summary sit the schema findings, all `type: "ParserStaleWarning"`, `subtype: "parser_stale"`, under the store's `app`: for an Android store `SchemaOutsideValidated` (the shared marker with `seen_schema_version`, `supported_range`, `message`, detail and name post-stamped; a disclosure with no incompleteness claim) when the version is outside its window and the rows still parse; `SchemaVersionUndetermined` with `content_incomplete: true`, reason `unresolved_structure`, when the pragma would not read; `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` with no incompleteness pair when it is 0 — each of the three carrying `validated_against` naming the real store the window was read from (Magnet 2022 Pixel 3 `calllog.db`, Magnet 2019 `contacts2.db`); and for either platform one `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` (`source_table`, `unresolved_fields`, `records_recovered`, the `content_incomplete` pair) when any field had no column. Then one `CallLog` summary (`subtype: "summary"`) with `platform`, `call_count` (what this tool extracted), `incoming_count`, `outgoing_count`, `missed_count`, `unknown_direction_count`, `other_direction_count` (voicemail/rejected/blocked), `file_name`, and at the cap `truncated: true`, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `cap_reached`, `max_entries: 200000` and a sentence that the oldest calls were not extracted; where any row would not decode, `rows_dropped`, `inventory_incomplete: true` and `content_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` (a cap's reason is not overwritten). An artifact with no data source yields one `CallLog` record with `status: "Identified"`; a file carrying the SQLite header that would not open, whose catalogue or column list would not read, or whose query would not prepare or run yields one `CallLog` record with `status: "ParseFailed"`, the error, and both incompleteness pairs under `unresolved_structure`. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended.

**Cannot.** It cannot see past the two-hundred-thousandth call: both walks are newest-first, so the cap drops the oldest, and the summary says so with the pair. It cannot name a caller: the Android `name` (cached contact name) column is deliberately not selected because not every validated store carried it, `contacts2.db`'s address book is not joined even when the calls live in the same file, and the iOS `ZCALLRECORD` `ZNAME` is not read — `contact` is the number or the literal `Unknown`. It cannot tell which SIM, which account, or whether a call was FaceTime, cellular or a third-party VoIP service: `ZCALLTYPE` and `call_type` are passed through as integers with no decoding, and `ZSERVICE_PROVIDER`, `phone_account_id`, `subscription_id`, `countryiso`, `geocoded_location` and `features` are not read. Its Android schema knowledge is one point wide per store (5 and 1), so a real log on any other version is parsed on the assumption its columns mean the same thing with the `SchemaOutsideValidated` finding beside the rows; the iOS store has no numeric version and drift there is caught only by the column map. Every field has exactly one physical name (two for the Android id), so any rename is an unresolved field. It cannot tell a missed call from an unanswered one it does not know about: an iOS row with `ZORIGINATED` 0 and `ZANSWERED` NULL is `incoming`, not `missed`; an Android `type` outside 1–6 is `unknown`. A truncated `ZDURATION` real loses its fraction. It does not read `-journal` siblings and recovers no deleted rows; a `contacts2.db` with both a `calls` table and an address book is read here for calls only.

**Refuses.** It refuses to file a corrupt call log as a device that placed no calls: a catalogue that will not answer, a column list that will not read, and a query that will not prepare or run all reach the `ParseFailed` record carrying both incompleteness pairs, and only a file with no SQLite header, or a readable catalogue with neither `ZCALLRECORD` nor `calls`, is passed over in silence. It refuses to invent a direction: a NULL or unrecognised `type`/`ZORIGINATED` is written as the literal `unknown` and tallied in `unknown_direction_count`, never as `missed` or `incoming`, because direction is the evidentiary content of a call record. It refuses to write `answered: false` or `duration_seconds: 0` for a column that was NULL. It refuses to place an unset or negative date at the 1970 or 2001 epoch, keeping the raw value under `timestamp_unusable`/`timestamp_raw` where no consumer can read it as a time, and refuses to read a 16-digit microsecond value as milliseconds. It refuses to drop the fraction: two calls inside one second are ordered only by it, so `timestamp_ns` and the RFC 3339 string carry it. It refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as "older than the window", refuses to spend a pragma that would not read as in range, and refuses to declare a window for the Core Data store whose version is not a number. It refuses to substitute a guess for an unresolved column, naming it instead with the count of records that lack it. It refuses to let a dropped row vanish — every undecodable row is counted into `rows_dropped` with the `inventory_incomplete` pair — and refuses to count a schema finding as a call: the direction tally is taken over the call records before the findings join the list.

### `plugin.mobile.contacts`

**Reads.** Mobile address books from two platforms, selected loosely by name and strictly by schema. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `SystemArtifact` with `InputCapability::Stream`, lower-cases the artifact's `name` and opens any file whose name ends `addressbook.sqlitedb` or `contacts2.db`, or contains `addressbook`; `contacts2.db` is shared with the call-history parser and the schema decides what each reads. An artifact with no data source is not opened and leaves an identification record. Otherwise the whole file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 2 GiB cap (`MAX_DB_BYTES`) with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one; the staged copy's first 16 bytes must be `SQLite format 3\0` or the file is passed over in silence. The copy is opened read-only and dispatched on the catalogue — a table or view named `ABPerson` is iOS, failing that `raw_contacts` is Android, and a catalogue that will not answer is an error, not an absence. The schema version is read per platform: iOS from `_SqliteDatabaseProperties` where `key = '_ClientVersion'` (an integer or a numeric string is the version; an absent table or row is "not recorded"; a catalogue that will not answer, a non-numeric value or a query error is "undetermined"), compared with the single-point range `83..=83` read from the one real `AddressBook.sqlitedb` this project holds — ios2022ffs (iPhone 8, iOS 15) `/private/var/mobile/Library/AddressBook/AddressBook.sqlitedb`, whose `PRAGMA user_version` is 0 and is not consulted; Android from `PRAGMA user_version` (0 meaning "not recorded"), compared with `1300..=1300` from the one real `contacts2.db` with a contacts schema — android2022 (Pixel, Android 12) `data/data/com.android.providers.contacts/databases/contacts2.db`. Every column is resolved through a `FieldMap` against `PRAGMA table_info` before a query is written, each from one candidate name: iOS `ABPerson` (`First`, `Last`, `Organization`; `ROWID` is SQLite's own) and `ABMultiValue` (`record_id`, `property`, `value`); Android `raw_contacts` (`_id`, `display_name`), `data` (`raw_contact_id`, `mimetype_id`, `data1`) and `mimetypes` (`_id`, `mimetype`); a column list that will not read is an error for the parse. On iOS every `ABPerson` row is read, then every `ABMultiValue` row when that table exists and its three columns resolved: a value containing `@` or of property 4 is an e-mail, property 3 a phone, anything else counted as unmapped. On Android every `raw_contacts` row is read when `_id` resolved, then `data JOIN mimetypes` when both tables exist and their columns resolved: a mimetype ending `/phone_v2` or `/phone` is a phone, `/email_v2` or `/email` an e-mail, `/organization` the organisation (first wins), `/name` a display name where `raw_contacts` had none, anything else counted as unmapped. People are capped at 200,000 (`MAX_CONTACT_ENTRIES`); the multi-value tables are not capped.

**Produces.** One `ParsedRecord` per person, `type: "Contact"`, `subtype: "contact"`, `platform: "iOS"` or `"Android"`, `rowid`, `display_name` (iOS `First` and `Last` joined by a space, Android `display_name`; else the organisation; else the literal `Unknown`), `phone_numbers` and `emails` as de-duplicated lists in store order, `organization` (null when none), and — only where the store held more about this person than the record shows — `unmapped_value_count` and `unmapped_value_kinds` (up to 32 distinct iOS `property <n>` codes or Android mimetype strings), stated as counts and deliberately not as the incompleteness pair, because on a Google-synced Android device nearly every contact carries a `group_membership` or `identity` row and a banner on every contact is a banner nobody reads; `name` is `Contact: <display_name>`. After the people, in this order: one `ParserStaleWarning` (`subtype: "parser_stale"`, `status: "SchemaFieldsUnresolved"`, `app: "ios-addressbook"` or `"android-contacts"`, `store`, `source_table`, `unresolved_fields`, `present_columns`, `supported_range`, `validated_against`, `records_recovered`, both incompleteness pairs under reason `unvalidated`, `message`) per table whose required field did not resolve — a moved `First`/`Last`/`display_name` is read as NULL and the people are still listed; a moved `ABMultiValue` or `data`/`mimetypes` column skips that join entirely and is declared; then one of `status: "SchemaOutsideValidated"` (the shared `StaleWarning` marker with `seen_schema_version`, `supported_range`, `message`; a disclosure with no incompleteness claim), `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` (no incompleteness claim), or `SchemaVersionUndetermined` (`content_incomplete: true`, reason `unresolved_structure`), each with `store`, `parser_record_type: "Contact"`, `validated_against`, `content_incomplete_detail` and `name`, and none when the version is inside the point. Then one `Contact` summary (`subtype: "summary"`) with `platform`, `contact_count` (what this tool extracted), `with_phone_count`, `with_email_count`, `file_name`; at the cap `truncated: true`, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `cap_reached`, `max_entries: 200000` and a sentence; where any row would not decode, `rows_dropped`, `inventory_incomplete: true` and `content_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` (a cap's reason is not overwritten); and where any value was unmapped, the total `unmapped_value_count`, up to 64 `unmapped_value_kinds`, `inventory_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure`, and an `unmapped_value_message` saying this parser decodes names, numbers, e-mails and organisations and the counted values were stored and not decoded — raised once here as a scope statement rather than on every record. An artifact with no data source yields one `Contact` record with `status: "Identified"`; a file carrying the SQLite header that would not open, whose catalogue or column list would not read, or whose query would not prepare or run yields one `Contact` record with `status: "ParseFailed"`, the error, and both incompleteness pairs under `unresolved_structure`. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended.

**Cannot.** It cannot see past the two-hundred-thousandth person, and says so. It decodes four things about a person — name, phone numbers, e-mail addresses, organisation — and nothing else: postal addresses (iOS property 5), URLs (22), birthdays (23), IM handles (46), notes, nicknames, photos, group memberships, linked-contact and account provenance are counted as unmapped and not carried, so their absence from a record is not evidence of absence from the device, as the summary says. It cannot say which account a contact was synced from (`raw_contacts.account_name`/`account_type`), whether it was deleted (`raw_contacts.deleted`), or when it was created or last modified (`ABPerson.CreationDate`/`ModificationDate`, `contact_last_updated_timestamp`); a soft-deleted Android contact is listed as if live. It cannot merge Android raw contacts into aggregate contacts: it lists `raw_contacts` rows, so a person synced from two accounts appears twice. Its iOS e-mail test is `value.contains('@')` before the property code, so a phone-typed value containing `@` is filed as an e-mail. Its schema knowledge is one point wide per platform (83 and 1300, from one device each), so any other version is disclosed as outside the validated range and parsed on the assumption the columns mean the same; every field has exactly one candidate name. An `ABMultiValue` or `data` row whose person is not among those read — including everyone past the cap — is silently skipped, uncounted. It reads only `AddressBook.sqlitedb`, not `AddressBookImages.sqlitedb`, and only `contacts2.db`, not `profile.db` or a third-party contacts app's store. It recovers no deleted rows.

**Refuses.** It refuses to file a corrupt address book as a device with no contacts: a catalogue that will not answer, a column list that will not read, and a query that will not prepare or run all reach the `ParseFailed` record carrying both incompleteness pairs; only a file with no SQLite header, or a readable catalogue with neither `ABPerson` nor `raw_contacts`, is passed over in silence. It refuses to let a renamed name column fail the store: the column set is read first, a moved `First`, `Last`, `Organization` or `display_name` is read as NULL and declared, and the people are still listed; a moved join column skips the join and is declared rather than hanging nothing off nobody. It refuses to present phone-and-email-only as everything the device stored, counting every unmapped value per person and stating the scope once on the summary. It refuses to raise the incompleteness banner on every contact for that scope, because a banner seen everywhere is a banner not read and a real truncation then gets missed. It refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as "older than 1300" or an absent `_ClientVersion` as "older than 83", refuses to spend a version that would not read as in range, and refuses to widen either single-point range past the one file read. It refuses to let a dropped row vanish, counting every undecodable `ABPerson`, `ABMultiValue`, `raw_contacts` or `data` row into `rows_dropped` with the `inventory_incomplete` pair. And it refuses to invent a name: with no name and no organisation the record says `Unknown`.

### `plugin.mobile.google_keep`

**Reads.** Google Keep's Android store, selected by name or path: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess` and acts on a file named `keep.db` (case-insensitively) or whose path contains `com.google.android.keep`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The file is spilled by `TempDb::spill` under a 64 MiB cap (`MAX_CONTENT_BYTES`) with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one, and the copy opened read-only; a copy that will not open is reported when it carries the SQLite header and passed over in silence when it does not. `probe_table` must list `tree_entity`: absent in a readable catalogue means not the Keep store, and a catalogue that will not answer is reported. The `tree_entity` columns are read through `PRAGMA table_info` before any query is written and resolved from candidate lists — `_id`, `title`, `type`, `time_created` (from `time_created` or `timestamp`), `user_edited_timestamp` (from `user_edited_timestamp` or `time_last_updated`), `is_trashed`, `is_archived`, `color_name` as required, and `text` as optional, because the validated store keeps a note's body in `list_item`, not on the note. `list_item` is looked for through a `SchemaProbe` and, when present, its `text`, `list_parent_id` and `order_in_parent` resolved. `PRAGMA user_version` is read through the connection, 0 meaning "not recorded", and compared with the single-point range `95..=95`, read from the one real `keep.db` this project holds — android2022 `data/data/com.google.android.keep/databases/keep.db`. Notes are read by `SELECT * FROM tree_entity LIMIT 100001` (one past the 100,000 cap) with each field fetched by its resolved column name; for every note with an `_id`, its checklist lines are read by `SELECT <text> FROM list_item WHERE <list_parent_id> = ?1 ORDER BY <order_in_parent>`. A Keep timestamp's unit is judged by magnitude — above 10^15 microseconds, above 10^12 milliseconds, else seconds — because it has differed across versions.

**Produces.** One `AndroidNote` (`subtype: "android_note"`, `source: "google_keep"`) per `tree_entity` row that has a title or a body: `title`, `text` (the note's own `text` column, if any, followed by its non-empty checklist lines joined with newlines), `note_type: "list"` when `type` is 1, `color`, `created` in whole Unix seconds with `created_rfc3339`, `edited_rfc3339`, `is_trashed` and `is_archived` as booleans when recorded, and a `name` of `Note: <first 60 characters of the title, else the first line of the text>`; a row with neither title nor text — a folder or label placeholder — yields nothing. A note some of whose `list_item` rows would not decode carries `list_items_dropped` and `content_incomplete: true` with reason `unresolved_structure` on the note itself, because it is that record an examiner reads. After the notes: one `AndroidNoteParseStatus` `RowsUndecodable` marker (`subtype: parse_incomplete`, both pairs under `unresolved_structure`, `rows_dropped` for `tree_entity`, `secondary_rows_dropped` for `list_item`, `extracted_count`) when any row would not decode; one `AndroidNoteParseStatus` cap marker (`subtype: "android_note_incomplete"`, `truncated: true`, `content_incomplete: true` with reason `cap_reached`, `max_entries: 100000`, `extracted_count`) when more than 100,000 notes were present; an `AndroidNoteIncomplete` `SchemaUndetermined` marker (both pairs, `schema_probe_failed`, `schema_probe_detail`, `records_recovered` counted over notes only) when the `list_item` probe, query or walk could not be answered; `ParserStaleWarning` findings with `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `app: "google-keep"`, `store: "keep.db"`, `parser_record_type: "AndroidNote"`, `validated_against`, `content_incomplete_detail` and `name` — `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` per table (`source_table`, `unresolved_fields`, `present_columns`, `records_recovered`, both pairs under `unvalidated`) when a required `tree_entity` or `list_item` field did not resolve (a moved `list_item` column skips every checklist), and one of `SchemaOutsideValidated` (the shared marker; a disclosure with no incompleteness claim), `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` (no incompleteness claim) or `SchemaVersionUndetermined` (`content_incomplete: true`, reason `unresolved_structure`). A `keep.db` that could not be staged yields one `GoogleKeepNote` `StoreUnreadable` marker; one carrying the SQLite header that would not open, whose catalogue would not read, or whose `tree_entity` or `list_item` column list or `tree_entity` query failed yields one `AndroidNoteIncomplete` `StoreUnreadable` marker naming the table and SQLite's error, instead of a module error. Every record from a short-staged or WAL-refused copy is stamped `content_incomplete: true` with its reason and one `SqliteSpillIncomplete` marker is appended. No timeline event of its own.

**Cannot.** It cannot see past the hundred-thousandth note, and says so. It does not read `is_deleted`, `is_pinned`, `server_id`, `account_id`, `parent_id`, `order_in_parent`, `time_last_updated` beyond its use as an edited time, nor `blob`, `blob_node`, `label`, `note_label`, `sharing`, `reminder` or `annotation`, so images, drawings, audio, labels, collaborators, reminders and links attached to a note are not on the record, a note is not attributed to an account, and a checklist line's own checked state (`is_checked`) is not read — a completed item and an open one read the same. It cannot tell which lines of the body came from the note and which from its checklist once joined. A `list_item` column list that will not read is reported as the whole store unread, not as notes without checklists. Its schema knowledge is one point wide (95 from one Pixel), so any other version is disclosed as outside the validated range and parsed on the assumption the columns mean the same; the time columns have two candidates each, every other field one. A NULL checklist line is treated as an empty line, not a loss. It recovers no deleted rows.

**Refuses.** It refuses to file a damaged notebook as one the custodian never wrote in: a catalogue that will not answer yields `StoreUnreadable`, and a `list_item` probe, query or walk that fails is declared as `SchemaUndetermined` rather than spent as "this note had no checklist". It refuses to return nothing when the spill failed for an environmental reason after the name established the store, and refuses to turn a `tree_entity` it could not query into a module error with no artifact. It refuses to let a renamed column read as a silent NULL: the column sets are read before the queries are written and a missing required field is declared by name. It refuses to drop a checklist line in silence — one dropped leaves a note body that reads as complete while missing a line the custodian wrote — so the count and the pair go on the note itself, and a note row that would not decode is counted so the listing does not read as exact. It refuses to present a capped walk as the whole notebook, fetching one row past the cap. It refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as "older than 95", refuses to spend a pragma that would not read as in range, and refuses to widen the point past the one file read. It refuses to place an unset (0 or negative) timestamp at the epoch, and refuses to emit a placeholder note with neither title nor body.

### `plugin.mobile.installed_apps`

**Reads.** Three installed-application inventories, selected by name or path: it subscribes to `FileEntry` and `FileContent` with `InputCapability::RandomAccess` and acts on a file named `packages.xml` (case-insensitively) or whose path ends `/system/packages.xml`, one named `packages.list` or whose path ends `/system/packages.list`, or one named `applicationState.db`; a directory entry or an artifact with no data source yields nothing. The file is read whole through `read_capped` under a 64 MiB cap (`MAX_CONTENT_BYTES`), and a shortfall against the declared size is recorded. `packages.xml` is Android's package-manager settings: if the bytes begin `ABX\0` — Android 12 and later — they are decoded by `seance_xml_util::abx::decode` (bounded at 256 levels, 65,535 interned strings and 256 MiB of output; a decode that stops before `END_DOCUMENT` still yields every event before the stop) and rendered to text; otherwise they are taken as lossy UTF-8. The text is walked with `quick_xml` under an `XmlGuard` (256 attributes per element, refused attributes counted) and every `<package>` element's `name`, `codePath`, `version`, `userId` (else `sharedUserId`), `ft`/`it`/`ut` (hex strings of Unix milliseconds, with or without `0x`), `installer`, and Android 14's `installInitiator`, `updateOwner` and `isOrphaned` are read; `<shared-user>`, `<permissions>`, `<keyset-settings>` and the rest are ignored. `packages.list` is one app per line, `packageName userId debugFlag dataPath seinfo gids…`. `applicationState.db` is FrontBoard's SQLite store: its first 16 bytes must be the SQLite header, it is staged by `TempDb::write_with_sidecars` with its `-wal` sibling where the source can open one (a live store keeps its newest rows there), opened read-only, its version read as the single row of `schema(version)` — `PRAGMA user_version` is 0 on every real store and is not consulted — and compared with the single-point range `1..=1`, read from both real stores this project holds: ios2022ffs `/private/var/mobile/Library/FrontBoard/applicationState.db` and macos2021 `Users/eliflatt/Library/FrontBoard/applicationState.db`; the `application_identifier` column of `application_identifier_tab` is resolved from its one candidate before the query `SELECT <column> … WHERE <column> IS NOT NULL AND <column> <> '' ORDER BY <column>` is written.

**Produces.** One `InstalledApp` record per application (`analysis_type: "installed_app"`, `subtype: "InstalledApp"`, `package`, `name` the same, `source` naming the file). From `packages.xml`: `code_path`, `version`, `user_id`, and for each of `ft`/`it`/`ut` that decodes to a positive millisecond value before 2100-01-01, `first_install`/`install_time`/`update_time` as integer milliseconds with `*_rfc3339` beside them; `code_partition` (`data`, `system` for `/system` or `/system_ext`, `product`, `vendor`, `apex`, else `other`) from the first path segment; `installer_package`, `install_initiator_package`, `update_owner_package` where recorded; `is_orphaned` as a boolean with an `is_orphaned_note` saying the flag is reported as written and that what it selects is not established (on the two graded images 40 of 62 and 59 of 123 Play-installed packages carry it while the Play Store is installed); the Android 14 pair is graded on a Pixel 7a, where 123 packages carry `installInitiator` and 56 `updateOwner`, matching an independent ABX count; and `install_source` as `installer_recorded`, `shipped_with_the_os` (no installer, code on a read-only partition, with a note that the absence is not a sideload signal), `no_installer_recorded` (no installer, code under `/data`, with a note that this is the signal a sideload leaves and a signal not a proof), or `not_recorded`. From `packages.list`: `user_id` and `data_path`. From `applicationState.db`: `platform: "iOS"` and the bundle id, one per non-empty row, sorted. Absent fields are omitted, never null. Then any schema findings for the iOS store — `ParserStaleWarning` with `subtype: "parser_stale"`, `app: "ios-applicationstate"`, `store`, `parser_record_type: "InstalledApp"`, `validated_against` naming both files, `detail` and `name`: `status: "SchemaOutsideValidated"` (the shared marker, `seen_schema_version`, `supported_range: "1..=1"`; a disclosure with no incompleteness claim), `SchemaVersionNotRecorded` (no `schema` table or no row; no incompleteness claim), `SchemaVersionUndetermined` (`content_incomplete: true`, reason `unresolved_structure`), or `SchemaFieldsUnresolved` (`source_table`, `unresolved_fields`, `present_columns`, `records_recovered: 0`, both pairs under `unvalidated`) when the identifier column did not resolve, in which case no row is read. Then exactly one `InstalledAppSummary` (`subtype: "installed_app_summary"`, `app_count` counted before the findings joined the list, `source`, `encoding: "abx"|"text"` for `packages.xml`, `abx_lossy_strings` with a detail sentence when any ABX string was not valid UTF-8 — an approximation, not an incompleteness). Where the file was not read whole or the walk did not reach its end, the summary carries `content_incomplete: true` and `inventory_incomplete: true` with one reason — `cap_reached` when the declared size exceeds 64 MiB, else `short_read` when fewer bytes arrived than declared, else the parser's own (`short_read` for an ABX document that simply ends, `cap_reached` for one whose decode exceeded 256 MiB, otherwise `unresolved_structure`) — plus `input_truncated`, `parse_stopped_early`, `parse_stopped_at_offset` where the ABX decoder can name one, `bytes_read`, `declared_size`, `max_content_bytes`, an `incomplete_detail` sentence (the ABX error; a text-XML parse error; the count of `<package>` elements whose attributes were refused; the count of attributes that would not decode; for iOS the non-SQLite header, the staging error, the query error, the unresolved column, or the number of rows that would not decode), and a `message` that the app list is a floor, not the installed set. No timeline event.

**Cannot.** It cannot say who installed an app when the package manager did not: `install_source: no_installer_recorded` is the signal a sideload leaves and is stated as a signal, not a proof, because the attribute is also absent when the record predates the Android version that writes it, when the app was restored from a backup, or when the installer has since been uninstalled — and a data-partition path is not a user install either, since on the graded image 62 of 63 packages there were Play Store updates of system apps. It cannot interpret `isOrphaned`. It reads only the `<package>` element's attributes: permissions granted, signing keys, enabled state, the `<disabled-components>`, split APKs, `<domain-verification>` and per-user install state under `<package><user…>` are not read, so an app disabled for a user is listed as installed. It does not read `packages-backup.xml`, `packages-stopped.xml`, `runtime-permissions.xml` or the ABX-era `packages.xml` of a device whose ABX uses a token type the decoder does not know beyond the point it stops. From `packages.list` it reads only the package, user id and data path. From `applicationState.db` it reads bundle ids and nothing else: no install date, no display name, no `kvs` blob, and a bundle whose id is empty or NULL is skipped uncounted — and the same store on macOS (where it lists app bundle ids under FrontBoard too) is read as `platform: "iOS"`. Its iOS schema knowledge is one point wide, from two files, and the one column has one candidate name. An install timestamp beyond 2100-01-01 or non-positive is dropped as garbage with nothing on the record to say a value was present. A `packages.list` cut short by the cap or a short read is reported on the summary but has no parse-level detail of its own. It recovers no deleted rows and does not read the `-journal` sibling.

**Refuses.** It refuses to report zero packages from a binary file it did not decode: ABX is detected by magic and decoded before the walk, and the summary says which encoding was read, because a text parser handed the ABX form reports zero packages and on every modern device that is where the install times are. It refuses to present a prefix as the installed set: a file over the cap, a short read, an ABX decode or XML walk that stopped, an element whose attributes were refused, an attribute that would not decode, a store that would not stage or query, an unresolved identifier column and an undecodable row each put `content_incomplete` and `inventory_incomplete` on the summary with the reason and the detail, and an ABX document that merely ends is called a short read rather than a broken structure so an examiner is not sent looking for the rest of a file that has no rest. It refuses to quote a replacement-charactered name as the device's, counting `abx_lossy_strings` and saying so. It refuses to read an absent installer as a sideload on a read-only partition, and refuses to read it as proof of one on the data partition. It refuses to interpret `isOrphaned`, reporting the flag as written with the note that the common reading does not hold on either graded device. It refuses to invent an install time from a non-hex, non-positive or absurd value, and refuses to emit a null field. It refuses to spend `PRAGMA user_version` 0 as the FrontBoard version, reading the `schema` table instead; refuses to spend a missing `schema` row as "older than 1" or an unreadable one as in range; and refuses to widen the point past the two files read. And it refuses to let a renamed `application_identifier` surface as a query error that reads like a broken file: it is declared by name as `SchemaFieldsUnresolved`, with the summary saying no application was inventoried.

### `plugin.mobile.ios_backup`

**Reads.** An iTunes or Finder backup folder on the examiner's own disk, by path. It subscribes to `FileEntry` and `RawEvidence` with `InputCapability::FilePath`, and needs the `path` metadata or returns `InvalidInputFormat`; a path that is not a directory yields nothing, and a directory is a backup only if `Manifest.plist` exists beside `Manifest.db` or `Manifest.mbdb`. Through the API a folder is ingested as a `RawEvidence` artifact with `is_directory: true` and its path, and the CLI's `scan` writes the same shape. `Manifest.plist` is read with `plist::from_file`: `IsEncrypted` as a boolean, or an integer other than 0, or — where absent or of another shape — inferred from the presence of `ManifestKey`; `Version`; `Date`; the device's `Display Name`, `Product Type`, `Product Version`, `Build Version`, `Serial Number` and `Unique Identifier` at the top level, else `DeviceName`, `ProductType`, `ProductVersion`, `BuildVersion`, `SerialNumber` and `UniqueDeviceID` inside `Lockdown`; `BackupKeyBag` and `ManifestKey` as data. The password is the credential an examiner supplied for this backup folder through `POST …/credential` with kind `ios_backup_password`, held zeroed for the one run and visible to this module only for that artifact, else the process-level `--ios-backup-password` / `SEANCE_IOS_BACKUP_PASSWORD`; a password in the artifact's metadata is not read. With a supplied credential the module reports it accepted once the RFC 3394 unwrap of at least one passcode-wrapped class key succeeds — a keybag with none (no `WRAP` bit 2) never tests the password and reports no verdict — and rejected, in its own words and never the password, when that integrity check fails, returning no records so the orchestrator keeps nothing and audits the refusal; the rejection says the password is wrong or the wrapped class key corrupt, because the integrity check cannot tell the two apart. A wrapped key that is not a valid RFC 3394 length is a malformed keybag and a module error, not a verdict on the password. For an unencrypted backup `Manifest.db` is opened with rusqlite and `SELECT fileID, domain, relativePath, flags, file FROM Files` is read; each `file` blob is a plist, either an `NSKeyedArchiver` archive whose root is `$top.root` (defaulting to object 1) or a plain dictionary, from which `Size`, `Mode`, `LastModified`, `Birth`, `InodeNumber`, `UserID`, `GroupID` and `ProtectionClass` are read, timestamps accepted as integers, reals or plist dates, and `EncryptionKey` followed to an `NSMutableData` whose `NS.data` is a 4-byte little-endian class prefix and an RFC 3394 wrapped key. A stored file is located as `<ab>/<fileID>` then `<fileID>`, only after the id is checked to be ASCII alphanumeric, and opened with `FileDataSource`. Where there is no `Manifest.db`, `Manifest.mbdb` is walked record by record (signature `mbdb`, domain, path, link target, data hash, key, mode, inode, uid, gid, mtime, size), with ids from `Manifest.mbdx` where present, else `SHA-1(domain-path)`. For an encrypted backup with a password: the keybag TLVs (`UUID`, `SALT`, `ITER`, `DPSL`, `DPIC`, `CLAS`, `WRAP`, `WPKY`, `KTYP`) are parsed; the passcode key is PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 over `DPSL`/`DPIC` then PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 over `SALT`/`ITER` where `DPSL` is present (iOS 10.2+), else a single SHA-1 round; every class key whose `WRAP` has bit 2 set is unwrapped with RFC 3394, but one whose `WRAP` also has bit 1 (`WRAP` = 3, device-bound) keeps nothing: its passcode layer is checked, which tests the password, and the value it yields — still wrapped under the device's hardware key — is zeroed and the class recorded `device_bound`, so no file or keychain item is ever decrypted with it; the `ios_backup_decrypted` record lists the keybag's classes by number as `usable`, `device_bound` and `not_unwrapped` (`keybag_classes`, no key bytes); `ManifestKey` (class prefix plus wrapped key) is unwrapped with its class key and `Manifest.db` decrypted with AES-256-CBC and a zero IV into a temporary file for rusqlite; and each file's key is unwrapped with the class from the metadata blob's `ProtectionClass`, else the key's own prefix, and its bytes decrypted in memory below `STREAMING_THRESHOLD` (10,485,760 bytes) or through `DecryptedFileDataSource` above it, which validates the PKCS#7 padding of the last block before stating a size. When the decrypted backup holds `KeychainDomain/keychain-backup.plist` — a binary plist of `genp`, `inet`, `cert` and `keys` arrays of `{v_Data, v_PersistentRef}` and a `keybag-uuid`, not a `keychain-2.db` — it is read whole (to 256 MiB) while the class keys are in scope: each `v_Data` is taken as version 3 (`<u32 version><u32 class><u32 length>` little-endian, an RFC 3394 wrapped item key, then AES-256-GCM ciphertext with an empty IV and a 16-byte tag), the item key is unwrapped with the backup's class key for that keychain class, the tag is verified before any byte is used, and the plaintext is read as a DER `SET` of `SEQUENCE { UTF8String, value }` attributes.

**Produces.** One artifact per manifest row and a handful of backup-level records, all parented to the directory artifact. On the unencrypted `Manifest.db` path each row is `type: IosBackupFile` with `name` (the basename of `relativePath`, so `sms.db` is findable by the parsers that key on that name), `file_id`, `domain`, `relative_path`, `flags`, `is_directory`, `size`, `mode`, `last_modified` and `birth` as RFC 3339, the same two again as `modified` and `created` for the file grid and the timeline, `inode`, `user_id`, `group_id`, `protection_class` and `backup_path`: a directory (flag 0x2) is a `ParsedRecord` with no data; a file is a `FileEntry` with a `FileDataSource` over its stored blob; a symlink (flag 0x4) with no blob is a `FileEntry` with `is_symlink: true` and `content_omitted: symlink_has_no_stored_content`; a row carrying a per-file `EncryptionKey` inside a backup that did not declare itself encrypted is a `FileEntry` with no data, `content_incomplete: true`, `content_incomplete_reason: encrypted`, `content_omitted: stored_blob_is_ciphertext` and a message; a row whose blob will not open is a `FileEntry` with no data, the pair with reason `unresolved_structure`, `content_omitted: backup_blob_unreadable` and `open_error`; and a row whose metadata blob would not decode carries `inventory_incomplete: true`, reason `unresolved_structure`, `metadata_parse_error` and a sentence that its size and times are unknown, not absent. On the `Manifest.mbdb` path the rows are `type: IosBackupFileLegacy` with `format: mbdb_legacy`, `link_target`, `has_encryption_key`, `has_data_hash` and `modified` from the 32-bit mtime, under the same three content rules. On the encrypted path each decrypted file is a `FileEntry` with `encrypted: true`, `decrypted: true`, `protection_class_used` and `protection_class_source` (`manifest_protection_class_field` or `encryption_key_class_prefix`), and each file that could not be produced is a `ParsedRecord` with `subtype: ios_backup_undecrypted`, `decrypted: false`, the incompleteness pair, a message, and a `status` of `InvalidFileId` (reason `unresolved_structure`), `NoFileKey`, `UnknownProtectionClass`, `NoClassKey`, `KeyUnwrapFailed` or `DecryptFailed` (reason `encrypted`), or `ReadFailed` (reason `short_read`).
